title: 日本語総まとめ N1 語彙

items.q: 私の夫はとても金づかいが（ ）。
items.qr: Watashi no otto wa totemo kanezukai ga (___).
items.en: My husband is a real spendthrift.
items.hi: मेरे पति बहुत फ़िज़ूलख़र्ची करते हैं।
items.gu: મારા પતિ ખૂબ ઉડાઉ છે.
items.why: 金遣いが荒い is a fixed idiom for being wasteful with money — 悪い simply doesn't collocate with 金遣い this way.

items.q: 彼はちょっと時間に（ ）ところがある。
items.qr: Kare wa chotto jikan ni (___) tokoro ga aru.
items.en: He's a bit sloppy/unpunctual about time.
items.hi: वह समय को लेकर थोड़ा ढीला-ढाला है।
items.gu: તે સમય બાબતે થોડો ઢીલો છે.
items.why: ルーズな時間 describes being unpunctual/sloppy about time; まめ describes diligence — the opposite trait.

items.q: 彼女は大スターなのに、とても（ ）人です。
items.qr: Kanojo wa daisutaa na noni, totemo (___) hito desu.
items.en: Even though she's a big star, she's a very approachable person.
items.hi: वह एक बड़ी स्टार होते हुए भी बहुत मिलनसार इंसान है।
items.gu: તે મોટી સ્ટાર હોવા છતાં ખૂબ મળતાવડી વ્યક્તિ છે.
items.why: なのに ("even though") signals a contrast with the stereotype that big stars are hard to approach — so the blank must be the opposite trait, 気さくな.

items.q: 豪華で（ ）輝きの宝石。
items.qr: Gouka de (___) kagayaki no houseki.
items.en: A gem shining with luxurious dignity.
items.hi: भव्य और गरिमामय चमक वाला रत्न।
items.gu: ભવ્ય અને ગૌરવપૂર્ણ ચમકવાળું રત્ન.
items.why: 気品 (dignity/elegance) naturally describes a jewel's refined brilliance; 色気 (sex appeal) is a trait of people, not gemstones.

items.q: あまりお金に（ ）人は嫌われます。
items.qr: Amari okane ni (___) hito wa kirawaremasu.
items.en: People who are too greedy about money are disliked.
items.hi: जो लोग पैसों को लेकर बहुत लालची होते हैं, उन्हें नापसंद किया जाता है।
items.gu: જે લોકો પૈસા બાબતે ખૂબ લોભી હોય છે, તેમને નાપસંદ કરવામાં આવે છે.
items.why: お金にいやしい is the natural collocation for someone stingy/greedy about money; でしゃばり is about butting into others' business, unrelated to money specifically.

items.q: あの店員はだれにでも（ ）。
items.qr: Ano ten'in wa dare ni demo (___).
items.en: That shop clerk is friendly to everyone.
items.hi: वह दुकान वाला हर किसी से खुशमिज़ाजी से पेश आता है।
items.gu: તે દુકાનદાર દરેક સાથે મળતાવડાપણે વર્તે છે.

opts.en: good taste (unrelated to だれにでも)

items.why: 愛想がいい describes a friendly manner toward others, fitting だれにでも ("to anyone"); センスがいい is about taste/judgment, unrelated to how one treats people.

items.q: 彼女は将来（ ）新人女優です。
items.qr: Kanojo wa shourai (___) shinjin joyuu desu.
items.en: She is a promising newcomer actress.
items.hi: वह भविष्य में होनहार नई अभिनेत्री है।
items.gu: તે ભવિષ્યમાં આશાસ્પદ નવી અભિનેત્રી છે.
items.why: 将来 ("future") specifically collocates with 有望な ("promising") — the other three describe personality/manner, not future potential.

items.q: 彼は（ ）肉体をしている。
items.qr: Kare wa (___) nikutai o shite iru.
items.en: He has a robust, muscular physique.
items.hi: उसका शरीर मज़बूत/हट्टा-कट्टा है।
items.gu: તેનું શરીર મજબૂત/કદાવર છે.
items.why: 肉体 ("physical body") pairs with たくましい (physically strong/robust); the other three describe demeanor or character, not physical build.

items.q: 電車に乗り遅れそうになり（ ）。
items.qr: Densha ni noriokuresou ni nari (___).
items.en: I panicked because I was about to miss the train.
items.hi: ट्रेन छूटने वाली थी, इसलिए मैं घबरा गया।
items.gu: ટ્રેન છૂટવાની હતી એટલે હું ગભરાઈ ગયો.
items.why: Almost missing a train causes panic/hurry (焦る), not offense — 気に障る is about being offended by someone's words/actions, unrelated here.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 2 · どんな気持ち？

items.q: 山田先生は、怒るととても（ ）よ。
items.qr: Yamada sensei wa, okoru to totemo (___) yo.
items.en: Mr./Ms. Yamada is really scary when angry.
items.hi: यामादा सेंसे गुस्सा होने पर बहुत डरावने लगते हैं।
items.gu: યામાડા સેન્સેઈ ગુસ્સે થાય ત્યારે ખૂબ ડરામણા લાગે છે.
items.why: The sentence describes how the teacher appears to others (frightening), not the speaker's own irritation — しゃくに障る describes one's own annoyance, not someone else's scariness.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 2 · どんな気持ち？

items.q: 旅行に行く日がとても（ ）。
items.qr: Ryokou ni iku hi ga totemo (___).
items.en: I can hardly wait for the day of the trip.
items.hi: यात्रा के दिन का बेसब्री से इंतज़ार है।
items.gu: પ્રવાસના દિવસની આતુરતાથી રાહ જોઉં છું.
items.why: 待ち遠しい specifically means "so anticipated that the wait feels long" — exactly the feeling before a trip; 快い describes pleasantness/willingness, not anticipation.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 2 · どんな気持ち？

items.q: 近所に（ ）楽器の練習ができない。
items.qr: Kinjo ni (___) gakki no renshuu ga dekinai.
items.en: I can't practice my instrument because I feel constrained by the neighbors.
items.hi: पड़ोसियों का ख्याल करके मैं वाद्ययंत्र का अभ्यास नहीं कर पाता।
items.gu: પડોશીઓની ચિંતાને કારણે હું વાદ્ય વગાડવાની પ્રેક્ટિસ કરી શકતો નથી.
items.why: Holding back from practicing out of consideration for neighbors is 気兼ねする (feeling hesitant about imposing), not むかつく (anger/nausea) — the wrong emotion entirely.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 2 · どんな気持ち？

items.q: 梅雨時は雨ばかりで（ ）。
items.qr: Tsuyudoki wa ame bakari de (___).
items.en: During the rainy season it's nothing but rain, which is gloomy.
items.hi: बरसात के मौसम में लगातार बारिश उदासी भर देती है।
items.gu: ચોમાસામાં સતત વરસાદ ઉદાસી લાવે છે.
items.why: うっとうしい天気 is the fixed collocation for gloomy/oppressive weather; 空しい describes emptiness/futility of life or effort, not weather.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 2 · どんな気持ち？

items.q: こんな簡単な問題を間違えてしまい、とても（ ）。
items.qr: Konna kantan na mondai o machigaete shimai, totemo (___).
items.en: I made a mistake on such an easy problem — how pathetic of me.
items.hi: इतना आसान सवाल गलत कर दिया, बहुत शर्मनाक है।
items.gu: આટલો સહેલો સવાલ ખોટો કર્યો, ખૂબ શરમજનક છે.
items.why: 情けない is self-directed disappointment/shame at one's own poor performance; 心細い is anxiety from being alone/unsupported — a different feeling entirely.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 2 · どんな気持ち？

items.q: このパソコンは（ ）配線の必要がありません。
items.qr: Kono pasokon wa (___) haisen no hitsuyou ga arimasen.
items.en: This computer doesn't need troublesome wiring.
items.hi: इस कंप्यूटर को झंझट भरी वायरिंग की ज़रूरत नहीं है।
items.gu: આ કમ્પ્યુટરને કંટાળાજનક વાયરિંગની જરૂર નથી.
items.why: Complicated/troublesome wiring is exactly the sense of わずらわしい (troublesome complexity); the others describe unrelated feelings (despicability, dissatisfaction, guilt).
items.unit: Week 1 Day 2 · どんな気持ち？

items.q: 彼こそ大統領に（ ）人物です。
items.qr: Kare koso daitouryou ni (___) jinbutsu desu.
items.en: He is precisely the fitting person to be president.
items.hi: वही राष्ट्रपति बनने के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त व्यक्ति है।
items.gu: તે જ રાષ્ટ્રપતિ બનવા માટે સૌથી યોગ્ય વ્યક્તિ છે.
items.why: ～にふさわしい ("fitting/suitable for ～") is the fixed collocation for matching a role or qualification like 大統領 (president); the other three don't fit that role-matching sense.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 2 · どんな気持ち？

items.q: 肩までお湯によく（ ）。
items.qr: Kata made oyu ni yoku (___).
items.en: Let's soak well in the hot water up to our shoulders.
items.hi: कंधों तक गरम पानी में अच्छी तरह डूबें।
items.gu: ખભા સુધી ગરમ પાણીમાં સારી રીતે પલળીએ.

opts.en: let's scoop up (wrong verb for bathing)

items.why: 湯につかる is the fixed collocation for soaking in a bath; すくう is for scooping something up (like water in your hands), not immersing your whole body.

items.q: 車の前に飛び出してきた猫を（ ）電柱にぶつかってしまった。
items.qr: Kuruma no mae ni tobidashite kita neko o (___) denchuu ni butsukatte shimatta.
items.en: When I swerved to avoid a cat that jumped out in front of the car, I ended up hitting a utility pole.
items.hi: गाड़ी के सामने कूदी बिल्ली से बचने पर बिजली के खंभे से टकरा गया।
items.gu: ગાડી સામે કૂદેલી બિલાડીથી બચતાં વીજળીના થાંભલા સાથે અથડાઈ ગયો.
items.why: よける is the natural verb for swerving/dodging an obstacle like a cat in the road; そらす is for deflecting something (a gaze, a topic), not steering around a physical object.

items.q: 踏切の遮断機を（ ）いけません。
items.qr: Fumikiri no shadanki o (___) ikemasen.
items.en: You must not duck under a railroad crossing gate.
items.hi: रेलवे क्रॉसिंग के फाटक के नीचे से नहीं निकलना चाहिए।
items.gu: રેલવે ક્રોસિંગના ગેટ નીચેથી પસાર થવું જોઈએ નહીં.

opts.en: wander (wrong verb — not about a gate)

items.why: くぐる specifically means passing under/through a low barrier like a gate; さまよう means to wander aimlessly, which doesn't fit a specific barrier at all.

items.q: それは、私が子どものころよく（ ）歌です。
items.qr: Sore wa, watashi ga kodomo no koro yoku (___) uta desu.
items.en: That's a song I often used to hum as a child.
items.hi: यह वह गीत है जिसे मैं बचपन में अक्सर गुनगुनाता था।
items.gu: આ એ ગીત છે જે હું બાળપણમાં વારંવાર ગણગણતો હતો.
items.why: 口ずさむ specifically takes 歌 (a song/tune) as its object; つぶやく is for muttering words to oneself, not melodies.

items.q: ごはんをのりで（ ）食べます。
items.qr: Gohan o nori de (___) tabemasu.
items.en: I eat rice wrapped in nori (seaweed).
items.hi: मैं चावल को नोरी (समुद्री शैवाल) में लपेटकर खाता हूँ।
items.gu: હું ભાતને નોરી (દરિયાઈ શેવાળ)માં લપેટીને ખાઉં છું.
items.why: くるむ means to wrap something around an object (like rice in nori); めくる means to flip/turn a flat page-like thing, not wrap it.

items.q: しかられた生徒は（ ）泣いていた。
items.qr: Shikarareta seito wa (___) naite ita.
items.en: The scolded student hung their head and cried.
items.hi: डाँटा गया छात्र सिर झुकाकर रो रहा था।
items.gu: ઠપકો સાંભળેલો વિદ્યાર્થી માથું નમાવીને રડતો હતો.

opts.en: nodding (wrong — doesn't fit crying in shame)

items.why: A scolded student crying would hang their head down in shame (うつむく), the opposite motion from nodding (うなずく), which signals agreement, not dejection.

items.q: 疲れたのでちょっとソファーで（ ）いいでしょうか。
items.qr: Tsukareta node chotto sofaa de (___) ii deshou ka.
items.en: I'm tired — would it be alright if I lay down on the sofa for a bit?
items.hi: मैं थक गया हूँ, क्या थोड़ी देर सोफे पर लेट सकता हूँ?
items.gu: હું થાકી ગયો છું, થોડીવાર સોફા પર સૂઈ શકું?
items.why: 横になる is the general, unmarked way to say "lie down" for a quick rest — うつ伏せ/仰向け specify a particular position (face-down/up) which isn't implied here, and もがく (struggle) is unrelated to resting.

items.q: 休日に庭を（ ）のが、私の趣味です。
items.qr: Kyuujitsu ni niwa o (___) no ga, watashi no shumi desu.
items.en: Puttering around in the garden on my days off is my hobby.
items.hi: छुट्टी के दिन बगीचे की देखभाल करना मेरा शौक़ है।
items.gu: રજાના દિવસે બગીચામાં થોડું ઘણું કામ કરવું એ મારો શોખ છે.

opts.en: to putter around with, tend to casually

items.why: 庭をいじる is the fixed, general phrase for "puttering around in the garden" as a hobby; さする/むしる/つまむ each describe one narrow physical action, none of which mean "tending a garden generally."

items.q: うちの犬は母にいちばん（ ）います。
items.qr: Uchi no inu wa haha ni ichiban (___) imasu.
items.en: Our dog is most attached to my mother.
items.hi: हमारा कुत्ता माँ से सबसे ज़्यादा हिल-मिल गया है।
items.gu: અમારો કૂતરો માતાથી સૌથી વધુ હળીમળી ગયો છે.

opts.en: popular with (wrong — not about romantic popularity)

items.why: なつく describes an animal or child becoming attached/fond of someone; もてる specifically means being popular with the opposite sex, which doesn't fit a dog and its owner.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 4 · どんな行動・態度？①

items.q: 監督と（ ）その選手は、結局やめさせられてしまった。
items.qr: Kantoku to (___) sono senshu wa, kekkyoku yamesaserarete shimatta.
items.en: The player who clashed with the coach ended up being forced to quit.
items.hi: कोच से झगड़ने वाले उस खिलाड़ी को आख़िरकार टीम छोड़नी पड़ी।
items.gu: કોચ સાથે તકરાર કરનાર એ ખેલાડીને છેવટે છોડવું પડ્યું.
items.why: もめる describes mutual friction/discord between two parties (with と), fitting a falling-out with a coach; ののしる is a one-directional act of cursing at someone, not a mutual clash.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 4 · どんな行動・態度？①

items.q: だれも私のことを（ ）くれない。
items.qr: Dare mo watashi no koto o (___) kurenai.
items.en: Nobody covers for/protects me.
items.hi: कोई भी मेरा बचाव नहीं करता।
items.gu: કોઈ મારો બચાવ કરતું નથી.
items.why: かばう means to protect/stand up for someone under criticism; おごる specifically means paying for someone's meal, an unrelated act of generosity.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 4 · どんな行動・態度？①

items.q: 彼女はご主人によく（ ）います。
items.qr: Kanojo wa go-shujin ni yoku (___) imasu.
items.en: She devotes herself well to her husband.
items.hi: वह अपने पति की बहुत सेवा/समर्पण करती है।
items.gu: તે પોતાના પતિ માટે ખૂબ સમર્પિત રહે છે.

opts.en: support financially (wrong direction — husband typically supports)

items.why: 尽くす means devoting effort/care to someone, fitting a spouse's devotion; 養う specifically means financially supporting dependents, the wrong relationship direction here.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 4 · どんな行動・態度？①

items.q: このまんがの主人公は、最後に悪者をやっと（ ）。
items.qr: Kono manga no shujinkou wa, saigo ni warumono o yatto (___).
items.en: The manga's protagonist finally defeated the villain at the end.
items.hi: इस मंगा के नायक ने अंत में आख़िरकार खलनायक को हरा दिया।
items.gu: આ મંગાના નાયકે અંતે છેવટે ખલનાયકને હરાવી દીધો.

opts.en: reproached (too mild for a final showdown)

items.why: やっつける means to soundly defeat/beat an opponent, fitting a climactic manga showdown; とがめる only means to verbally reproach/blame, far too mild for defeating a villain.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 4 · どんな行動・態度？①

items.q: 彼は親に（ ）育てられた。
items.qr: Kare wa oya ni (___) sodaterareta.
items.en: He was raised being doted on/pampered by his parents.
items.hi: वह अपने माता-पिता के लाड़-प्यार में पला-बढ़ा।
items.gu: તે માતાપિતાના લાડમાં ઉછર્યો.

opts.en: hosted/entertained (wrong — for guests, not raising a child)

items.why: ちやほやする describes spoiling/doting on a person (fitting how a child is raised); もてなす means hosting/entertaining a guest, a one-off act of hospitality, not a child-rearing style.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 4 · どんな行動・態度？①

items.q: いたずらを先生に（ ）された。
items.qr: Itazura o sensei ni (___) sareta.
items.en: [Someone] told on me to the teacher about the mischief.
items.hi: शरारत की चुगली टीचर से कर दी गई।
items.gu: તોફાનની ચાડી શિક્ષકને ખાવામાં આવી.
items.why: 告げ口される is the natural passive form fitting "＿を先生に＿された" (report [X] to the teacher); 言いつける normally takes a different frame (言いつけられた works but not as smoothly with を...に...された here), and the other two options don't mean "tell on" at all.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 4 · どんな行動・態度？①

items.q: 風邪を（ ）入院する騒ぎになってしまった。
items.qr: Kaze o (___) nyuuin suru sawagi ni natte shimatta.
items.en: I let my cold get worse, and it turned into such a fuss that I ended up hospitalized.
items.hi: मेरी सर्दी बिगड़ गई और इतनी हंगामा मच गई कि मुझे अस्पताल भर्ती होना पड़ा।
items.gu: મારી શરદી બગડી ગઈ અને એટલો હોબાળો થયો કે મારે દવાખાનામાં દાખલ થવું પડ્યું.
items.why: 風邪をこじらせる is the fixed idiom for letting a cold worsen through neglect; the other three verbs don't collocate with 風邪 at all.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 4 · どんな行動・態度？①

items.q: 風呂場にかびが（ ）。
items.qr: Furoba ni kabi ga (___).
items.en: Mold grew in the bathroom.
items.hi: बाथरूम में फफूंद उग आई।
items.gu: બાથરૂમમાં ફૂગ ઊગી ગઈ.
items.why: 生える is the intransitive verb for something growing on its own (mold, hair, plants) with が; 生ける means to deliberately arrange flowers, an unrelated action a person does to flowers, not something mold does.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · どんな行動・態度？②

items.q: サルにえさを（ ）ください。
items.qr: Saru ni esa o (___) kudasai.
items.en: Please don't feed the monkeys.
items.hi: कृपया बंदरों को खाना न दें।
items.gu: કૃપા કરીને વાંદરાઓને ખોરાક ન આપો.

opts.en: without setting up (a trap) — wrong object

items.why: 与える is the general verb for giving something (like food) to an animal or person; 仕掛ける specifically means setting up a device/trap, which doesn't take えさ as its object.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · どんな行動・態度？②

items.q: カーテンで光を（ ）。
items.qr: Kaaten de hikari o (___).
items.en: [I] blocked the light with the curtain.
items.hi: पर्दे से रोशनी को रोक दिया।
items.gu: પડદાથી પ્રકાશને રોકી દીધો.

opts.en: applied intensively (wrong — pairs with 工夫, not 光)

items.why: 遮る naturally takes 光 (light) or 話 (speech) as an object it blocks/cuts off; 凝らす is fixed to 工夫 (ingenuity) and doesn't apply to blocking light.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · どんな行動・態度？②

items.q: 切った玉ネギを水に（ ）ください。
items.qr: Kitta tamanegi o mizu ni (___) kudasai.
items.en: Please soak the cut onion in water.
items.hi: कटे हुए प्याज़ को पानी में भिगो दें।
items.gu: સમારેલી ડુંગળીને પાણીમાં પલાળી દો.
items.why: 水にさらす is the fixed cooking-prep phrase for soaking cut vegetables in water; 与える only means "to give," which doesn't describe a soaking process.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · どんな行動・態度？②

items.q: 暑いので、つけていたネクタイを（ ）。
items.qr: Atsui node, tsukete ita nekutai o (___).
items.en: It was hot, so [I] loosened the necktie I was wearing.
items.hi: गर्मी थी, इसलिए पहनी हुई टाई ढीली कर दी।
items.gu: ગરમી હતી, એટલે પહેરેલી ટાઈ ઢીલી કરી.
items.why: 緩める is the physical act of loosening something worn tight, like a necktie; 控える means to moderate/hold back on an amount or habit (like salt intake), not to physically loosen an object.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · どんな行動・態度？②

items.q: 手が滑り、ポップコーンを床に（ ）しまった。
items.qr: Te ga suberi, poppukoon o yuka ni (___) shimatta.
items.en: My hand slipped, and I ended up scattering popcorn all over the floor.
items.hi: हाथ फिसल गया और पॉपकॉर्न फ़र्श पर बिखर गया।
items.gu: હાથ લપસી ગયો અને પોપકોર્ન ફર્શ પર વેરાઈ ગયું.

opts.en: missed/let escape (wrong — for chances, not objects)

items.why: ばらまく describes physically scattering small objects (popcorn, beans); 逃す means missing/letting a chance slip away, an abstract meaning unrelated to spilling something.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · どんな行動・態度？②

items.q: けんかになりそうになったので、あわてて話題を（ ）。
items.qr: Kenka ni narisou ni natta node, awatete wadai o (___).
items.en: It looked like it was about to turn into a fight, so I hurriedly changed the subject.
items.hi: झगड़ा होने वाला था, इसलिए मैंने जल्दी से बात बदल दी।
items.gu: ઝઘડો થવાનો હતો, એટલે મેં ઉતાવળે વિષય બદલી નાખ્યો.
items.why: 話をそらす is the fixed idiom for deliberately changing/deflecting a subject to avoid conflict; the other three verbs don't collocate with 話題 in this sense.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · どんな行動・態度？②

items.q: 彼と（ ）約束を破ってしまった。
items.qr: Kare to (___) yakusoku o yabutte shimatta.
items.en: I ended up breaking the promise I had exchanged with him.
items.hi: उसके साथ किए वादे को मैंने तोड़ दिया।
items.gu: તેની સાથે કરેલું વચન મેં તોડી નાખ્યું.

opts.en: aligned/joined — wrong verb for a promise

items.why: 約束を交わす ("to exchange a promise") is the fixed collocation for two people mutually agreeing to something; 合わす (align), 凝らす (apply ingenuity), and 手掛ける (undertake a project) don't take 約束 as a natural object.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · どんな行動・態度？②

items.q: 母が病院に通うのに（ ）いけない。
items.qr: Haha ga byouin ni kayou no ni (___) ikenai.
items.en: I have to accompany my mother when she goes to the hospital.
items.hi: माँ को अस्पताल जाते समय मुझे उनके साथ जाना पड़ता है।
items.gu: માતાને દવાખાને જતી વખતે મારે તેમની સાથે જવું પડે છે.

opts.en: must visit (wrong verb — for a one-off visit, not accompanying)

items.why: 付き添う means staying by/accompanying someone (like a patient), fitting "going along with mother"; 面会する means visiting someone once, not accompanying them continuously.

items.q: 魚の骨がのどに（ ）。
items.qr: Sakana no hone ga nodo ni (___).
items.en: A fish bone got stuck in my throat.
items.hi: गले में मछली की हड्डी चुभ गई।
items.gu: ગળામાં માછલીનું હાડકું ભોંકાઈ ગયું.

opts.en: was stung/bitten (wrong verb — for insects, not objects)

items.why: 刺さる is intransitive, for an object like a bone or splinter getting stuck in something; 刺される is the passive of 刺す, used for a bug/animal biting/stinging a person, the wrong subject-object relationship here.

items.q: 熱中症で意識が（ ）。
items.qr: Necchuushou de ishiki ga (___).
items.en: Due to heatstroke, his/her consciousness is hazy.
items.hi: लू लगने से होश धुंधला पड़ रहा है।
items.gu: લૂ લાગવાથી ભાન ઝાંખું પડી રહ્યું છે.

opts.en: feels sluggish (wrong subject — describes the body, not 意識)

items.why: 意識がもうろうとする is the fixed phrase for consciousness becoming hazy; だるい describes the body feeling sluggish (体がだるい), a different subject entirely.

items.q: 虫に刺された指がこんなに（ ）しまった。
items.qr: Mushi ni sasareta yubi ga konna ni (___) shimatta.
items.en: The finger that got bitten by a bug swelled up like this.
items.hi: कीड़े के काटने वाली उँगली इतनी सूज गई।
items.gu: જીવડાએ કરડેલી આંગળી આટલી સૂજી ગઈ.

opts.en: scratched (wrong — describes an action, not the swelling result)

items.why: はれる describes a bump/bruise/bite swelling up, the visible result being described here; かく means to scratch, an action rather than the resulting swelling.

items.q: 疲れたせいか、目が（ ）よく見えない。
items.qr: Tsukareta sei ka, me ga (___) yoku mienai.
items.en: Maybe because I'm tired, my vision is blurry and I can't see well.
items.hi: शायद थकान की वजह से, नज़र धुंधली है और साफ़ नहीं दिख रहा।
items.gu: કદાચ થાકને લીધે, નજર ઝાંખી છે અને બરાબર દેખાતું નથી.
items.why: 目がかすむ is the fixed phrase for blurry vision from fatigue; 意識が遠ざかる describes consciousness fading, a different subject (意識, not 目).

items.q: 薬を飲んだらだいぶ痛みが（ ）。
items.qr: Kusuri o nondara daibu itami ga (___).
items.en: After taking medicine, the pain eased up considerably.
items.hi: दवा लेने के बाद दर्द काफ़ी कम हो गया।
items.gu: દવા લીધા પછી દુખાવો ઘણો ઓછો થયો.

opts.en: became weak (wrong subject — 体, not 痛み, though close)

items.why: 痛みが和らぐ is the natural intransitive verb for pain easing on its own (e.g. after medicine); 弱る means one's body/strength weakening, not specifically pain lessening.

items.q: （ ）がするほど、腹が減っている。
items.qr: (___) ga suru hodo, hara ga hette iru.
items.en: I'm so hungry I feel dizzy.
items.hi: इतनी भूख लगी है कि चक्कर आ रहे हैं।
items.gu: એટલી ભૂખ લાગી છે કે ચક્કર આવે છે.

opts.en: a chill (wrong — describes cold, not hunger-induced dizziness)

items.why: めまいがするほど ("to the point of feeling dizzy") is a natural way to emphasize extreme hunger; the other three symptoms don't collocate with intense hunger this way.

items.q: 病気の進行が（ ）、彼はついに意識不明になってしまった。
items.qr: Byouki no shinkou ga (___), kare wa tsui ni ishiki fumei ni natte shimatta.
items.en: As the disease's progression accelerated, he finally became unconscious.
items.hi: बीमारी का बढ़ना तेज़ हो गया, और आख़िरकार वह बेहोश हो गया।
items.gu: રોગની પ્રગતિ ઝડપી થઈ, અને છેવટે તે બેભાન થઈ ગયો.

opts.en: weakened (wrong direction — disease is worsening, not weakening)

items.why: 進行が早まる ("progression speeds up") fits a worsening disease leading to unconsciousness; 早めり isn't a real conjugation, and 弱り／弱まり describe things weakening/easing, the opposite of what leads to becoming unconscious.

items.q: （ ）の発作が起きるとせきが止まらなくなる。
items.qr: (___) no hossa ga okiru to seki ga tomaranaku naru.
items.en: When an asthma attack occurs, the coughing won't stop.
items.hi: जब दमे का दौरा पड़ता है, तो खाँसी रुकती नहीं है।
items.gu: જ્યારે અસ્થમાનો હુમલો આવે છે, ત્યારે ખાંસી અટકતી નથી.
items.why: Day 6's ぜんそくの発作 (asthma attack) is the fixed collocation for a sudden attack that causes uncontrollable coughing.

items.q: 彼女と手をつないで歩いていたら、友達に（ ）。
items.qr: Kanojo to te o tsunaide aruite itara, tomodachi ni (___).
items.en: While I was walking hand-in-hand with my girlfriend, a friend teased me about it.
items.hi: जब मैं अपनी गर्लफ़्रेंड का हाथ थामे चल रहा था, तो दोस्त ने मुझे छेड़ा।
items.gu: હું મારી ગર્લફ્રેન્ડનો હાથ પકડીને ચાલતો હતો ત્યારે મિત્રએ મને ચીડવ્યો.

opts.en: showed off (wrong voice — active, and wrong subject)

items.why: Day 4's 冷やかす describes playful teasing — exactly the reaction friends give when they see a couple holding hands.

items.q: 気に入って買ったバッグを友達に（ ）気分が悪かった。
items.qr: Ki ni itte katta baggu o tomodachi ni (___) kibun ga warukatta.
items.en: A friend badmouthed the bag I'd bought because I liked it, and it put me in a bad mood.
items.hi: जो बैग मुझे पसंद आकर ख़रीदा था, दोस्त ने उसकी बुराई की तो मेरा मूड ख़राब हो गया।
items.gu: મને ગમેલી અને ખરીદેલી બેગની મિત્રએ નિંદા કરી, એટલે મારો મૂડ ખરાબ થયો.

opts.en: was kidnapped/snatched away (wrong — too extreme for a bag comment)
was sneered at (fits mocking a person, not a thing's quality)

items.why: Day 4's けなす (to speak ill of/disparage) is the natural verb for a friend criticizing the quality of a thing you like, like a bag; あざ笑う mocks a person's action, not an object's quality.

items.q: 3歳ぐらいの女の子が、（ ）公園で遊んでいた。
items.qr: San-sai gurai no onna no ko ga, (___) kouen de asonde ita.
items.en: A girl of about three was playing innocently in the park.
items.hi: क़रीब तीन साल की एक बच्ची मासूमियत से पार्क में खेल रही थी।
items.gu: આશરે ત્રણ વર્ષની એક છોકરી નિર્દોષતાથી બગીચામાં રમતી હતી.

opts.en: mild-manneredly (wrong fit for a toddler playing)
gloomily (wrong tone for a child playing)

items.why: Day 1's 無邪気な specifically describes childlike innocence — the natural word for describing how a small child plays.

items.q: 彼はだれにでも優しい（ ）人で、みんなに好かれている。
items.qr: Kare wa dare ni demo yasashii (___) hito de, minna ni sukarete iru.
items.en: He's a considerate person who's kind to everyone, and is liked by all.
items.hi: वह सबके प्रति दयालु और सबका ख़याल रखने वाला है, इसलिए सभी उसे पसंद करते हैं।
items.gu: તે બધા પ્રત્યે માયાળુ અને બધાની કાળજી રાખનાર છે, એટલે બધા તેને પસંદ કરે છે.

opts.en: pushy, intrusive (contradicts being liked by all)

items.why: Day 1's 思いやりがある (considerate) fits someone kind to everyone and universally liked; でしゃばり/きざ describe traits people usually dislike.

items.q: バスタオルを（ ）枕の代わりにした。
items.qr: Basutaoru o (___) makura no kawari ni shita.
items.en: I rolled up a bath towel and used it in place of a pillow.
items.hi: बाथ टॉवल को गोल लपेटकर तकिए की जगह इस्तेमाल किया।
items.gu: બાથ ટુવાલને ગોળ વાળીને ઓશીકાની જગ્યાએ વાપર્યો.
items.why: Day 3's 丸める means rolling something into a compact shape, exactly what you do with a towel to use it as a makeshift pillow.

items.q: 母に（ ）早く家を出た。
items.qr: Haha ni (___) hayaku ie o deta.
items.en: Prompted by my mother, I left home early.
items.hi: माँ के कहने पर मैं जल्दी घर से निकल गया।
items.gu: માતાએ ઉતાવળ કરાવી એટલે હું વહેલો ઘરેથી નીકળ્યો.

opts.en: had a trap set on me (wrong meaning)

items.why: Day 5's 促す (to urge/prompt) fits being encouraged by one's mother to hurry up and leave.

items.q: 長い間立ちっぱなしだったので、足が（ ）しまった。
items.qr: Nagai aida tacchippanashi datta node, ashi ga (___) shimatta.
items.en: Since I was standing for a long time, my legs ended up swelling.
items.hi: लंबे समय तक खड़ा रहने से पैरों में सूजन आ गई।
items.gu: લાંબા સમય સુધી ઊભા રહેવાથી પગમાં સોજો આવી ગયો.

opts.en: became hazy (wrong subject — for 意識, not legs)

items.why: Day 6's 足がむくむ is the fixed phrase for legs swelling after prolonged standing.

items.q: これはみそを（ ）調理器具です。
items.qr: Kore wa miso o (___) chouri kigu desu.
items.en: This is a cooking tool for straining miso.
items.hi: यह मिसो को छानने का रसोई उपकरण है।
items.gu: આ મિસો ગાળવાનું રસોઈ સાધન છે.
items.why: Day 5's こす (to filter/strain) is exactly what a strainer-type tool does to dissolved miso when making soup.

items.q: 細いひもを何本も（ ）太いロープを作った。
items.qr: Hosoi himo o nanbon mo (___) futoi roopu o tsukutta.
items.en: By bundling together many thin strings, I made a thick rope.
items.hi: कई पतली डोरियों को एक साथ बाँधकर एक मोटी रस्सी बनाई।
items.gu: ઘણી પાતળી દોરીઓ ભેગી બાંધીને એક જાડું દોરડું બનાવ્યું.
items.why: Day 5's 束ねる (to bundle/tie up) is exactly the action of gathering many thin strings into one thick rope.

items.q: 性格が良くやさしい。 ("Good-natured and kind.")
items.qr: Seikaku ga yoku yasashii.

opts.en: desirable (describes situations, not a person's nature)

items.why: Day 1's 気立てがいい is defined exactly as "good-natured, kind at heart" — a direct match.

items.q: ひそかに計画する。 ("To plan secretly.")
items.qr: Hisoka ni keikaku suru.
items.why: Day 5's もくろむ carries exactly this connotation of scheming/planning something secretly.

items.q: 相手の気にいるようなことを言って、得意にさせる。 ("To say things that please the other person, making them feel proud of themselves.")
items.qr: Aite no ki ni iru you na koto o itte, tokui ni saseru.

opts.en: to tease (wrong tone — teasing isn't flattering)

items.why: Day 4's おだてる is defined exactly as saying pleasing things to make someone feel proud/pleased with themselves.

items.q: 暑いときになりやすい症状。 ("A symptom that's common in hot weather.")
items.qr: Atsui toki ni nariyasui shoujou.
items.why: Day 6's 熱中症 (heatstroke) is literally caused by heat — the only option directly tied to hot weather.

items.q: 複雑な事情が絡んで物事がすらすら行かなくなること。 ("When complicated circumstances get tangled up and things stop going smoothly.")
items.qr: Fukuzatsu na jijou ga karande monogoto ga surasura ikanaku naru koto.
items.why: Day 4's 話がこじれる is defined exactly as a matter getting complicated through tangled circumstances.

items.q: あの若者はりりしくて立派だ。
items.qr: Ano wakamono wa ririshikute rippa da.
items.en: That young man is gallant and admirable.
items.why: Day 1's りりしい (gallant/dashing) and 勇ましい (brave/valiant) both describe an admirable, bold bearing — the closest match among the options.

items.q: 一人で行くのはいやだ。だれか一緒に行ってほしい。
items.u: 一緒に行って / issho ni itte
items.qr: Hitori de iku no wa iyada. Dareka issho ni itte hoshii.
items.en: I don't want to go alone. I want someone to come along with me.

opts.en: to run into by chance — wrong meaning
to feel constrained about imposing — wrong meaning

items.why: Day 6's 付き添う (to accompany/stay with someone) is the closest match to wanting someone to go along together.

items.q: だめだとわかったら、きっぱりあきらめよう。
items.qr: Dame da to wakattara, kippari akirameyou.
items.en: Once you know it's no good, give up decisively/cleanly.
items.why: Day 1's いさぎよい describes accepting/deciding something cleanly without complaint — the closest match to きっぱり (decisively).

items.q: 彼は上司の命令に反して行動したため、首になった。
items.qr: Kare wa joushi no meirei ni hanshite koudou shita tame, kubi ni natta.
items.en: He acted against his boss's orders, so he was fired.

opts.en: reproaching (wrong meaning — that's what you do to a person, not an order)

items.why: Day 5's 命令に背く is the direct synonym of 命令に反する — both mean disobeying an order.

items.q: 寄付は強制されるとしたくなくなるものだ。
items.qr: Kifu wa kyousei sareru to shitakunaku naru mono da.
items.en: If a donation is forced on you, you lose the will to give it.

opts.en: has effort devoted to it (wrong meaning)

items.why: Day 4's 寄付を強いる (to press/force someone to contribute) is the direct source of 強制される here — 強いられる is its exact passive-voice synonym.

items.q: しぶとい
items.qr: shibutoi

opts.t: 敵もしぶとく、なかなか負けを認めない。
opts.r: Teki mo shibutoku, nakanaka make o mitomenai.
opts.en: The enemy too is tenacious, and won't easily admit defeat.

opts.t: この柿はちょっとしぶとい。
opts.en: This persimmon is a bit [shibutoi] — wrong word; astringent taste is 渋い(shibui), not しぶとい

opts.t: しぶといお茶はとてもおいしい。
opts.en: [Shibutoi] tea is delicious — same confusion with 渋い

opts.t: 庭の木がとてもしぶとくなってきた。
opts.r: Niwa no ki ga totemo shibutoku natte kita.
opts.en: The garden tree became very [shibutoi] — doesn't fit a tree

items.why: しぶとい means stubborn/tenacious about a person or agent refusing to give up — only sentence 1 fits. Sentences 2–3 confuse it with the unrelated word 渋い (shibui, "astringent/bitter-tasting"), a classic sound-alike trap.

items.q: 近寄りがたい
items.qr: chikayorigatai

opts.t: 私の上司は気さくで近寄りがたい。
opts.r: Watashi no joushi wa kisaku de chikayorigatai.
opts.en: My boss is friendly and hard-to-approach — self-contradictory

opts.t: 彼女は近寄りがたいほど美しい。
opts.en: She is beautiful to the point of being hard to approach.

opts.t: 泥棒が近寄りがたい柵を作った。
opts.r: Dorobou ga chikayorigatai saku o tsukutta.
opts.en: A thief made a hard-to-approach fence — wrong, describes a feeling toward people, not a physical barrier's own trait

opts.t: 古本屋で近寄りがたい本を手に入れた。
opts.r: Furuhon'ya de chikayorigatai hon o te ni ireta.
opts.en: Got a hard-to-approach book at a used bookstore — doesn't fit an object

items.why: 近寄りがたい naturally describes a person so impressive (often beautiful) that others feel hesitant to approach — sentence 1 is self-contradictory (気さく directly means approachable), and 3–4 misapply it to objects.

items.q: 見せびらかす
items.qr: misebirakasu

opts.t: おばあちゃんは孫にお年玉を見せびらかした。
opts.r: Obaachan wa mago ni otoshidama o misebirakashita.
opts.en: Grandma showed off New Year's money to her grandchild — doesn't fit the boastful-to-a-peer connotation

opts.t: 美容院で髪を見せびらかしてもらった。
opts.r: Biyouin de kami o misebirakashite moratta.
opts.en: Had my hair "shown off" at the salon — not idiomatic

opts.t: 今日は私が食事を見せびらかします。
opts.r: Kyou wa watashi ga shokuji o misebirakashimasu.
opts.en: Today I will show off the meal — not idiomatic

opts.t: 彼は新しい腕時計をみんなに見せびらかしていた。
opts.r: Kare wa atarashii udedokei o minna ni misebirakashite ita.
opts.en: He was showing off his new watch to everyone.

items.why: 見せびらかす means boastfully showing off a possession to others, exactly like Day 4's own example 新しいバッグを見せびらかす — sentence 4 matches that pattern precisely.

items.q: むせる
items.qr: museru

opts.t: そのパーティー会場には、むせるほど人が来ていた。
opts.r: Sono paatii kaijou ni wa, museru hodo hito ga kite ita.
opts.en: So many people had come to the party venue it was stifling.

opts.t: タバコの煙が目にむせた。
opts.r: Tabako no kemuri ga me ni museta.
opts.en: Cigarette smoke "choked" in the eyes — wrong; むせる is about throat/breathing, not eyes

opts.t: 今日はよく晴れたむせる天気だ。
opts.r: Kyou wa yoku hareta museru tenki da.
opts.en: Today is clear, "choking" weather — doesn't fit clear weather

opts.t: 捻挫した足がだんだんむせてきた。
opts.r: Nenza shita ashi ga dandan musete kita.
opts.en: The sprained foot gradually "choked" — wrong verb for swelling

items.why: むせる (to choke, from smoke/crowding/humidity) extends idiomatically to an overwhelming, stifling crowd (人いきれでむせる); the other three misapply it to eyes, clear weather, and an injury, none of which involve choking/breathing difficulty.

items.q: 片思い
items.qr: kataomoi

opts.t: 上司の不正を片思いして警察に通報した。
opts.r: Joushi no fusei o kataomoi shite keisatsu ni tsuuhou shita.
opts.en: "Kataomoi'd" the boss's misconduct and reported it — nonsensical

opts.t: 彼女の帰りを片思いして待っていた。
opts.r: Kanojo no kaeri o kataomoi shite matte ita.
opts.en: Was "kataomoi-ing" waiting for her return — wrong grammar/sense

opts.t: 私の初恋は片思いで終わってしまった。
opts.r: Watashi no hatsukoi wa kataomoi de owatte shimatta.
opts.en: My first love ended in unrequited love.

opts.t: 親はかわいいわが子に片思いするものです。
opts.r: Oya wa kawaii waga ko ni kataomoi suru mono desu.
opts.en: Parents "kataomoi" their cute children — wrong; parental love isn't romantic one-sided love

items.why: 片思い specifically means one-sided romantic love that isn't reciprocated — only sentence 3 uses it in that exact romantic sense; the others misapply it to unrelated situations (whistleblowing, waiting, parental love).

items.q: 駅で電車の乗り換えに（ ）。
items.qr: Eki de densha no norikae ni (___).
items.en: I was flustered/confused transferring trains at the station.
items.hi: स्टेशन पर ट्रेन बदलते समय मैं घबरा गया।
items.gu: સ્ટેશન પર ટ્રેન બદલતી વખતે હું ગભરાઈ ગયો.
items.why: Not knowing how to transfer trains causes confusion/flustered fumbling (まごつく), not fear (おびえる) — there's no threat here, just unfamiliarity.

items.q: ピントが合っていない（ ）写真。
items.qr: Pinto ga atte inai (___) shashin.
items.en: An out-of-focus photo whose focus isn't right.
items.hi: जो फोटो का फोकस सही नहीं है, वह धुंधली तस्वीर।
items.gu: જે ફોટોનું ફોકસ બરાબર નથી, તે અસ્પષ્ટ તસવીર.
items.why: ぼける applied to a photo means "out of focus/blurry" — とぼける is a completely different word meaning "to play dumb," a classic sound-alike trap.

items.q: 彼は自分に才能があると（ ）いる。
items.qr: Kare wa jibun ni sainou ga aru to (___) iru.
items.en: He's conceited, thinking he has talent.
items.hi: वह यह सोचकर घमंड करता है कि उसमें प्रतिभा है।
items.gu: તે એવું માનીને ગુમાન કરે છે કે તેનામાં પ્રતિભા છે.
items.why: Believing you have talent and feeling proud/superior about it is exactly うぬぼれる (conceit) — こだわる is about being fussy/particular, not about self-image.

items.q: あの建物はかなり（ ）造りをしている。
items.qr: Ano tatemono wa kanari (___) tsukuri o shite iru.
items.en: That building has quite an elaborate/intricate construction.
items.hi: उस इमारत की बनावट काफ़ी बारीक/जटिल है।
items.gu: તે ઇમારતની બાંધણી ખૂબ ઝીણવટભરી/જટિલ છે.
items.why: こった (past form of 凝る used adjectivally) describes something made with elaborate care/detail, like an intricate building design — 懲りる (learn a lesson) doesn't fit a building at all, another sound-alike trap between 凝る and 懲りる.

items.q: 1時間待ってもバスが来ない。もう待ち（ ）よ。
items.qr: Ichijikan matte mo basu ga konai. Mou machi(___) yo.
items.en: I've waited an hour and the bus still hasn't come. I'm tired of waiting!
items.hi: एक घंटे से इंतज़ार कर रहा हूँ, बस अभी तक नहीं आई। अब इंतज़ार करते-करते थक गया!
items.gu: એક કલાકથી રાહ જોઉં છું, બસ હજી આવી નથી. હવે રાહ જોઈ જોઈને થાકી ગયો!

opts.en: became exhausted (too strong/physical for just waiting)

items.why: 待ちくたびれる is the fixed collocation for growing weary of waiting; ばてる implies physical exhaustion from exertion (overtime, exercise), not idle waiting.

items.q: 彼は自分の失敗を（ ）。
items.qr: Kare wa jibun no shippai o (___).
items.en: He lamented his own failure.
items.hi: उसने अपनी असफलता पर शोक जताया।
items.gu: તેણે પોતાની નિષ્ફળતા પર શોક વ્યક્ત કર્યો.

opts.en: was stunned (wrong nuance — passive shock, not active grief)

items.why: 失敗を嘆く actively grieves/laments over a failure one caused; ぼうぜんとする describes a stunned, blank-minded reaction to a shock, not a reflective lament.

items.q: 夢が（ ）プロの野球選手になれた！
items.qr: Yume ga (___) puro no yakyuu senshu ni nareta!
items.en: My dream came true and I became a pro baseball player!
items.hi: मेरा सपना पूरा हुआ और मैं एक पेशेवर बेसबॉल खिलाड़ी बन गया!
items.gu: મારું સપનું પૂરું થયું અને હું પ્રોફેશનલ બેઝબોલ ખેલાડી બની ગયો!

opts.en: got fired up (wrong grammar — describes a person, not a dream)

items.why: 夢がかなう ("a dream comes true") is the fixed collocation for 夢 as the grammatical subject — the other three don't take 夢 as their subject this way.

items.q: 少年は年齢を（ ）たばこを買った。
items.qr: Shounen wa nenrei o (___) tabako o katta.
items.en: The boy lied about his age and bought cigarettes.
items.hi: लड़के ने अपनी उम्र के बारे में झूठ बोलकर सिगरेट ख़रीदी।
items.gu: છોકરાએ પોતાની ઉંમર વિશે જૂઠું બોલીને સિગારેટ ખરીદી.
items.why: 年齢をごまかす is the fixed collocation for lying/falsifying one's age — exactly what a minor does to buy cigarettes.

items.q: 最近、先の（ ）靴がはやっているようだ。
items.qr: Saikin, saki no (___) kutsu ga hayatte iru you da.
items.en: Pointy-toed shoes seem to be trending recently.
items.hi: आजकल आगे से नुकीले जूते चलन में लग रहे हैं।
items.gu: હમણાં આગળથી અણીદાર બૂટ ચલણમાં હોય એવું લાગે છે.

opts.en: towered (wrong scale — for buildings, not shoe tips)

items.why: A shoe's pointed toe is とがった (sharp/pointed) — そびえる describes something towering high, the wrong scale for a shoe tip.

items.q: 戸が（ ）キーキーうるさい音がする。
items.qr: To ga (___) kiikii urusai oto ga suru.
items.en: The door creaks, making an annoying squeaky sound.
items.hi: दरवाज़ा चरचराकर कर्कश आवाज़ करता है।
items.gu: બારણું કિચૂડ કિચૂડ કરીને કર્કશ અવાજ કરે છે.
items.why: きしむ is the natural verb for a door/floor making a squeaky, grating sound; さえずる is reserved for birds chirping.

items.q: このシチューは牛肉が（ ）ようにやわらかくて、とてもおいしい。
items.qr: Kono shichuu wa gyuuniku ga (___) you ni yawarakakute, totemo oishii.
items.en: This stew's beef is so tender it melts in your mouth — it's delicious.
items.hi: इस स्टू का गोश्त इतना नरम है कि मुँह में घुल जाता है, बहुत स्वादिष्ट है।
items.gu: આ સ્ટ્યુનું માંસ એટલું નરમ છે કે મોંમાં ઓગળી જાય છે, ખૂબ સ્વાદિષ્ટ છે.
items.why: とろけるよう (melt-in-your-mouth) is the standard way to praise very tender meat — たるむ describes sagging/slackening, not texture.

items.q: 母が穴の空いた靴下を（ ）くれた。
items.qr: Haha ga ana no aita kutsushita o (___) kureta.
items.en: Mother mended my socks that had holes in them.
items.hi: माँ ने छेद वाले मोज़ों की सिलाई कर दी।
items.gu: મમ્મીએ કાણાં પડેલા મોજાં સાંધી આપ્યાં.
items.why: 繕う is exactly the verb for mending a hole/tear in clothing; 潤う describes something becoming moist or prospering, unrelated to sewing.

items.q: バットを振ったが、ボールは（ ）だけで飛ばなかった。
items.qr: Batto o futta ga, booru wa (___) dake de tobanakatta.
items.en: I swung the bat, but it only grazed the ball, which didn't fly.
items.hi: बल्ला घुमाया, पर गेंद को बस छूकर निकल गया, वह उड़ नहीं पाई।
items.gu: બેટ ફેરવ્યું, પણ બોલને ફક્ત સ્પર્શ થયો, તે ઊડી ન શક્યો.

opts.en: approached/reached (wrong meaning — for a point in time/place)

items.why: A bat barely touching a ball is かする (graze); 差し掛かる describes approaching a turning point or life stage, not a glancing physical contact.

items.q: メガネが合わないのか、字が（ ）よく見えない。
items.qr: Megane ga awanai no ka, ji ga (___) yoku mienai.
items.en: Maybe my glasses don't fit — the letters look blurry and I can't see them well.
items.hi: शायद चश्मा ठीक नहीं है, अक्षर धुंधले दिख रहे हैं।
items.gu: કદાચ ચશ્માં બરાબર નથી, અક્ષરો ઝાંખા દેખાય છે.
items.why: Letters being hard to see clearly is ぼやける (indistinct/blurry); かする means a glancing touch, not a visual quality.

items.q: この布は水を（ ）加工がされている。
items.qr: Kono nuno wa mizu o (___) kakou ga sarete iru.
items.en: This cloth has been treated to repel water.
items.hi: इस कपड़े को पानी को परे धकेलने के लिए प्रोसेस किया गया है।
items.gu: આ કાપડને પાણી દૂર ધકેલવા માટે પ્રોસેસ કરવામાં આવ્યું છે.
items.why: 水を弾く is the fixed phrase for a water-repellent treatment on fabric — exactly this sentence's example from the word list.

items.q: 虫歯で顔が（ ）しまった。
items.qr: Mushiba de kao ga (___) shimatta.
items.en: My face swelled up because of a cavity.
items.hi: दाँत में कीड़ा लगने से चेहरे पर सूजन आ गई।
items.gu: દાંતમાં કીડો પડવાથી ચહેરા પર સોજો આવી ગયો.

opts.en: camera-shake blurred (wrong subject — photos, not faces)

items.why: A face swelling from a bad tooth is はれる (swell) — the other three options describe peeling/balding, misalignment, and photo blur, none of which fit a swollen face.

items.q: 彼の順位は周囲の予想を（ ）3位に終わった。
items.qr: Kare no jun'i wa shuui no yosou o (___) san'i ni owatta.
items.en: His ranking overturned everyone's predictions, ending in 3rd place.
items.hi: उसकी रैंकिंग ने सबके अनुमान को पलट दिया और वह तीसरे स्थान पर रहा।
items.gu: તેનો ક્રમ બધાની ધારણાને ઊંધી પાડીને ત્રીજા સ્થાને આવ્યો.

opts.en: was cut off (wrong meaning — for contact/news)

items.why: 予想を覆す (overturn expectations) is the fixed phrase for defying what everyone predicted; 途絶える describes contact/news stopping, unrelated to predictions.

items.q: 結婚式のスピーチで、型に（ ）あいさつが続いた。
items.qr: Kekkonshiki no supiichi de, kata ni (___) aisatsu ga tsuzuita.
items.en: At the wedding speeches, one formulaic, by-the-book greeting after another continued.
items.hi: शादी के भाषणों में एक के बाद एक रटी-रटाई शुभकामनाएँ चलती रहीं।
items.gu: લગ્નના ભાષણોમાં એક પછી એક ઢાંચાગત શુભેચ્છાઓ ચાલુ રહી.
items.why: 型にはまる (fit the mold) describes something clichéd and formulaic, exactly the wedding-speech stereotype; 染まる means "to be dyed," unrelated.

items.q: 左右のバランスが（ ）いるのなら、まっすぐに進むはずだ。
items.qr: Sayuu no baransu ga (___) iru no nara, massugu ni susumu hazu da.
items.en: If the left-right balance is even, it should go straight.
items.hi: अगर दायाँ-बायाँ संतुलन बराबर है, तो यह सीधा चलना चाहिए।
items.gu: જો ડાબે-જમણે સંતુલન બરાબર હોય, તો તે સીધું જવું જોઈએ.

opts.en: is biased/leaning to one side (contradicts going straight)

items.why: Only a balanced (釣り合っている) left-right weight lets something travel straight; 偏る (leaning to one side) would logically cause it to veer off course instead.

items.q: 彼は山の草や木の実を食べて飢えを（ ）らしい。
items.qr: Kare wa yama no kusa ya ki no mi o tabete ue o (___) rashii.
items.en: He apparently staved off his hunger by eating mountain grass and nuts.
items.hi: लगता है उसने पहाड़ की घास और मेवे खाकर भूख मिटाई।
items.gu: લાગે છે કે તેણે પહાડની ઘાસ અને ફળો ખાઈને ભૂખ સહન કરી.

opts.en: ran out (wrong grammar — 飢えが尽きる isn't natural)

items.why: 飢えをしのぐ (stave off hunger) is the fixed collocation for enduring hunger with makeshift food; 尽きる describes something running out, not being endured.

items.q: そのとき一瞬、雲が（ ）陽がさした。
items.qr: Sono toki isshun, kumo ga (___) hi ga sashita.
items.en: At that moment, the clouds broke for an instant and the sun shone through.
items.hi: उस पल एक क्षण के लिए बादल छँट गए और धूप निकल आई।
items.gu: તે ક્ષણે વાદળો એક પળ માટે તૂટ્યાં અને તડકો પડ્યો.
items.why: A momentary gap/break in the clouds is 途切れる; 廃れる only applies to fashions/customs going obsolete, not a physical break in clouds.

items.q: 浮気が妻に（ ）しまった。
items.qr: Uwaki ga tsuma ni (___) shimatta.
items.en: His affair got exposed to his wife.
items.hi: उसका अफेयर पत्नी के सामने उजागर हो गया।
items.gu: તેની બેવફાઈ પત્નીની સામે ખુલ્લી પડી ગઈ.
items.why: An affair being found out is うそ／浮気がばれる (exposed); 化ける means to disguise or transform into something else — a sound-alike but unrelated verb.

items.q: 酔っ払いに（ ）けんかになった。
items.qr: Yopparai ni (___) kenka ni natta.
items.en: A drunk person picked a fight with me, and it turned into a quarrel.
items.hi: एक शराबी ने झगड़ा मोल लिया और बात लड़ाई तक पहुँच गई।
items.gu: એક દારૂડિયાએ ઝઘડો ઊભો કર્યો અને વાત મારામારી સુધી પહોંચી.

opts.en: had someone pick a fight with me

items.why: 酔っ払いに絡まれる is the fixed phrase for a drunk picking a fight/pestering you — exactly matching the word list's own example.

items.q: その村の人口の減少は（ ）ことがなく、とうとう小学校もなくなってしまった。
items.qr: Sono mura no jinkou no genshou wa (___) koto ga naku, toutou shougakkou mo nakunatte shimatta.
items.en: That village's population decline never stopped, and finally even the elementary school disappeared.
items.hi: उस गाँव की जनसंख्या में गिरावट कभी नहीं रुकी, और आख़िरकार प्राथमिक स्कूल भी बंद हो गया।
items.gu: તે ગામની વસ્તીનો ઘટાડો ક્યારેય અટક્યો નહીં, અને છેવટે પ્રાથમિક શાળા પણ બંધ થઈ ગઈ.
items.why: とどまることがない ("never stops") is the fixed pattern for describing a trend that keeps going unabated, exactly matching the word list's 物価の上昇はとどまることがない example.

items.q: あの役者は年を取ってからはとても落ち着いた（ ）演技をする。
items.qr: Ano yakusha wa toshi o totte kara wa totemo ochitsuita (___) engi o suru.
items.en: Since getting older, that actor gives a very calm, understated performance.
items.hi: उस अभिनेता का अभिनय उम्र बढ़ने के बाद बहुत शांत और गंभीर हो गया है।
items.gu: તે અભિનેતાનો અભિનય ઉંમર વધ્યા પછી ખૂબ શાંત અને ગંભીર થઈ ગયો છે.
items.why: 渋い演技 describes a mature, understated acting style — fitting "calm" (落ち着いた); 華々しい means flashy/glorious, the opposite of calm and understated.

items.q: そのサッカー選手は（ ）技で、観客を魅了した。
items.qr: Sono sakkaa senshu wa (___) waza de, kankyaku o miryou shita.
items.en: That soccer player captivated the audience with skillful technique.
items.hi: उस फुटबॉल खिलाड़ी ने अपनी कुशल तकनीक से दर्शकों को मंत्रमुग्ध कर दिया।
items.gu: તે ફૂટબોલ ખેલાડીએ પોતાની કુશળ ટેકનિકથી પ્રેક્ષકોને મંત્રમુગ્ધ કરી દીધા.
items.why: A player's technique/skill is described with 巧みな (skillful); つぶらな only describes round eyes, unrelated to athletic ability.

items.q: スタートは（ ）だったのに、最後は力が尽きて最下位になった。
items.qr: Sutaato wa (___) datta noni, saigo wa chikara ga tsukite saikai ni natta.
items.en: Even though the start was strong, they ran out of strength at the end and came in last.
items.hi: शुरुआत अच्छी थी, फिर भी आख़िर में ताक़त ख़त्म होने से वह आख़िरी स्थान पर आया।
items.gu: શરૂઆત સારી હતી, છતાં અંતે તાકાત ખૂટવાથી તે છેલ્લા સ્થાને આવ્યો.

opts.en: sound (wrong domain — abstract soundness, not race performance)

items.why: A race/performance starting well is 好調 (in good form); 健全 describes soundness of mind/systems/finances, not athletic performance.

items.q: 彼女はいつも（ ）アクセサリーを身につけている。
items.qr: Kanojo wa itsumo (___) akusesarii o mi ni tsukete iru.
items.en: She always wears dazzling, gorgeous accessories.
items.hi: वह हमेशा चमक-दमक भरे गहने पहनती है।
items.gu: તે હંમેશાં ઝગમગાટ ભર્યાં ઘરેણાં પહેરે છે.
items.why: Flashy, gorgeous accessories are きらびやか; しなやか describes physical suppleness (a body, a branch), not jewelry's appearance.

items.q: お客様に（ ）サービスを提供する。
items.qr: Okyakusama ni (___) saabisu o teikyou suru.
items.en: Provide attentive, thoughtful service to customers.
items.hi: ग्राहकों को बारीकी से ध्यान रखने वाली सेवा देना।
items.gu: ગ્રાહકોને ઝીણવટભરી કાળજીવાળી સેવા આપવી.

opts.en: smooth (texture, wrong domain for service quality)

items.why: 細やかなサービス (attentive, detail-oriented service) is the standard collocation for good customer care; 滑らか describes a physically smooth texture, not service quality.

items.q: 景気は（ ）回復しています。
items.qr: Keiki wa (___) kaifuku shite imasu.
items.en: The economy is recovering gradually/gently.
items.hi: अर्थव्यवस्था धीरे-धीरे सुधर रही है।
items.gu: અર્થતંત્ર ધીમે ધીમે સુધરી રહ્યું છે.

opts.en: tranquilly (wrong domain — scenery/pace of life, not an economy)

items.why: A gradual economic recovery is 緩やかに回復する (recover gently/gradually); のどか describes a peaceful, unhurried scene or lifestyle, not an economic trend.

items.q: パーティーは（ ）雰囲気で進行していった。
items.qr: Paatii wa (___) fun'iki de shinkou shite itta.
items.en: The party proceeded in a friendly, harmonious atmosphere.
items.hi: पार्टी एक मैत्रीपूर्ण माहौल में आगे बढ़ती रही।
items.gu: પાર્ટી મૈત્રીપૂર્ણ માહોલમાં આગળ વધતી રહી.
items.why: A friendly social atmosphere is 和やかな雰囲気 — a fixed collocation; the other options describe color vividness, physical health, and speed, none of which fit "atmosphere."

items.q: 夫婦（ ）で、幸せな生活を送っています。
items.qr: Fuufu (___) de, shiawase na seikatsu o okutte imasu.
items.en: The couple is happy and harmonious, living a good life together.
items.hi: पति-पत्नी के बीच सामंजस्य है, वे सुखी जीवन बिता रहे हैं।
items.gu: પતિ-પત્ની વચ્ચે સંવાદિતા છે, તેઓ સુખી જીવન જીવે છે.

opts.en: going well (wrong domain — for performance/sales, not a marriage)

items.why: 夫婦円満 (marital harmony) is a fixed four-character-style phrase specifically for a happy marriage — none of the other options collocate with 夫婦.

items.q: ドライブの前に（ ）車の点検をした。
items.qr: Doraibu no mae ni (___) kuruma no tenken o shita.
items.en: Before the drive, I did a thorough car inspection.
items.hi: ड्राइव से पहले मैंने गाड़ी की बारीकी से जाँच की।
items.gu: ડ્રાઇવ પહેલાં મેં ગાડીની ઝીણવટપૂર્વક તપાસ કરી.
items.why: 念入りな点検 (a thorough inspection) is the fixed collocation for carefully checking something before a trip; まとも means "proper/decent," not "thorough."

items.q: 一軒家といっても、二部屋だけの（ ）家です。
items.qr: Ikkenya to itte mo, futaheya dake no (___) ie desu.
items.en: Though it's called a house, it's just a tiny two-room place.
items.hi: घर तो कहते हैं, पर यह सिर्फ़ दो कमरों का बहुत छोटा-सा घर है।
items.gu: ઘર કહેવાય છે, પણ તે ફક્ત બે ઓરડાનું ખૂબ નાનું ઘર છે.

opts.en: scarce/lacking (wrong grammar — describes a lack of something, not a house's size)

items.why: A small, two-room house is ちっぽけな (tiny); 乏しい describes a shortage/scarcity of something (like resources), not a building's physical size.

items.q: 子育ては決して（ ）ことではない。
items.qr: Kosodate wa kesshite (___) koto dewa nai.
items.en: Raising children is by no means an easy thing.
items.hi: बच्चों की परवरिश करना बिल्कुल भी आसान काम नहीं है।
items.gu: બાળઉછેર બિલકુલ સહેલું કામ નથી.
items.why: 決して〜ない (by no means) sets up a denial of ease, so たやすい (easy) is needed to negate; おろそか describes neglecting a duty, a different idea entirely.

items.q: 電話から（ ）声が聞こえてきた。
items.qr: Denwa kara (___) koe ga kikoete kita.
items.en: An eerie voice came through the phone.
items.hi: फ़ोन से एक डरावनी आवाज़ सुनाई दी।
items.gu: ફોનમાંથી ડરામણો અવાજ સંભળાયો.

opts.en: unshapely/ugly (wrong domain — describes appearance, not sound)

items.why: A creepy, unsettling voice is 不気味な; 不細工 describes physical ugliness/unshapeliness, which doesn't apply to a sound.

items.q: （ ）から、電車の中でお化粧するのはやめなさい。
items.qr: (___) kara, densha no naka de okeshou suru no wa yamenasai.
items.en: It's unseemly, so stop putting on makeup on the train.
items.hi: यह शर्मनाक लगता है, इसलिए ट्रेन में मेकअप करना बंद करो।
items.gu: તે બેઢંગું લાગે છે, એટલે ટ્રેનમાં મેકઅપ કરવાનું બંધ કરો.
items.why: Doing your makeup in public is a breach of decorum — みっともない (unseemly behavior); みすぼらしい describes a poor/shabby appearance, unrelated to manners.

items.q: 生まれて1週間で死ぬという（ ）命の虫。
items.qr: Umarete isshuukan de shinu to iu (___) inochi no mushi.
items.en: An insect with such a fleeting life that it dies just one week after being born.
items.hi: एक ऐसा कीट जिसकी ज़िंदगी इतनी क्षणभंगुर है कि जन्म के एक हफ़्ते में ही मर जाता है।
items.gu: એક એવો જીવડો જેની જિંદગી એટલી ક્ષણભંગુર છે કે જન્મના એક અઠવાડિયામાં જ મરી જાય છે.

opts.en: precarious/in danger (wrong nuance — implies an external threat, not a naturally short lifespan)

items.why: はかない命 (a fleeting life) is the classic phrase for a creature whose entire natural lifespan is short (like a mayfly) — 危うい describes danger from an outside threat, not a naturally brief life.

items.q: 友人に金を貸してほしいと言ったら、（ ）いやな顔をされた。
items.qr: Yuujin ni kane o kashite hoshii to ittara, (___) iya na kao o sareta.
items.en: When I asked a friend to lend me money, they openly made a displeased face.
items.hi: जब मैंने दोस्त से पैसे उधार माँगे, तो उसने साफ़-साफ़ नाराज़गी वाला चेहरा बना लिया।
items.gu: મેં મિત્રને પૈસા ઉધાર માંગ્યા ત્યારે તેણે ખુલ્લંખુલ્લા નારાજગીભર્યો ચહેરો બનાવ્યો.

opts.en: secretly (wrong meaning — contradicts an overt facial reaction)

items.why: 露骨にいやな顔をする (openly show displeasure on one's face) is the fixed collocation for an unmistakably visible reaction — ひそか means "secretly," the opposite of an open display.

items.q: 警察は詐欺師の（ ）手口を解明した。
items.qr: Keisatsu wa sagishi no (___) teguchi o kaimei shita.
items.en: The police uncovered the fraudster's vicious/crooked methods.
items.hi: पुलिस ने ठग के धोखेबाज़ तरीक़ों का पर्दाफ़ाश किया।
items.gu: પોલીસે ઠગના કપટી હથકંડા ખુલ્લા પાડ્યા.

opts.en: careless/rough manner (wrong nuance — about carelessness, not deliberate viciousness)
filthy/disgusting (wrong domain — about visceral disgust, not scheming methods)

items.why: あくどい手口 (a vicious/crooked scheme) is the standard phrase for describing a scammer's deliberately malicious methods; the other options describe carelessness, disgust, or anticlimax, none of which fit a fraud investigation.

items.q: （ ）の人が、彼の意見に賛成した。
items.qr: (___) no hito ga, kare no iken ni sansei shita.
items.en: Most people agreed with his opinion.
items.hi: अधिकतर लोग उसकी राय से सहमत थे।
items.gu: મોટા ભાગના લોકો તેના અભિપ્રાય સાથે સંમત હતા.

opts.en: rough/broad (describes manner, not a subgroup of people)

items.why: おおかたの人 (most people) uses おおかた as "the greater part of" a group; おおまか describes doing something in a rough/broad manner, not a portion of people.

items.q: 今回、価格を（ ）値下げしました。
items.qr: Konkai, kakaku o (___) nesage shimashita.
items.en: This time, we've cut prices substantially.
items.hi: इस बार हमने कीमतों में बड़ी कटौती की है।
items.gu: આ વખતે અમે ભાવમાં મોટો ઘટાડો કર્યો છે.

opts.en: extremely (wrong grammar — modifies adjectives, not a verb like 値下げする directly this way)

items.why: 大幅に値下げする (cut prices drastically) is the standard collocation for a big price change; 極めて typically modifies an adjective (極めて重要) rather than directly quantifying a price cut.

items.q: 消費税の値上げには（ ）反対します。
items.qr: Shouhizei no neage niwa (___) hantai shimasu.
items.en: I'm absolutely opposed to raising the consumption tax.
items.hi: मैं उपभोग कर बढ़ाने का पुरज़ोर विरोध करता हूँ।
items.gu: હું વપરાશ કર વધારવાનો સંપૂર્ણપણે વિરોધ કરું છું.

opts.en: extreme (describes a noun/opinion itself, not the strength of one's opposition)

items.why: 断然反対する (be resolutely/absolutely opposed) intensifies the verb 反対する itself; 極端 describes something as "extreme" (an extreme opinion), not the intensity of one's stance.

items.q: コンピューターはここ10年で（ ）進歩を遂げた。
items.qr: Konpyuutaa wa koko juunen de (___) shinpo o togeta.
items.en: Computers have made remarkable progress in the past 10 years.
items.hi: पिछले 10 सालों में कंप्यूटर ने उल्लेखनीय प्रगति की है।
items.gu: છેલ્લા 10 વર્ષમાં કમ્પ્યુટરે નોંધપાત્ર પ્રગતિ કરી છે.

opts.en: exaggerated (wrong meaning — implies false claims, not real progress)

items.why: 目覚ましい進歩 (remarkable progress) is the fixed collocation for genuinely impressive advancement; 大げさ describes something exaggerated/overstated, which would undercut the claim rather than praise it.

items.q: このあたりは（ ）ところにコンビニがあります。
items.qr: Kono atari wa (___) tokoro ni konbini ga arimasu.
items.en: There are convenience stores everywhere around here.
items.hi: यहाँ आस-पास हर जगह कन्वीनियंस स्टोर हैं।
items.gu: આ વિસ્તારમાં દરેક જગ્યાએ કન્વીનિયન્સ સ્ટોર છે.

opts.en: limitless (wrong grammar — describes an unbounded quantity/extent, not "every place")

items.why: いたるところ is a fixed phrase meaning "everywhere"; 限りない describes something without limit in extent/degree (endless prairie, boundless love), not distribution across every location.

items.q: 砂糖は（ ）多めに入れたほうがおいしいです。
items.qr: Satou wa (___) oome ni ireta hou ga oishii desu.
items.en: It tastes better if you put in slightly more sugar.
items.hi: चीनी थोड़ी ज़्यादा डालने से स्वाद बेहतर होता है।
items.gu: ખાંડ થોડી વધારે નાખવાથી સ્વાદ સારો આવે છે.

opts.en: faintly (wrong domain — for barely perceptible sounds/light, not quantities)

items.why: 若干多め (a bit more) is the natural way to quantify "slightly more" of an ingredient; かすか describes something barely perceptible to the senses (a faint sound/light), not a small extra amount.

items.q: 口げんかでは妻のほうが（ ）強い。
items.qr: Kuchigenka dewa tsuma no hou ga (___) tsuyoi.
items.en: In verbal arguments, my wife is overwhelmingly stronger.
items.hi: बहस में मेरी पत्नी कहीं ज़्यादा तेज़ है।
items.gu: બોલાચાલીમાં મારી પત્ની ઘણી વધારે તેજ છે.

opts.en: infinitely (too abstract/literal for a skill comparison)
perfectly (wrong nuance — about flawlessness, not a comparative gap)

items.why: 圧倒的に強い (overwhelmingly stronger) is the natural way to describe a lopsided comparison between two people; 無限 and 完ぺき describe absolute/abstract qualities, not a comparative edge.

items.q: （ ）場合でも相談に応じます。
items.qr: (___) baai demo soudan ni oujimasu.
items.en: We'll offer consultation whatever the case may be.
items.hi: चाहे जो भी मामला हो, हम सलाह देने के लिए तैयार हैं।
items.gu: ભલે ગમે તે કિસ્સો હોય, અમે સલાહ આપવા તૈયાર છીએ.

opts.en: every (place) — wrong grammar, only pairs with ところ
general (wrong grammar — doesn't combine with 場合でも this way)

items.why: いかなる〜でも ("whatever ___ it may be") is a fixed pattern for "in any case whatsoever" — いたる only ever pairs with ところ, and the other two options describe rough approximation, not "any kind of."

items.q: 一度払い込んだ入学金は、（ ）理由があっても返金しません。
items.qr: Ichido haraikonda nyuugakukin wa, (___) riyuu ga atte mo henkin shimasen.
items.en: Once paid, the entrance fee will not be refunded, whatever the reason.
items.hi: एक बार जमा की गई प्रवेश शुल्क राशि किसी भी कारण से वापस नहीं की जाएगी।
items.gu: એકવાર ભરેલી પ્રવેશ ફી કોઈપણ કારણસર પરત કરવામાં આવશે નહીં.
items.why: Day 6's いかなる〜でも ("whatever ___ it may be") is the fixed pattern for "no matter the reason" — none of the others combine with 理由 this way.

items.q: 母はいつも「お金がない、お金がない」と（ ）いる。
items.qr: Haha wa itsumo "Okane ga nai, okane ga nai" to (___) iru.
items.en: My mother always grumbles "no money, no money."
items.hi: मेरी माँ हमेशा "पैसे नहीं हैं, पैसे नहीं हैं" कहकर बड़बड़ाती रहती है।
items.gu: મારી મમ્મી હંમેશાં "પૈસા નથી, પૈસા નથી" કહીને બબડ્યા કરે છે.
items.why: Day 1's ぼやく (grumble) fits this casual, habitual complaint about money — the other three are unrelated verbs that only sound similar.

items.q: 彼女はいま、ロックに（ ）います。
items.qr: Kanojo wa ima, rokku ni (___) imasu.
items.en: She's really into rock music right now.
items.hi: वह इन दिनों रॉक संगीत में पूरी तरह डूबी हुई है।
items.gu: તે હાલમાં રોક સંગીતમાં સંપૂર્ણપણે ડૂબેલી છે.

opts.en: being fired up (wrong grammar with に)

items.why: Day 3's ロックにかぶれる is the word list's own example for being really into/influenced by a music genre.

items.q: 凶悪犯は（ ）逮捕されてしまった。
items.qr: Kyouakuhan wa (___) taiho sarete shimatta.
items.en: The vicious criminal was arrested with surprising ease.
items.hi: क्रूर अपराधी बड़ी आसानी से पकड़ा गया।
items.gu: ક્રૂર ગુનેગાર ખૂબ સહેલાઈથી પકડાઈ ગયો.

opts.en: curtly (wrong meaning — describes a manner of response, not an arrest's ease)

items.why: Day 5's あっけない describes something ending faster/more easily than expected — a dangerous criminal being caught without a struggle is exactly this "anticlimactic" nuance.

items.q: このアイスクリームはとても（ ）舌触りですね。
items.qr: Kono aisukuriimu wa totemo (___) shitazawari desu ne.
items.en: This ice cream has a very smooth texture, doesn't it.
items.hi: इस आइसक्रीम का टेक्सचर बहुत मुलायम है, है ना?
items.gu: આ આઇસક્રીમનું ટેક્સચર ખૂબ મુલાયમ છે, ખરું ને?
items.why: Day 4's 滑らか describes a smooth texture — exactly what "舌触り" (mouthfeel) calls for; the others describe color, scenery, and speed.

items.q: 母の愛情の（ ）手作りのマフラー。
items.qr: Haha no aijou no (___) tezukuri no mafuraa.
items.en: A handmade scarf filled with mother's love.
items.hi: माँ के स्नेह से भरा हाथ से बना मफ़लर।
items.gu: મમ્મીના સ્નેહથી ભરેલો હાથે બનાવેલો મફલર.
items.why: Day 1's こもる can mean a feeling is "packed into" something made with care — 愛情のこもった手作り (handmade, filled with love/affection) is a common set phrase.

items.q: 地震で倒れたビルの下から（ ）声が聞こえる。
items.qr: Jishin de taoreta biru no shita kara (___) koe ga kikoeru.
items.en: A faint voice can be heard from under the building that collapsed in the earthquake.
items.hi: भूकंप से गिरी इमारत के नीचे से एक धीमी आवाज़ सुनाई देती है।
items.gu: ભૂકંપથી પડી ગયેલી ઇમારત નીચેથી એક ઝાંખો અવાજ સંભળાય છે.
items.why: Day 6's かすか describes something barely perceptible to the senses, exactly fitting a faint voice heard from under rubble.

items.q: 津波はその地方に大きな被害を（ ）。
items.qr: Tsunami wa sono chihou ni ookina higai o (___).
items.en: The tsunami brought great damage to that region.
items.hi: सुनामी ने उस क्षेत्र में भारी नुक़सान पहुँचाया।
items.gu: સુનામીએ તે વિસ્તારમાં ભારે નુકસાન સર્જ્યું.
items.why: Day 3's 被害をもたらす (bring about damage) is the fixed collocation for a disaster causing harm.

items.q: 近所に雷が落ちて、（ ）音がした。
items.qr: Kinjo ni kaminari ga ochite, (___) oto ga shita.
items.en: Lightning struck nearby, making a tremendous sound.
items.hi: पास में बिजली गिरी और ज़बरदस्त आवाज़ हुई।
items.gu: નજીકમાં વીજળી પડી અને જબરદસ્ત અવાજ થયો.

opts.en: extreme (usu. negative traits, not a sound's intensity)
a great number of (wrong domain — for countable things, not sound intensity)

items.why: Day 6's ものすごい directly intensifies things like sounds/wind (ものすごい風); おびただしい quantifies countable nouns (an insect swarm), not a single sound's loudness.

items.q: 安かったから仕方がないかもしれないが、このソファーは作りがとても（ ）です。
items.qr: Yasukatta kara shikata ga nai kamoshirenai ga, kono sofaa wa tsukuri ga totemo (___) desu.
items.en: It might not be helped since it was cheap, but this sofa's construction is very sloppy.
items.hi: सस्ता था इसलिए शायद मजबूरी थी, पर इस सोफ़े की बनावट बहुत लापरवाही से की गई है।
items.gu: સસ્તું હતું એટલે કદાચ છૂટકો ન હતો, પણ આ સોફાની બનાવટ ખૂબ બેદરકારીથી કરેલી છે.

opts.en: blunt/overt (wrong domain — for attitudes, not craftsmanship)
cunning (wrong meaning — implies clever scheming, not shoddiness)

items.why: Day 5's 雑な仕事/作り describes sloppy, careless workmanship — exactly this cheap sofa's construction.

items.q: 気が抜けてぼんやりしている。 ("The tension has left, and one is left dazed/spaced-out.")
items.qr: Ki ga nukete bonyari shite iru.
items.why: Day 1's ぼうぜんとする describes a stunned, blank-minded daze — the closest match among the options to "spaced out with the tension gone."

items.q: 丸くてかわいらしい様子。 ("A round, cute-looking appearance.")
items.qr: Marukute kawairashii yousu.
items.why: Day 4's つぶらな瞳 (round, cute eyes) is a direct match for "round and cute-looking."

items.q: 複雑でわかりにくい様子。 ("Complicated and hard to understand.")
items.qr: Fukuzatsu de wakarinikui yousu.

opts.en: easily mistaken (close, but about ambiguity/mix-ups, not general complexity)

items.why: Day 5's ややこしい is defined by the book itself with the example 「ややこしい関係」(a complicated relationship) — a direct match; 紛らわしい is about being confused for something else, a narrower idea.

items.q: こわれやすい様子。 ("Easily broken.")
items.qr: Kowareyasui yousu.

opts.en: precarious (close, but about danger, not physical fragility)

items.why: Day 5's もろい is defined with もろく壊れやすい (fragile, easily broken) — an exact match, right down to sharing 壊れやすい in the book's own gloss.

items.q: 新鮮で生き生きしている様子。 ("Fresh and lively/vivid.")
items.qr: Shinsen de ikiiki shite iru yousu.
items.why: Day 4's みずみずしい describes fresh, vibrant things like vegetables — a direct match for "fresh and lively."

items.q: ジョギングをしたら、とても疲れた。
items.u: とても疲れた / totemo tsukareta
items.qr: Jogingu o shitara, totemo tsukareta.
items.en: After jogging, I got very tired.
items.why: Day 1's ばてる (become exhausted from exertion) is the closest match to being very tired after physical exercise like jogging.

items.q: 私はスポーツは何でも得意だが、水泳だけは田中さんに負ける。
items.qr: Watashi wa supootsu wa nan demo tokui da ga, suiei dake wa Tanaka-san ni makeru.
items.en: I'm good at every sport, but in swimming alone, I lose to Tanaka.

opts.en: dull/unimpressive (close in tone, but not "to lose to someone" specifically)

items.why: Day 1's 彼にはかなわない (to be no match for him) is the direct synonym of 負ける (to lose) when comparing skill against a specific person.

items.q: それはどこにでもいる平凡な虫です。
items.qr: Sore wa doko ni demo iru heibon na mushi desu.
items.en: That's a common, unremarkable insect found everywhere.
items.why: Day 3's word list defines ありふれた directly as (=平凡な) — the exact word underlined in this question.

items.q: 久しぶりに会った高校時代の同級生は、とても実際の年齢より上に見えた。
items.u: 実際の年齢より上に見えた / jissai no nenrei yori ue ni mieta
items.qr: Hisashiburi ni atta koukou jidai no doukyuusei wa, totemo jissai no nenrei yori ue ni mieta.
items.en: A high school classmate I met after a long time looked much older than their actual age.

opts.en: went bald (too specific, not the general idea)

items.why: Day 1's 老ける(ふける) is defined with the example 彼は年のわりには老けて見える — an exact match for "looked older than their actual age."

items.q: そのスケート選手は最初のジャンプを失敗してしまった。
items.u: 失敗してしまった / shippai shite shimatta
items.qr: Sono sukeeto senshu wa saisho no janpu o shippai shite shimatta.
items.en: That skater failed the first jump.
items.why: Day 1's しくじる (fail, blunder) is defined with the example 入試でしくじる — the direct synonym of 失敗する in this context.

items.q: かさばる
items.qr: kasabaru

opts.t: 今月は食事代がかさばってしまった。
opts.r: Kongetsu wa shokujidai ga kasabatte shimatta.
opts.en: This month's food costs "took up space" — wrong; cost increases use かさむ, not かさばる

opts.t: 雨が降ってきたのでかさばって歩いた。
opts.r: Ame ga futte kita node kasabatte aruita.
opts.en: Walked "bulkily" because it started raining — nonsensical

opts.t: 袋が大きく、かさばって持ちにくい。
opts.en: The bag is big, bulky, and hard to carry.

opts.t: 住宅がたくさんかさばっている。
opts.en: Houses are "bulking up" a lot — doesn't fit; houses aren't objects one carries

items.why: かさばる describes a physical object being awkwardly bulky to carry/store — sentence 3 matches Day 2's own word-list example almost verbatim; sentence 1 confuses it with かさむ (costs increasing), a classic same-root trap.

items.q: どもる
items.qr: domoru

opts.t: 社長との面談で、緊張のあまりどもってしまった。
opts.r: Shachou to no mendan de, kinchou no amari domotte shimatta.
opts.en: In the meeting with the president, I stammered out of nervousness.

opts.t: 家に明かりがどもっている。
opts.r: Ie ni akari ga domotte iru.
opts.en: Light in the house is "stammering" — wrong word, likely confusing with ともる (to be lit)

opts.t: 年をとって頭がだんだんどもってきた。
opts.r: Toshi o totte atama ga dandan domotte kita.
opts.en: As I aged, my head gradually "stammered" — wrong; should be ぼける

opts.t: 調子の悪かったパソコンがついにどもった。
opts.r: Choushi no warukatta pasokon ga tsuini domotta.
opts.en: The malfunctioning PC finally "stammered" — wrong; should be いかれる

items.why: どもる only describes a person stammering while speaking — sentence 1 matches Day 1's own example (スピーチでどもる); the others misapply it to lights, aging minds, and machines, each of which has its own correct verb (ともる, ぼける, いかれる).

items.q: そっけない
items.qr: sokkenai

opts.t: 家の裏でそっけない音がする。
opts.r: Ie no ura de sokkenai oto ga suru.
opts.en: A "curt" sound is heard behind the house — nonsensical, wrong domain

opts.t: その事件はそっけなく解決した。
opts.r: Sono jiken wa sokkenaku kaiketsu shita.
opts.en: The incident was resolved "curtly" — wrong; should be あっけなく

opts.t: 相当がんばってもそっけなく合格できないでしょう。
opts.r: Soutou ganbatte mo sokkenaku goukaku dekinai deshou.
opts.en: Even with great effort, you probably won't "curtly" pass — nonsensical combination

opts.t: 怒った妻は「勝手にすれば？」とそっけない返事をした。
opts.r: Okotta tsuma wa "Katte ni sureba?" to sokkenai henji o shita.
opts.en: The angry wife gave a curt reply, "Do whatever you want?"

items.why: 素っ気ない describes a cold, curt response or attitude toward a person — sentence 4 matches Day 5's own example (素っ気ない返事) exactly; sentences 2–3 confuse it with あっけない (anticlimactic/surprisingly easy), a sound-alike trap.

items.q: すたれる
items.qr: sutareru

opts.t: 長い間水をあげなかったから、植木がすたれてしまった。
opts.r: Nagai aida mizu o agenakatta kara, ueki ga sutarete shimatta.
opts.en: The plant "went out of fashion" from not being watered — wrong; should be 枯れる (wither)

opts.t: 彼の考え方はすたれていて、年寄りはもちろん若者にも理解できない。
opts.r: Kare no kangaekata wa sutarete ite, toshiyori wa mochiron wakamono ni mo rikai dekinai.
opts.en: His thinking is "outdated," not understood even by the young, let alone the old — logically backwards (old-fashioned ideas are typically the elderly's, not something young people alone would fail to get)

opts.t: あんなにはやったゲームだが、あっという間にすたれてしまった。
opts.r: Anna ni hayatta geemu da ga, atto iu ma ni sutarete shimatta.
opts.en: That game was so popular, but it went out of fashion in an instant.

opts.t: 「知らない」とすたれてもだめだよ。みんな知っているんだから。
opts.r: "Shiranai" to sutaretemo dame da yo. Minna shitte irun dakara.
opts.en: Saying "I don't know" and "going obsolete" doesn't work — wrong word entirely, likely confusing with とぼける

items.why: 廃れる describes something that was popular/prevalent falling out of use — sentence 3 mirrors Day 3's own example (流行が廃れる) precisely; sentence 2 misuses it with contradictory logic, and 1/4 confuse it with 枯れる and とぼける respectively.

items.q: ひさしい
items.qr: hisashii

opts.t: ひさしく素晴らしい映画を見た。
opts.en: Watched a "long-time" wonderful movie — wrong; should be 久々に (for the first time in a while)

opts.t: そういえば、ひさしくすきやきを食べていないなあ。
opts.r: Souieba, hisashiku sukiyaki o tabete inai naa.
opts.en: Come to think of it, I haven't had sukiyaki in a long time.

opts.t: 彼は自分の意見をひさしく述べた。
opts.r: Kare wa jibun no iken o hisashiku nobeta.
opts.en: He stated his opinion "for a long time" — wrong; should be 長々と (at length)

opts.t: ひさしくない関係の人には、メールアドレスを知らせていない。
opts.r: Hisashikunai kankei no hito niwa, meeru adoresu o shirasete inai.
opts.en: Haven't given my email to people who aren't "hisashii"-related — nonsensical, likely confusing with 親しい (close/intimate)

items.why: 久しい pairs with a negative verb to mean "it's been a long time since ___" — sentence 2 matches Day 5's own example (彼に久しく会っていない) exactly; the others misapply it where 久々に, 長々と, or 親しい would be the correct word instead.

items.q: 雨の日が続いて部屋が（a. ざあざあ b. じめじめ）している。
items.qr: Ame no hi ga tsuzuite heya ga (a. zaazaa / b. jimejime) shite iru.
items.en: With the rainy days continuing, the room is damp.
items.hi: बारिश के दिन लगातार होने से कमरा नम हो गया है।
items.gu: સતત વરસાદના દિવસોના કારણે રૂમ ભેજવાળો થઈ ગયો છે.

opts.en: pouring (rain itself, not a room's state)

items.why: じめじめ describes a damp, humid state (a room, weather, mood); ざあざあ describes the sound/intensity of rain falling, not the resulting dampness of a room.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · こつこつ努力しよう

items.q: 犬がえさを前にして、（a. ずるずる b. だらだら）よだれをたらしている。
items.qr: Inu ga esa o mae ni shite, (a. zuruzuru / b. daradara) yodare o tarashite iru.
items.en: With food in front of it, the dog is drooling profusely.
items.hi: खाना सामने देखकर कुत्ता लगातार लार टपका रहा है।
items.gu: ખોરાક સામે જોઈને કૂતરો સતત લાળ ટપકાવી રહ્યો છે.
items.why: だらだら is the word for liquid (sweat, drool) dripping continuously; ずるずる is for dragging a heavy object or a situation dragging on unresolved.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · こつこつ努力しよう

items.q: 運送料は業者によって（a. まちまち b. まるまる）です。
items.qr: Unsouryou wa gyousha ni yotte (a. machimachi / b. marumaru) desu.
items.en: Shipping fees vary depending on the carrier.
items.hi: ढुलाई शुल्क कंपनी के अनुसार अलग-अलग होता है।
items.gu: વહન ખર્ચ કંપની પ્રમાણે અલગ-અલગ હોય છે.
items.why: まちまち describes something that differs case by case (fees by carrier); まるまる describes something being a complete, whole unit (a whole baby, three whole days).
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · こつこつ努力しよう

items.q: 野原をちょうちょが（a. ぶかぶか b. ひらひら）飛んでいる。
items.qr: Nohara o choucho ga (a. bukabuka / b. hirahira) tonde iru.
items.en: A butterfly is fluttering through the field.
items.hi: मैदान में तितली फड़फड़ाते हुए उड़ रही है।
items.gu: મેદાનમાં પતંગિયું ફરફરતું ઊડી રહ્યું છે.
items.why: ひらひら describes something light fluttering through the air (a butterfly, a curtain); ぶかぶか describes clothing being too loose, an unrelated domain.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · こつこつ努力しよう

items.q: （a. ばらばら b. だらだら）のジグソーパズルを組み合わせて完成させた。
items.qr: (a. Barabara / b. Daradara) no jigusoo pazuru o kumiawasete kansei saseta.
items.en: I put together the scattered jigsaw puzzle pieces and completed it.
items.hi: बिखरे हुए जिगसॉ पज़ल के टुकड़ों को जोड़कर उसे पूरा किया।
items.gu: વિખરાયેલા જિગ્સો પઝલના ટુકડા જોડીને પૂરું કર્યું.
items.why: Puzzle pieces before assembly are ばらばら (scattered, in separate pieces) — だらだら has nothing to do with physical scattering.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · こつこつ努力しよう

items.q: （a. ずるずる b. すらすら）と日本語が読めるようになりたい。
items.qr: (a. Zuruzuru / b. Surasura) to nihongo ga yomeru you ni naritai.
items.en: I want to become able to read Japanese fluently.
items.hi: मैं जापानी भाषा को सहजता से पढ़ पाना चाहता हूँ।
items.gu: મારે જાપાનીઝ સહેલાઈથી વાંચતા આવડવું છે.
items.why: すらすら describes doing something (reading, solving) smoothly and without hesitation; ずるずる only fits dragging or a situation stalling.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · こつこつ努力しよう

items.q: 契約に失敗した。上司は（ ）怒るだろうなあ。
items.qr: Keiyaku ni shippai shita. Joushi wa (___) okoru darou naa.
items.en: I failed to close the deal. My boss is probably going to be furious.
items.hi: सौदा नहीं हो पाया। बॉस ज़रूर बहुत गुस्सा होंगे।
items.gu: સોદો નિષ્ફળ ગયો. બોસ ચોક્કસ ખૂબ ગુસ્સે થશે.

opts.en: (wrong — がんがん is for headaches/loud sound, not anger)

items.why: かんかんに怒る is the fixed collocation for being furious; がんがん sounds similar but describes a pounding headache or blaring noise, not anger.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · こつこつ努力しよう

items.q: 絶対に当選すると思っていたので、彼が落選したのは（ ）残念なことです。
items.qr: Zettai ni tousen suru to omotte ita node, kare ga rakusen shita no wa (___) zannen na koto desu.
items.en: Since I was sure he'd win, his losing the election is extremely disappointing.
items.hi: मुझे यक़ीन था कि वह ज़रूर जीतेंगे, इसलिए उनका चुनाव हारना बेहद अफ़सोस की बात है।
items.gu: મને ખાતરી હતી કે તે ચોક્કસ જીતશે, એટલે તેમનું ચૂંટણી હારવું ખૂબ જ દુઃખદ છે.

opts.en: severely (wrong register — describes an ordeal one goes through, not a fact being "extremely" regrettable)

items.why: 甚だ (hanahada) is a formal intensifier that pairs naturally with 残念 (regrettable); さんざん intensifies an experience someone directly suffers through (being scolded, a disaster), not an abstract judgment like "regrettable."
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · こつこつ努力しよう

items.q: 彼は住居を（a. 種々 b. 転々）とした。
items.qr: Kare wa juukyo o (a. shushu / b. tenten) to shita.
items.en: He moved from residence to residence.
items.hi: वह बार-बार अपना घर बदलता रहा।
items.gu: તે વારંવાર પોતાનું ઘર બદલતો રહ્યો.
items.why: 転々とする is the fixed pattern for repeatedly moving/changing location (homes, jobs); 種々 only describes variety among things, not movement.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 着々と進めよう

items.q: このラーメン屋には（a. ぼつぼつ b. ちょくちょく）きます。
items.qr: Kono raamen-ya ni wa (a. botsubotsu / b. chokuchoku) kimasu.
items.en: I come to this ramen shop every once in a while.
items.hi: मैं इस रामेन दुकान पर कभी-कभी आता हूँ।
items.gu: હું આ રામેન દુકાન પર ક્યારેક ક્યારેક આવું છું.
items.why: ちょくちょく describes a recurring habit (visiting occasionally); ぼつぼつ describes being on the verge of starting/leaving right now, an unrelated time sense.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 着々と進めよう

items.q: 済んだことをいつまでも（a. くよくよ b. ふらふら）しても仕方がない。
items.qr: Sunda koto o itsu made mo (a. kuyokuyo / b. furafura) shite mo shikata ga nai.
items.en: There's no use brooding forever over something that's already over.
items.hi: जो हो चुका है उस पर हमेशा परेशान होते रहने का कोई फ़ायदा नहीं।
items.gu: જે થઈ ગયું તેના વિશે કાયમ ચિંતા કરવાનો કોઈ ફાયદો નથી.
items.why: くよくよ describes mentally dwelling on and worrying about something past; ふらふら is a physical unsteadiness/dizziness, unrelated to worrying.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 着々と進めよう

items.q: 話題のゲームソフトを買おうと思って（a. 方々 b. 代わる代わる）探したが、どこも売り切れだった。
items.qr: Wadai no geemu sofuto o kaou to omotte (a. houbou / b. kawarugawaru) sagashita ga, doko mo urikire datta.
items.en: I wanted to buy the trending game, so I looked everywhere, but it was sold out everywhere.
items.hi: मशहूर गेम ख़रीदने के लिए मैंने हर जगह ढूँढा, पर हर जगह वह बिक चुका था।
items.gu: ચર્ચિત ગેમ ખરીદવા મેં દરેક જગ્યાએ શોધ્યું, પણ બધે જ વેચાઈ ગયેલી હતી.
items.why: 方々探す means searching in many different places; 代わる代わる describes multiple people taking turns doing something, not searching locations.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 着々と進めよう

items.q: このレポートは（a. ところどころ b. 点々）字の間違いはあるが、いい内容だ。
items.qr: Kono repooto wa (a. tokorodokoro / b. tenten) ji no machigai wa aru ga, ii naiyou da.
items.en: This report has typos here and there, but the content is good.
items.hi: इस रिपोर्ट में जगह-जगह वर्तनी की ग़लतियाँ हैं, पर सामग्री अच्छी है।
items.gu: આ રિપોર્ટમાં ઠેકઠેકાણે જોડણીની ભૂલો છે, પણ સામગ્રી સારી છે.

opts.en: dotted (wrong domain — physical drops/spots, not scattered errors in text)

items.why: ところどころ is the general word for "here and there" applying to abstract things like typos; 点々 specifically describes visible physical dots/drops (blood, spots), a narrower physical image.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 着々と進めよう

items.q: 彼女は文句を言いながらも（a. しぶしぶ b. つくづく）仕事を手伝ってくれた。
items.qr: Kanojo wa monku o iinagara mo (a. shibushibu / b. tsukuzuku) shigoto o tetsudatte kureta.
items.en: Complaining the whole time, she reluctantly helped with the work.
items.hi: शिकायत करते हुए भी उसने अनिच्छा से काम में मदद की।
items.gu: ફરિયાદ કરતાં કરતાં પણ તેણે અનિચ્છાએ કામમાં મદદ કરી.

opts.en: deeply, thoroughly (wrong meaning — an intensifier for feelings, not "unwillingly")

items.why: しぶしぶ describes doing something unwillingly while still doing it — matching "complaining but still helping"; つくづく intensifies an inner feeling (e.g. utter disappointment), not one's willingness to act.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 着々と進めよう

items.q: 今から駅に向かったら、10時の電車に（ ）間に合うでしょう。
items.qr: Ima kara eki ni mukattara, juuji no densha ni (___) ma ni au deshou.
items.en: If you head to the station now, you'll make the 10 o'clock train with plenty of time to spare.
items.hi: अगर अभी स्टेशन के लिए निकलें, तो 10 बजे की ट्रेन आराम से पकड़ लेंगे।
items.gu: જો હમણાં સ્ટેશન તરફ નીકળો, તો 10 વાગ્યાની ટ્રેન નિરાંતે પકડી શકશો.

opts.en: occasionally (wrong meaning — a frequency word, not about timing margin)

items.why: ゆうゆう間に合う is the book's own set phrase for making it with comfortable time to spare; the others don't describe timing margin at all.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 着々と進めよう

items.q: 彼は家を買う資金を（ ）貯めている。
items.qr: Kare wa ie o kau shikin o (___) tamete iru.
items.en: He is steadily saving up money to buy a house.
items.hi: वह घर ख़रीदने के लिए धीरे-धीरे पैसे जमा कर रहा है।
items.gu: તે ઘર ખરીદવા માટે ધીરે ધીરે પૈસા બચાવી રહ્યો છે.

opts.en: often (wrong meaning — frequency, not manner of saving)
going out of one's way (wrong meaning)

items.why: こつこつ貯める is the book's own headline example for steady, incremental saving; the others describe frequency or effort of a different kind, not the slow-and-steady manner of accumulating money.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 着々と進めよう

items.q: 「たばこ」という言葉は（a. きっぱり b. てっきり）日本語だと思っていたけど、違うんだね。
items.qr: "Tabako" to iu kotoba wa (a. kippari / b. tekkiri) nihongo da to omotte ita kedo, chigau n da ne.
items.en: I was absolutely certain the word "tabako" was Japanese, but it isn't, huh.
