items.hi: मुझे पक्का यक़ीन था कि "तबाको" शब्द जापानी है, पर ऐसा नहीं है।
items.gu: મને ચોક્કસ લાગતું હતું કે "તબાકો" શબ્દ જાપાનીઝ છે, પણ એવું નથી.

opts.en: flatly (wrong meaning — for refusing, not assuming)

items.why: てっきり describes a confident assumption that later turns out to be wrong — exactly this "I was sure it was Japanese, but..." pattern; きっぱり is only for firmly refusing/declaring something, unrelated to assuming.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · じっくり考えよう

items.q: 彼はそれが自分の犯行であることを（a. あっさり b. がっくり）認めた。
items.qr: Kare wa sore ga jibun no kouko de aru koto o (a. assari / b. gakkuri) mitometa.
items.en: He admitted it was his own crime, without any resistance.
items.hi: उसने बिना किसी विरोध के मान लिया कि यह उसका ही अपराध था।
items.gu: તેણે કોઈ પણ વિરોધ વગર સ્વીકારી લીધું કે તે તેનો જ ગુનો હતો.

opts.en: feel let down (wrong meaning — describes the emotional reaction to bad news, not the manner of confessing)

items.why: あっさり認める matches the book's own example あっさり負ける (lose easily/without a fight) — doing something readily, without putting up resistance; がっくり describes feeling crushed/dejected, not the act of admitting.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · じっくり考えよう

items.q: ライトアップで東京タワーが夜空に（a. くっきり b. きちっと）浮かび上がった。
items.qr: Raitoappu de Toukyou Tawaa ga yozora ni (a. kukkiri / b. kichitto) ukabiagatta.
items.en: Lit up, Tokyo Tower stood out clearly against the night sky.
items.hi: रोशनी से टोक्यो टावर रात के आसमान में साफ़-साफ़ उभर आया।
items.gu: લાઇટિંગથી ટોકિયો ટાવર રાત્રિના આકાશમાં સ્પષ્ટ રીતે ઉપસી આવ્યો.

opts.en: neatly (wrong domain — for tidiness, not visual clarity)

items.why: くっきり describes something being sharply, clearly visible against a backdrop (matching the book's own 富士山がくっきり見える example); きちっと is about neatness/order, not visibility.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · じっくり考えよう

items.q: 彼女は（a. さっと b. はっと）立ち上がって、座席を老人に譲った。
items.qr: Kanojo wa (a. satto / b. hatto) tachiagatte, zaseki o roujin ni yuzutta.
items.en: She quickly stood up and gave her seat to the elderly person.
items.hi: वह फुर्ती से खड़ी हुई और अपनी सीट बुज़ुर्ग को दे दी।
items.gu: તે ઝડપથી ઊભી થઈ અને પોતાની બેઠક વૃદ્ધને આપી દીધી.

opts.en: startled (wrong meaning — describes a reaction of surprise/realization, not the manner of standing up)

items.why: さっと describes performing a physical action quickly and smoothly; はっと describes a sudden internal jolt of surprise or realization, not a deliberate physical motion.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · じっくり考えよう

items.q: 新しい携帯電話の使い方が（a. うんざり b. さっぱり）わからない。
items.qr: Atarashii keitai denwa no tsukaikata ga (a. unzari / b. sappari) wakaranai.
items.en: I don't understand how to use the new phone at all.
items.hi: नए मोबाइल फ़ोन का इस्तेमाल करना मुझे बिल्कुल समझ नहीं आता।
items.gu: નવો મોબાઇલ ફોન કેવી રીતે વાપરવો તે મને બિલકુલ સમજાતું નથી.

opts.en: fed up (wrong meaning — an emotion of being tired of something, not "not at all")

items.why: さっぱり＋わからない is the fixed pattern for "don't understand at all," matching the book's own さっぱり思い出せない (can't remember a thing); うんざり expresses being sick and tired of something, a different feeling entirely.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · じっくり考えよう

items.q: 今日限りで（a. きっぱり b. きっかり）と酒をやめます。
items.qr: Kyou kagiri de (a. kippari / b. kikkari) to sake o yamemasu.
items.en: Starting today, I'm quitting alcohol completely and firmly.
items.hi: आज से मैं शराब पूरी तरह और दृढ़ता से छोड़ रहा हूँ।
items.gu: આજથી હું દારૂ સંપૂર્ણપણે અને દૃઢતાથી છોડી રહ્યો છું.

opts.en: exactly (wrong meaning — for precise time/amount, not resolve)

items.why: きっぱり(と)やめる is the set phrase for resolutely quitting something; きっかり only measures exact time or quantity (きっかり10時), not resolve.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · じっくり考えよう

items.q: 遊んだ後はおもちゃを（ ）片付けなさい。
items.qr: Asonda ato wa omocha o (___) katazukenasai.
items.en: Put your toys away neatly after you're done playing.
items.hi: खेलने के बाद खिलौनों को करीने से समेट दो।
items.gu: રમ્યા પછી રમકડાં વ્યવસ્થિત રીતે મૂકી દો.

opts.en: smoothly, easily (wrong domain — for a process going easily, not tidying)

items.why: きちっと(＝きちんと)片付ける is the natural collocation for tidying up neatly; the others don't describe orderliness.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · じっくり考えよう

items.q: 運動して汗を（ ）かいた。
items.qr: Undou shite ase o (___) kaita.
items.en: I exercised and worked up a drenching sweat.
items.hi: व्यायाम करके मैं पसीने से पूरी तरह भीग गया।
items.gu: કસરત કરીને હું પરસેવાથી સંપૂર્ણ ભીનો થઈ ગયો.

opts.en: gently moist (too mild a word for sweating from exercise)
tightly (wrong meaning — for gripping, not sweating)

items.why: 汗をびっしょりかく is the fixed collocation for sweating heavily/being drenched; しっとり is too gentle for exercise-induced sweat, and げっそり/ぎゅっと are unrelated meanings entirely.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · じっくり考えよう

items.q: 彼女はぐっすり寝ていて、（a. いっこうに b. とうてい）目を覚ます気配がない。
items.qr: Kanojo wa gussuri nete ite, (a. ikkou ni / b. toutei) me o samasu kehai ga nai.
items.en: She's sound asleep, showing no sign whatsoever of waking up.
items.hi: वह गहरी नींद में सोई है, जागने का कोई संकेत ही नहीं दिख रहा।
items.gu: તે ગાઢ ઊંઘમાં છે, જાગવાનો કોઈ સંકેત જ દેખાતો નથી.

opts.en: cannot possibly (wrong register — for flat impossibility of an action, not "no sign of")

items.why: 一向に…ない matches "not the slightest sign of" (一向に気配がない, echoing the book's own 一向に進まない); 到底…ない is for something being flatly impossible to achieve, a different shade of "not at all."
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · あらかじめ準備しておこう

items.q: 私は（a. いまに b. いまだに）カセットテープレコーダーを使っている。
items.qr: Watashi wa (a. ima ni / b. imada ni) kasetto teepu rekoodaa o tsukatte iru.
items.en: I'm still using a cassette tape recorder, even now.
items.hi: मैं आज भी कैसेट टेप रिकॉर्डर इस्तेमाल करता हूँ।
items.gu: હું આજે પણ કેસેટ ટેપ રેકોર્ડર વાપરું છું.

opts.en: someday (wrong tense — about the future, not an ongoing present habit)

items.why: いまだに describes something surprisingly still true/ongoing up to the present (still using an old cassette recorder); いまに points forward to a future outcome ("you'll regret it someday").
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · あらかじめ準備しておこう

items.q: 新タイプの機種ですが、値段は（a. さっぱり b. さほど）高くないですよ。
items.qr: Shin taipu no kishu desu ga, nedan wa (a. sappari / b. sahodo) takakunai desu yo.
items.en: It's a new-type model, but the price isn't all that high.
items.hi: यह नए मॉडल का है, पर क़ीमत इतनी ज़्यादा नहीं है।
items.gu: આ નવા મોડેલનું છે, પણ કિંમત એટલી બધી ઊંચી નથી.

opts.en: not at all (too strong — implies zero, not "not so much")

items.why: さほど…ない softens a negative to "not so much/not that" (a moderate degree), fitting a price that's merely not-too-high; さっぱり…ない is a total-absence intensifier ("not at all"), too strong here.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · あらかじめ準備しておこう

items.q: 最初は違和感があるけど、（a. 先に b. じきに）慣れるよ。
items.qr: Saisho wa iwakan ga aru kedo, (a. saki ni / b. jiki ni) nareru yo.
items.en: It feels off at first, but you'll get used to it soon.
items.hi: शुरू में अजीब लगेगा, पर जल्दी ही आदत हो जाएगी।
items.gu: શરૂઆતમાં અજુગતું લાગશે, પણ ટૂંક સમયમાં ટેવ પડી જશે.

opts.en: earlier/previously (wrong tense — refers back, not forward)

items.why: じきに points forward to something happening soon (getting used to it shortly); 先に points backward to something already mentioned/done earlier.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · あらかじめ準備しておこう

items.q: 妻は（a. 四六時中 b. 片時も）文句を言っている。
items.qr: Tsuma wa (a. shirokujichuu / b. katatoki mo) monku o itte iru.
items.en: My wife is complaining around the clock.
items.hi: मेरी पत्नी हर समय शिकायत करती रहती है।
items.gu: મારી પત્ની હંમેશા ફરિયાદ કરતી રહે છે.

opts.en: not even a moment (wrong — needs a following negative verb, but this sentence is affirmative)

items.why: 四六時中 pairs with an affirmative verb (言っている) to mean "constantly, all the time"; 片時も grammatically requires a negative verb afterward (片時も…ない), which this sentence doesn't have.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · あらかじめ準備しておこう

items.q: 後ろから（a. 時折 b. 不意に）呼びかけられて驚いた。
items.qr: Ushiro kara (a. tokiori / b. fui ni) yobikakerarete odoroita.
items.en: I was startled when someone unexpectedly called out to me from behind.
items.hi: पीछे से अचानक किसी ने पुकारा तो मैं चौंक गया।
items.gu: પાછળથી અચાનક કોઈએ બોલાવ્યું તો હું ચમકી ગયો.

opts.en: occasionally (wrong meaning — a frequency word, not "suddenly")

items.why: 不意に describes something happening without warning, causing surprise (matching 驚いた here); 時折 describes how often something recurs, unrelated to suddenness.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · あらかじめ準備しておこう

items.q: 最近の高校生は（ ）携帯電話を離さない。
items.qr: Saikin no koukousei wa (___) keitai denwa o hanasanai.
items.en: High schoolers these days won't put down their phones for even a moment.
items.hi: आजकल के हाई-स्कूल छात्र एक पल के लिए भी मोबाइल फ़ोन से दूर नहीं होते।
items.gu: આજકાલના હાઈસ્કૂલ વિદ્યાર્થીઓ એક ક્ષણ માટે પણ મોબાઇલ ફોનથી દૂર થતા નથી.

opts.en: all the time (doesn't fit the negative 離さない as tightly as 片時も)

opts.hi: एक पल के लिए भी नहीं

items.why: 片時も…ない is the fixed emphatic pattern for "not even a moment," which pairs precisely with 離さない (won't let go of); しょっちゅう describes frequency of repeated separate occasions, not continuous non-stop attachment.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · あらかじめ準備しておこう

items.q: 30年ぶりに母校を訪ねたら、（ ）校庭だったところに大きなマンションが建っていた。
items.qr: Sanjuu-nen buri ni bokou o tazunetara, (___) koutei datta tokoro ni ookina manshon ga tatte ita.
items.en: Visiting my old school for the first time in 30 years, a large apartment building now stood where the schoolyard used to be.
items.hi: 30 साल बाद अपने पुराने स्कूल गया तो जहाँ कभी खेल का मैदान हुआ करता था, वहाँ अब एक बड़ी इमारत बनी हुई थी।
items.gu: 30 વર્ષ પછી જૂની શાળાએ ગયો તો જ્યાં એક વખત રમતનું મેદાન હતું, ત્યાં હવે મોટી ઇમારત બની ગઈ હતી.

opts.en: someday (wrong tense — points to the future)
earlier (wrong — for referring back within the same speech, not to the distant past)
for some time now (wrong — implies a plan/knowledge held continuously, not a past state that has since changed)

items.why: かつて marks a state that was once true but no longer is (matching the book's own かつて住んでいた場所); かねて describes something known/planned continuously up to now, which doesn't fit a schoolyard that has since been replaced.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · あらかじめ準備しておこう

items.q: このカップ麺はあそこのラーメン屋より（a. よっぽど b. まして）おいしい。
items.qr: Kono kappumen wa asoko no raamen-ya yori (a. yoppodo / b. mashite) oishii.
items.en: This instant cup noodle is considerably tastier than that ramen shop.
items.hi: यह कप नूडल उस रामेन दुकान से कहीं ज़्यादा स्वादिष्ट है।
items.gu: આ કપ નૂડલ પેલી રામેન દુકાન કરતાં ઘણું વધારે સ્વાદિષ્ટ છે.

opts.en: let alone (wrong meaning — for adding a more extreme case, not comparing degree)

items.why: よっぽど intensifies a comparison (considerably more X than Y); まして is used to add "let alone [an even more extreme case]" to a preceding negative statement, a different sentence pattern entirely.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · ひたすら覚えよう

items.q: 彼は何も言わないが、（a. さも b. いたって）いやそうな顔をしている。
items.qr: Kare wa nani mo iwanai ga, (a. samo / b. itatte) iyasou na kao o shite iru.
items.en: He doesn't say anything, but his face clearly shows he doesn't like it.
items.hi: वह कुछ कहता नहीं, पर उसके चेहरे से साफ़ झलकता है कि उसे पसंद नहीं है।
items.gu: તે કંઈ કહેતો નથી, પણ તેના ચહેરા પર સ્પષ્ટ દેખાય છે કે તેને પસંદ નથી.

opts.en: extremely (wrong register — modifies a calm/neutral state, not an obvious visible expression)

items.why: さも describes an outward appearance that clearly, obviously conveys a feeling (matching the book's さもうれしそうに笑った); いたって is a mild-mannered intensifier for calm states like health, unrelated to visible expressions.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · ひたすら覚えよう

items.q: 虫に刺されたところをかいたら、（a. なおさら b. まさしく）かゆくなった。
items.qr: Mushi ni sasareta tokoro o kaitara, (a. naosara / b. masashiku) kayuku natta.
items.en: When I scratched the insect bite, it just got itchier.
items.hi: कीड़े के काटे हुए हिस्से को खुजलाने पर वह और भी ज़्यादा खुजली करने लगा।
items.gu: જંતુના ડંખવાળી જગ્યાએ ખંજવાળવાથી તે વધારે ખંજવાળવા લાગ્યું.

opts.en: definitely (wrong meaning — confirms a fact, doesn't intensify a resulting change)

items.why: なおさら matches the book's own pattern of "doing X makes it even more so" (だめだと言われるとなおさらやりたくなる); まさしく just confirms something is definitely true, without any "even more so" comparison.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · ひたすら覚えよう

items.q: あのおばあさんは、昔は（a. さぞかし b. なんと）美人だったことでしょう。
items.qr: Ano obaasan wa, mukashi wa (a. sazokashi / b. nanto) bijin datta koto deshou.
items.en: That old lady must surely have been a great beauty in her younger days.
items.hi: वह बुज़ुर्ग महिला अपने ज़माने में ज़रूर बहुत ख़ूबसूरत रही होंगी।
items.gu: તે વૃદ્ધ મહિલા પોતાના જમાનામાં ચોક્કસ ખૂબ સુંદર હશે.

opts.en: what a...! (wrong grammar — an exclamation about something known/seen directly, not a guess about the unseen past)

items.why: さぞかし expresses an empathetic guess about something you didn't witness yourself (matching ご両親はさぞお喜びでしょう); なんと is an exclamation of surprise about something directly observed, not a speculative guess with でしょう.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · ひたすら覚えよう

items.q: 今日、外は（a. まして b. やけに）寒いです。
items.qr: Kyou, soto wa (a. mashite / b. yake ni) samui desu.
items.en: It's unusually/awfully cold outside today.
items.hi: आज बाहर असामान्य रूप से ठंड है।
items.gu: આજે બહાર અસામાન્ય રીતે ઠંડી છે.

opts.en: let alone (wrong grammar — needs a preceding negative clause to contrast with)

items.why: やけに directly intensifies a simple standalone observation like today's cold weather; まして cannot stand alone — it needs an earlier negative clause to attach "let alone..." to.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · ひたすら覚えよう

items.q: 棚の角に（a. むろん b. もろに）頭をぶつけてしまった。
items.qr: Tana no kado ni (a. muron / b. moro ni) atama o butsukete shimatta.
items.en: I hit my head squarely on the corner of the shelf.
items.hi: मेरा सिर सीधे शेल्फ़ के कोने से टकरा गया।
items.gu: મારું માથું સીધું કબાટના ખૂણા સાથે અથડાયું.
items.why: もろに describes a direct, full-force impact or effect (matching もろに地震の被害を受けた); むろん means "of course," an unrelated word that only sounds slightly similar.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · ひたすら覚えよう

items.q: 試験問題はとても難しく、（ ）わからなかった。
items.qr: Shiken mondai wa totemo muzukashiku, (___) wakaranakatta.
items.en: The exam questions were so hard, I understood none of it at all.
items.hi: परीक्षा के सवाल इतने कठिन थे कि मुझे बिल्कुल कुछ समझ नहीं आया।
items.gu: પરીક્ષાના પ્રશ્નો એટલા અઘરા હતા કે મને બિલકુલ કંઈ સમજાયું નહીં.

opts.en: extremely (wrong — modifies calm states, not comprehension)
surely (wrong — a guess, not a statement of fact about yourself)
squarely (wrong meaning — for direct physical impact)

items.why: てんで requires and pairs naturally with a following negative to mean "not at all"; the other three don't fit the "total incomprehension" meaning here.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · ひたすら覚えよう

items.q: 年をとっても健康でいられるということは（ ）ですね。
items.qr: Toshi o totte mo kenkou de irareru to iu koto wa (___) desu ne.
items.en: Being able to stay healthy even as you age is the best thing there is, isn't it.
items.hi: उम्र बढ़ने पर भी स्वस्थ रह पाना सबसे बड़ी बात है, है ना।
items.gu: ઉંમર વધવા છતાં સ્વસ્થ રહી શકવું એ સૌથી મોટી વાત છે, ખરું ને.

opts.en: particularly (wrong — needs a group to single one item out of, not a standalone judgment)
more than anything, the best thing
single-mindedly (wrong meaning — describes an ongoing focused action, not a value judgment)

items.why: 何より is the set phrase for declaring something the best/most welcome thing of all (matching 合格して何よりうれしい); とりわけ needs a comparison group to pick "especially" from, which a standalone statement like this doesn't provide.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · ひたすら覚えよう

items.q: 夫婦円満だと思っていたのに、（a. どうにか b. どうやら）彼らは離婚したらしい。
items.qr: Fuufu enman da to omotte ita noni, (a. dounika / b. douyara) karera wa rikon shita rashii.
items.en: I thought they had a happy marriage, but it seems they've apparently divorced.
items.hi: मुझे लगता था कि उनकी शादी सुखी है, पर लगता है वे तलाक़ ले चुके हैं।
items.gu: મને લાગતું હતું કે તેમના લગ્નજીવન સુખી છે, પણ લાગે છે કે તેમણે છૂટાછેડા લીધા છે.

opts.en: somehow, manage to (wrong meaning — implies deliberate effort, not a hearsay observation)

items.why: どうやら…らしい is the pattern for reporting something you've inferred/heard secondhand; どうにか is about someone managing to achieve something through effort, which doesn't fit a passive observation about other people's lives.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · どうにか最後までやろう

items.q: （a. 仮に b. 現に）手術したとしても、彼は助からなかっただろう。
items.qr: (a. Kari ni / b. Gen ni) shujutsu shita to shite mo, kare wa tasukaranakatta darou.
items.en: Even hypothetically, even if he'd had surgery, he probably wouldn't have survived.
items.hi: मान लीजिए कि उसकी सर्जरी हो भी जाती, फिर भी शायद वह बच नहीं पाता।
items.gu: ધારો કે તેની સર્જરી થઈ પણ હોત, તોય કદાચ તે બચી ન શકત.

opts.en: actually, in fact (wrong meaning — states a real fact, contradicts a hypothetical としても clause)

items.why: 仮に…としても sets up a hypothetical scenario contrary to fact; 現に asserts something as real, directly-observed fact, which contradicts the very idea of a hypothetical.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · どうにか最後までやろう

items.q: あれ、おかしい。（a. ひょっとすると b. あえて）道を間違えたかもしれない。
items.qr: Are, okashii. (a. Hyotto suru to / b. Aete) michi o machigaeta kamoshirenai.
items.en: Huh, that's odd. We might possibly have taken the wrong road.
items.hi: अरे, यह अजीब है। हो सकता है हम रास्ता ग़लत आ गए हों।
items.gu: અરે, વિચિત્ર છે. કદાચ આપણે ખોટો રસ્તો લીધો હોય.

opts.en: dare to, deliberately (wrong meaning — for an intentional choice, not an uncertain guess)

items.why: ひょっとすると…かもしれない is the pattern for a speculative guess about an uncertain possibility (matching the book's own example); 敢えて describes doing something on purpose despite difficulty, unrelated to guessing.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · どうにか最後までやろう

items.q: チームは（a. なるたけ b. かろうじて）予選を勝ち抜いた。
items.qr: Chiimu wa (a. narutake / b. karoujite) yosen o kachinuita.
items.en: The team barely made it through the qualifying round.
items.hi: टीम बड़ी मुश्किल से क्वालिफ़ाइंग राउंड पार कर पाई।
items.gu: ટીમ માંડ માંડ ક્વોલિફાઇંગ રાઉન્ડ પાર કરી શકી.

opts.en: as much as possible (wrong meaning — modifies a request/desire, not a completed narrow-margin result)

items.why: かろうじて describes an outcome achieved with the narrowest possible margin (matching かろうじて最終電車に間に合った); なるたけ is about maximizing effort toward a future request, a different grammatical role.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · どうにか最後までやろう

items.q: お客様には（a. つとめて b. しいて）笑顔で接してください。
items.qr: Okyakusama ni wa (a. tsutomete / b. shiite) egao de sesshite kudasai.
items.en: Please make an effort to always deal with customers with a smile.
items.hi: कृपया ग्राहकों से हमेशा मुस्कुराकर पेश आने की पूरी कोशिश करें।
items.gu: કૃપા કરીને ગ્રાહકો સાથે હંમેશા સ્મિત સાથે વર્તવાનો પ્રયત્ન કરો.

opts.en: forcibly (wrong nuance — implies overriding resistance/reluctance, too strong for polite workplace advice)

items.why: 努めて笑顔で is the natural phrase for consciously making an effort to maintain a positive demeanor; 強いて implies forcing something despite reluctance/difficulty, an odd fit for routine customer-service advice.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · どうにか最後までやろう

items.q: 申し訳ありません。その本は（a. もしかして b. あいにく）在庫を切らしております。
items.qr: Moushiwake arimasen. Sono hon wa (a. moshika shite / b. ainiku) zaiko o kirashite orimasu.
items.en: I'm sorry. That book is unfortunately out of stock.
items.hi: माफ़ कीजिए। दुर्भाग्य से वह किताब स्टॉक में नहीं है।
items.gu: માફ કરશો. કમનસીબે તે પુસ્તક સ્ટોકમાં નથી.

opts.en: by any chance (wrong meaning — a question/guess word, not an apology intensifier)

items.why: あいにく is the standard polite way to soften bad news (matching あいにく留守にしています); もしかして is used when asking a speculative question, not delivering an apology.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · どうにか最後までやろう

items.q: これは、季節の野菜を（ ）使った料理です。
items.qr: Kore wa, kisetsu no yasai o (___) tsukatta ryouri desu.
items.en: This is a dish made with a generous amount of seasonal vegetables.
items.hi: यह मौसमी सब्ज़ियों का भरपूर इस्तेमाल करके बनाया गया व्यंजन है।
items.gu: આ મોસમી શાકભાજીનો પુષ્કળ ઉપયોગ કરીને બનાવેલી વાનગી છે.

opts.en: all, without exception (wrong nuance — about totality of a set, not abundance of quantity)

items.why: ふんだんに使う matches the book's own example (イチゴをふんだんに使ったケーキ) for using an abundant amount of an ingredient; the others don't describe quantity/abundance.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · どうにか最後までやろう

items.q: いくつも提案したが、私の案は（ ）受け入れられなかった。
items.qr: Ikutsu mo teian shita ga, watashi no an wa (___) ukeirerarenakatta.
items.en: I made several proposals, but every single one of my ideas was rejected.
items.hi: मैंने कई सुझाव दिए, पर मेरा एक भी सुझाव स्वीकार नहीं हुआ।
items.gu: મેં ઘણા સૂચનો આપ્યાં, પણ મારો એકેય વિચાર સ્વીકારાયો નહીં.
items.why: ことごとく matches the book's own example (私の案はことごとく却下された) for every single item in a set meeting the same fate; the others don't express "all of them, without exception."
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · どうにか最後までやろう

items.q: うそをついているのがばれるのではないかと、（ ）した。
items.qr: Uso o tsuite iru no ga bareru no de wa nai ka to, (___) shita.
items.en: I was on edge, worried that my lie might be found out.
items.hi: मुझे बेचैनी थी कि कहीं मेरा झूठ पकड़ा न जाए।
items.gu: મને ચિંતા હતી કે ક્યાંક મારું જૂઠ પકડાઈ ન જાય.

opts.en: on edge, nervously anticipating an uncertain outcome
timid in manner/presence (wrong nuance — about how one acts in front of others, not anticipatory anxiety)

items.why: Day 2's はらはらする describes the nervous, on-edge feeling of watching a risky/uncertain situation — exactly the anxiety of maybe being caught in a lie.

items.q: 父は（ ）医者に忠告されているにもかかわらず、酒をやめようとしない。
items.qr: Chichi wa (___) isha ni chuukoku sarete iru ni mo kakawarazu, sake o yameyou to shinai.
items.en: Even though the doctor has warned my father over and over, he won't quit drinking.
items.hi: डॉक्टर के बार-बार समझाने के बावजूद पिताजी शराब छोड़ने को तैयार नहीं हैं।
items.gu: ડૉક્ટરે વારંવાર ચેતવણી આપી હોવા છતાં પપ્પા દારૂ છોડવા તૈયાર નથી.

opts.en: not even a moment (wrong — needs a negative verb, but 忠告されている is affirmative)

items.why: Day 4's 再三 fits repeated warnings over time; the others don't describe repetition of an action.

items.q: 衝突事故を起こした車は（ ）つぶれていた。
items.qr: Shoutotsu jiko o okoshita kuruma wa (___) tsuburete ita.
items.en: The car involved in the collision was crushed into a mangled wreck.
items.hi: टक्कर में शामिल कार बुरी तरह चकनाचूर हो गई थी।
items.gu: અથડામણમાં સામેલ કાર સંપૂર્ણપણે ભાંગીને ભુક્કો થઈ ગઈ હતી.

opts.en: severely (wrong grammar — modifies an experience one undergoes, not the physical shape of an object)
extremely (wrong register — too formal/abstract for physical wreckage)
every once in a while (wrong meaning)

items.why: Day 1's ぐちゃぐちゃ describes something crushed into a disordered mess — exactly a wrecked car; the others don't fit physical destruction.

items.q: 荷物は（ ）そこに置いておいてください。
items.qr: Nimotsu wa (___) soko ni oite oite kudasai.
items.en: For now, please just leave the luggage there.
items.hi: फ़िलहाल सामान वहीं रख दीजिए।
items.gu: હાલ પૂરતું સામાન ત્યાં જ મૂકી દો.
items.why: Day 6's とりあえず is the fixed word for a provisional, for-now instruction; the others don't express temporariness.

items.q: 徹夜で作業して（ ）期限に間に合わせることができた。
items.qr: Tetsuya de sagyou shite (___) kigen ni ma ni awaseru koto ga dekita.
items.en: I worked through the night and just barely made the deadline.
items.hi: रात भर काम करके मैंने बड़ी मुश्किल से समय-सीमा पूरी की।
items.gu: આખી રાત કામ કરીને માંડ માંડ સમયમર્યાદા પૂરી કરી શક્યો.

opts.en: going out of one's way (wrong meaning)

items.why: Day 6's かろうじて describes an outcome achieved with the narrowest possible margin, matching "worked all night and just barely made it."

items.q: ブランド品と見れば何でも買う彼女には（ ）愛想が尽きた。
items.qr: Burando-hin to mireba nan demo kau kanojo ni wa (___) aiso ga tsukita.
items.en: I've thoroughly lost all patience with her buying anything as long as it's a brand-name item.
items.hi: ब्रांड का सामान देखते ही कुछ भी ख़रीद लेने वाली उससे अब पूरी तरह मन उचट गया है।
items.gu: બ્રાન્ડની વસ્તુ જોતાં જ ગમે તે ખરીદી લેતી તેનાથી હવે સંપૂર્ણપણે કંટાળી ગયો છું.

opts.en: irritated (close, but describes a flare of anger, not a settled, deep disillusionment)
single-mindedly (wrong meaning — describes focused action, not an emotional state)

items.why: Day 2's つくづく intensifies a deep, settled inner feeling (自分がつくづくいやになる) — fitting 愛想が尽きる (become thoroughly disillusioned/fed up), a slow-building realization rather than a sudden flare of anger.

items.q: 赤ちゃんの肌は（ ）している。
items.qr: Akachan no hada wa (___) shite iru.
items.en: A baby's skin is glossy/silky smooth.
items.hi: बच्चे की त्वचा चमकदार और मुलायम होती है।
items.gu: બાળકની ત્વચા ચમકદાર અને મુલાયમ હોય છે.

opts.en: plump (a real trait of babies, but describes body shape, not skin texture)
full of life/vigor (wrong domain — describes vitality, not skin texture)

items.why: Day 1's つやつや describes glossy, silky texture (skin/hair) directly; まるまる and ぴんぴん describe unrelated qualities (build, vitality) that a baby also happens to have, but don't answer "what is the skin like."

items.q: 注意しなくても（ ）間違いに気が付くだろう。
items.qr: Chuui shinakute mo (___) machigai ni ki ga tsuku darou.
items.en: Even without pointing it out, they'll naturally notice the mistake on their own.
items.hi: बताए बिना भी उसे अपनी ग़लती अपने आप पता चल जाएगी।
items.gu: કહ્યા વગર પણ તેને પોતાની ભૂલ પોતાની મેળે ખબર પડી જશે.

opts.en: as expected (wrong meaning — a comment on an outcome matching a prediction, not "by itself")
dare to (wrong meaning — implies deliberate effort, opposite of "without being told")

items.why: Day 6's 自ずと describes something happening on its own, without external intervention (努力すれば自ずから道は開ける) — matching noticing a mistake without being told.

items.q: そろそろ失礼します。（ ）とおじゃましました。
items.qr: Sorosoro shitsurei shimasu. (___) to ojama shimashita.
items.en: I should get going soon. I'm sorry to have stayed and imposed for so long.
items.hi: अब मुझे चलना चाहिए। इतनी देर तक बैठे रहने के लिए माफ़ी चाहता हूँ।
items.gu: હવે મારે નીકળવું જોઈએ. આટલો લાંબો સમય રોકાવા બદલ માફ કરશો.

opts.en: moving from place to place (wrong meaning)

items.why: Day 2's own example is nearly identical — 長々とおじゃましました, the set phrase for apologizing after a long visit.

items.q: 最近、昼食は（ ）隣のラーメン屋で済ませています。
items.qr: Saikin, chuushoku wa (___) tonari no raamen-ya de sumasete imasu.
items.en: Lately, I've been having lunch exclusively at the ramen shop next door.
items.hi: आजकल मैं दोपहर का खाना हमेशा बग़ल की रामेन दुकान पर ही खाता हूँ।
items.gu: આજકાલ હું બપોરનું ભોજન હંમેશા બાજુની રામેન દુકાનમાં જ કરું છું.

opts.en: single-mindedly (wrong nuance — for effort toward a goal, not a repeated habitual choice)

items.why: Day 5's もっぱら describes exclusively devoting a routine activity to one thing (休日はもっぱらゴルフをしている), matching always eating lunch at the same place.

items.q: あまるほどたくさんある様子。 ("A state of having so much of something that it's more than enough.")
items.qr: Amaru hodo takusan aru yousu.
items.why: Day 6's ふんだんに matches "so much it's more than enough" exactly (イチゴをふんだんに使ったケーキ).

items.q: 無理をしないで、確実に努力を続ける様子。 ("Continuing effort steadily and reliably, without overexerting.")
items.qr: Muri o shinaide, kakujitsu ni doryoku o tsuzukeru yousu.

opts.en: going out of one's way (wrong meaning)

items.why: Day 2's こつこつ is defined by the book's own example こつこつ貯金する — steady, incremental, sustainable effort.

items.q: 湿気が多くて気持ち悪いこと。 ("Humid and unpleasant.")
items.qr: Shikke ga ookute kimochi warui koto.

opts.en: drenched (close, but describes actual soaking wetness, not general humidity)
pleasantly moist/calm (wrong tone — positive, not unpleasant)

items.why: Day 1's じめじめ directly matches "humid and unpleasant" (梅雨で部屋がじめじめしている); しっとり describes a pleasant dampness/calmness, the opposite tone.

items.q: 明るく光り輝く様子。 ("Brightly shining and glittering.")
items.qr: Akaruku hikari kagayaku yousu.

opts.en: fluttering (wrong meaning — about motion, not light)

items.why: Day 1's こうこうと directly means shining brightly (ライトがこうこうとついている).

items.q: きわめて短い時間に。 ("In an extremely short span of time.")
items.qr: Kiwamete mijikai jikan ni.

opts.en: in the middle of (wrong meaning — a duration's midpoint, not a short instant)
unexpectedly (close, but about the lack of warning, not the shortness of time itself)

items.why: Day 4's とっさに directly means "in a split second" (とっさにブレーキを踏んだ); 不意に emphasizes surprise rather than duration.

items.q: 花は何でも好きですが、特にバラが好きです。
items.qr: Hana wa nan demo suki desu ga, tokuni bara ga suki desu.
items.en: I like all flowers, but I especially like roses.
items.why: Day 5's word list defines ことに directly as (＝特に、とりわけ) — the exact word underlined here.

items.q: あの先生の哲学の講義は私にはまったく理解できなかった。
items.qr: Ano sensei no tetsugaku no kougi wa watashi ni wa mattaku rikai dekinakatta.
items.en: I couldn't understand that professor's philosophy lecture at all.

opts.en: not that much (too mild — implies partial understanding, not zero)

items.why: Day 3's まるっきり(＝まるで) matches まったく's "completely/at all" force; さほど is a softer "not so much," too weak a match for total incomprehension.

items.q: 参加ご希望の方は、前もって申込書を提出しておいてください。
items.qr: Sanka gokibou no kata wa, maemotte moushikomisho o teishutsu shite oite kudasai.
items.en: Those who wish to participate, please submit the application form in advance.

opts.en: at this late stage (wrong meaning — opposite timing)

items.why: Day 4's word list explicitly glosses あらかじめ as (＝前もって) — the exact word underlined here.

items.q: 彼はたびたび遅刻します。
items.qr: Kare wa tabitabi chikoku shimasu.
items.en: He is often late.

opts.en: occasionally (too infrequent a match for たびたび)
not even a moment (wrong — needs a negative verb)

items.why: Day 4's しょっちゅう is the closest match to たびたび's "often, frequently" — both describe a high-frequency recurring habit; 時折 describes a much lower, occasional frequency.

items.q: 横柄な店員の態度に腹が立った。
items.u: 腹が立った / hara ga tatta
items.qr: Ouhei na ten'in no taido ni hara ga tatta.
items.en: I got angry at the arrogant clerk's attitude.
items.why: Day 2's own gloss for むかむかする includes (＝むかつく) "he annoys me/gets me angry" for someone's attitude — a direct match for 腹が立つ.

items.q: 到底
items.qr: toutei

opts.t: その計画は到底進展するでしょう。
opts.r: Sono keikaku wa toutei shinten suru deshou.
opts.en: "That plan will到底progress" — wrong; 到底 needs a negative, not an affirmative prediction

opts.t: そんな自分勝手な要求は、到底受け入れられません。
opts.r: Sonna jibun katte na youkyuu wa, toutei ukeiraremasen.
opts.en: Such a selfish demand cannot possibly be accepted.

opts.t: 今日は到底暑くないですね。
opts.r: Kyou wa toutei atsukunai desu ne.
opts.en: "It's到底not hot today" — wrong register; a mild "not very hot" needs さほど/それほど, not the extreme-impossibility word 到底

opts.t: タバコはここでは到底吸わないでください。
opts.r: Tabako wa koko de wa toutei suwanaide kudasai.
opts.en: "到底don't smoke here" — wrong; 到底 doesn't attach to a request/prohibition, only to statements of impossibility

items.why: 到底〜ない describes something being flatly, absolutely impossible to do or accept — sentence 2 matches Day 4's own examples (到底間に合わない, 到底無理だ) exactly; 1 wrongly pairs it with an affirmative, 3 confuses it with the much milder さほど, and 4 wrongly attaches it to a prohibition/request.

items.q: ぐっしょり
items.qr: gusshori

opts.t: 傘が無かったので、かばんの中までぐっしょりぬれてしまった。
opts.r: Kasa ga nakatta node, kaban no naka made gusshori nurete shimatta.
opts.en: Since I had no umbrella, even the inside of my bag got completely soaked.

opts.t: 川の水がぐっしょり流れている。
opts.r: Kawa no mizu ga gusshori nagarete iru.
opts.en: "The river water is flowingぐっしょり" — wrong; describes flowing motion, not a soaked state

opts.t: 今日は一日中雨がぐっしょり降っていた。
opts.r: Kyou wa ichinichijuu ame ga gusshori futte ita.
opts.en: "It rainedぐっしょりall day" — wrong; should be ざあざあ, describing the rain itself falling, not a soaked result

opts.t: 湿気が多くて部屋がぐっしょりしている。
opts.r: Shikke ga ookute heya ga gusshori shite iru.
opts.en: "The room isぐっしょりfrom humidity" — wrong; should be じめじめ, describing ambient dampness, not actual liquid soaking

items.why: ぐっしょり describes something already thoroughly soaked/drenched with liquid — sentence 1 matches Day 3's own example (汗でぐっしょりぬれる) exactly; 2–4 each confuse it with a different word for a related but distinct water-related state (flowing, falling, humid).

items.q: うんざり
items.qr: unzari

opts.t: その件に関してはうんざり考えてからお返事いたします。
opts.r: Sono ken ni kanshite wa unzari kangaete kara ohenji itashimasu.
opts.en: "I'll replyうんざりconsidering it" — wrong; should be じっくり (carefully), not "fed up"

opts.t: テレビは同じような番組ばかりでうんざりだ。
opts.r: Terebi wa onaji you na bangumi bakari de unzari da.
opts.en: I'm sick and tired of TV always having the same kind of programs.

opts.t: 彼女は風邪で熱があるのか、力なくうんざりと寝ていた。
opts.r: Kanojo wa kaze de netsu ga aru no ka, chikara naku unzari to nete ita.
opts.en: "She lay thereうんざり, weakly" — wrong; should be ぐったり (limply exhausted), not "fed up"

opts.t: あなたの言うことは、うんざりわかりません。
opts.r: Anata no iu koto wa, unzari wakarimasen.
opts.en: "I don'tうんざりunderstand you" — wrong; should be さっぱり (not at all), an intensifier, not an emotion word

items.why: うんざり describes being sick and tired of a recurring annoyance — sentence 2 matches Day 3's own example (その話はもううんざりだ) exactly; 1, 3, and 4 each substitute it for a different, unrelated word that happens to fit the same sentence slot.

items.q: ことごとく
items.qr: kotogotoku

opts.t: 新型ロケットの打ち上げはことごとく失敗してしまった。
opts.r: Shingata roketto no uchiage wa kotogotoku shippai shite shimatta.
opts.en: Every single launch of the new rocket model ended in failure.

opts.t: 私はお酒ではことごとくワインが好きです。
opts.r: Watashi wa osake de wa kotogotoku wain ga suki desu.
opts.en: "Among drinks Iことごとくlike wine" — wrong; should be とりわけ/もっぱら (particularly/exclusively), a preference word, not "all without exception"

opts.t: 駅までことごとく走り続けて、電車に間に合った。
opts.r: Eki made kotogotoku hashiritsuzukete, densha ni ma ni atta.
opts.en: "I kept runningことごとくto the station" — wrong; should be ひたすら (single-mindedly), describing manner of a continuous action, not totality of a set

opts.t: ことごとくできない問題を解いた。
opts.en: Nonsensical combination — should be something like かろうじて (barely) or やっと (finally), not "all without exception"

items.why: ことごとく describes every single item in a set meeting the same fate, without exception — sentence 1 mirrors Day 6's own example (私の案はことごとく却下された) precisely; 2–4 each misuse it in place of a preference, manner, or completion word.

items.q: とりわけ
items.qr: toriwake

opts.t: 料理の前にとりわけビールを2本お願いします。
opts.r: Ryouri no mae ni toriwake biiru o nihon onegai shimasu.
opts.en: "Before the food,とりわけtwo beers please" — wrong; should be とりあえず (for now), an unrelated word that merely sounds similar

opts.t: 休みの日はとりわけ家でごろごろしています。
opts.r: Yasumi no hi wa toriwake ie de gorogoro shite imasu.
opts.en: "On days off Iとりわけlaze around at home" — wrong; should be もっぱら (exclusively), describing an exclusive habit, not "especially"

opts.t: 遠いところをとりわけお越しいただきどうもありがとうございます。
opts.r: Tooi tokoro o toriwake okoshi itadaki doumo arigatou gozaimasu.
opts.en: "Thank you forとりわけcoming from so far" — wrong; should be わざわざ (going out of one's way), an unrelated word

opts.t: 私は甘いものの中でもとりわけショートケーキが好きです。
opts.r: Watashi wa amai mono no naka demo toriwake shootokeeki ga suki desu.
opts.en: Among sweets, I particularly like shortcake.

items.why: とりわけ singles one item out from an implied group — sentence 4 mirrors Day 5's own example (とりわけビールが好きだ) precisely, naming the group (甘いもの) explicitly; 1–3 each substitute it for とりあえず, もっぱら, and わざわざ, three unrelated words that happen to fit the same sentence slot.

items.q: だんだん年をとって、物事の良し悪しの（ ）がつくようになった。
items.qr: Dandan toshi o totte, monogoto no yoshi-ashi no (___) ga tsuku you ni natta.
items.en: As I've gotten older, I've come to be able to judge right from wrong.
items.hi: उम्र बढ़ने के साथ-साथ मुझमें सही-ग़लत परखने की समझ आ गई है।
items.gu: ઉંમર વધવાની સાથે મારામાં સાચા-ખોટાનો ભેદ પારખવાની સમજ આવી ગઈ છે.
items.why: 物事の良し悪しの分別 ("discretion about right and wrong") is the fixed collocation for good judgment; 分野 is a field of study/work, unrelated here.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 1 · 手分け・同い年・心地

items.q: 田中さんの意見に全員が（ ）した。
items.qr: Tanaka-san no iken ni zen'in ga (___) shita.
items.en: Everyone agreed with Tanaka's opinion.
items.hi: तनाका जी की राय से सभी सहमत हो गए।
items.gu: તનાકાના મંતવ્ય સાથે બધા સંમત થયા.

opts.en: same as above (wrong meaning — a citation phrase, not "agree")

items.why: 同意する means "to agree/consent" — the verb this sentence needs; 同上 only means "same as (what was written) above," used in documents, not for agreeing with a person.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 1 · 手分け・同い年・心地

items.q: 彼は平気な顔をしているが、（ ）は穏やかではない。
items.qr: Kare wa heiki na kao o shite iru ga, (___) wa odayaka de wa nai.
items.en: He looks unfazed, but inwardly he isn't calm.
items.hi: वह ऊपर से बेफ़िक्र दिखता है, पर मन ही मन शांत नहीं है।
items.gu: તે ઉપરથી બેફિકર દેખાય છે, પણ મનમાં શાંત નથી.
items.why: 内心 contrasts an outward appearance with an inner emotional state — exactly the が...but structure here; 心地 describes a sensory feeling like comfort, not a hidden emotion.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 1 · 手分け・同い年・心地

items.q: これはオークションで（ ）した中古の冷蔵庫です。
items.qr: Kore wa ookushon de (___) shita chuuko no reizouko desu.
items.en: This is a secondhand fridge I obtained at an auction.
items.hi: यह नीलामी में हासिल किया हुआ पुराना फ़्रिज है।
items.gu: આ હરાજીમાં મેળવેલું જૂનું ફ્રિજ છે.

opts.en: in one's grasp (doesn't take で於て object like this)

items.why: 入手する is the verb for actively acquiring an item (e.g. at an auction); 手中にする means "to have in one's grasp" and doesn't collocate with a place-marked acquisition like オークションで.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 1 · 手分け・同い年・心地

items.q: このパソコンは小さくて軽いので、（ ）に持ち運べる。
items.qr: Kono pasokon wa chiisakute karui node, (___) ni mochihakoberu.
items.en: This computer is small and light, so it can be carried around easily.
items.hi: यह लैपटॉप छोटा और हल्का है, इसलिए इसे आसानी से कहीं भी ले जाया जा सकता है।
items.gu: આ લેપટોપ નાનું અને હલકું છે, એટલે સહેલાઈથી ગમે ત્યાં લઈ જઈ શકાય છે.

opts.en: affordable/right-sized (describes price/size, not ease of an action)

items.why: 手軽に + verb describes doing an action easily/conveniently (here, carrying it); 手ごろ describes a price or size being "just right," not the ease of an action.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 1 · 手分け・同い年・心地

items.q: このメールの差出人には（ ）がありません。
items.qr: Kono meeru no sashidashinin ni wa (___) ga arimasen.
items.en: I have no idea who sent this email.
items.hi: मुझे नहीं पता कि यह ईमेल किसने भेजा है।
items.gu: મને ખબર નથી કે આ ઈમેલ કોણે મોકલ્યો છે.

opts.en: a physical clue/lead (wrong register — for detective work, not "I have no idea who")

items.why: 心当たりがない is the natural way to say "I have no idea/can't place who this is"; 手がかり is a tangible clue used in an investigation, a slightly different register.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 1 · 手分け・同い年・心地

items.q: 家族で（ ）して家中お掃除をした。
items.qr: Kazoku de (___) shite ie-juu osouji o shita.
items.en: The family split up the work and cleaned the whole house.
items.hi: परिवार ने काम बाँटकर पूरे घर की सफ़ाई की।
items.gu: પરિવારે કામ વહેંચીને આખા ઘરની સફાઈ કરી.
items.why: 手分けして + verb describes a group splitting up a task among themselves — exactly "the family split up (the cleaning)."
items.unit: Week 4 Day 1 · 手分け・同い年・心地

items.q: 給料をもらっても、支払いが多くて（ ）にはいくらも残らない。
items.qr: Kyuuryou o moratte mo, shiharai ga ookute (___) ni wa ikura mo nokoranai.
items.en: Even when I get paid, with so many expenses, hardly anything is left in hand.
items.hi: तनख़्वाह मिलने पर भी, ख़र्चे इतने ज़्यादा हैं कि हाथ में कुछ नहीं बचता।
items.gu: પગાર મળે તોય, ખર્ચા એટલા બધા છે કે હાથમાં ભાગ્યે જ કંઈ બચે છે.

opts.en: close at hand (an adjective, doesn't fit に残る)
in one's grasp (for things won/secured, not leftover cash)

items.why: 手元に残る is the set phrase for money that's "left in hand" after expenses; the other three don't collocate with money left over.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 1 · 手分け・同い年・心地

items.q: 彼は面倒なことはいつも（ ）にする。
items.qr: Kare wa mendou na koto wa itsumo (___) ni suru.
items.en: He always puts off troublesome things.
items.hi: वह हमेशा झंझट वाले कामों को टाल देता है।
items.gu: તે હંમેશા મુશ્કેલ કામોને મુલતવી રાખે છે.

opts.en: a detour (a route, not a way of handling tasks)

items.why: 後回しにする is the fixed phrase for postponing a task; 回り道 describes a physical detour on a route, unrelated to task priority.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 2 · 気長・下火・上の空

items.q: 彼の（ ）地は、青森です。
items.qr: Kare no (___) chi wa, Aomori desu.
items.en: His birthplace is Aomori.
items.hi: उसका जन्मस्थान आओमोरी है।
items.gu: તેનું જન્મસ્થળ આઓમોરી છે.

opts.en: giving birth (doesn't compound with 地 this way)

items.why: 出生地 ("place of birth") is the fixed compound; 出産 describes the act of giving birth and isn't used with 地 to mean "birthplace."
items.unit: Week 4 Day 2 · 気長・下火・上の空

items.q: ゲームに熱中していて、話しかけても（ ）だ。
items.qr: Geemu ni netchuu shite ite, hanashikakete mo (___) da.
items.en: He's absorbed in his game and spaced out even when spoken to.
items.hi: वह गेम में इतना डूबा है कि बुलाने पर भी उसका ध्यान नहीं जाता।
items.gu: તે ગેમમાં એટલો ડૂબેલો છે કે બોલાવવા છતાં તેનું ધ્યાન નથી જતું.

opts.en: a long way around (a route, unrelated to attention)

items.why: 上の空 describes being too absorbed elsewhere to pay attention — exactly "even when spoken to"; 遠回り is a route-related word, unrelated to attention.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 2 · 気長・下火・上の空

items.q: 火事が発生して、消防車が（ ）した。
items.qr: Kaji ga hassei shite, shoubousha ga (___) shita.
items.en: A fire broke out and the fire trucks were dispatched.
items.hi: आग लगने पर दमकल गाड़ियाँ मौक़े पर भेजी गईं।
items.gu: આગ લાગતાં ફાયર બ્રિગેડની ગાડીઓ ઘટનાસ્થળે મોકલવામાં આવી.

opts.en: to go to work (a daily commute, wrong register for an emergency)

items.why: 出動する is specifically for emergency services/troops being mobilized to a scene; 出勤する is the everyday word for commuting to work, wrong register here.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 2 · 気長・下火・上の空

items.q: しょうゆで（ ）をつけておいたので、焼くだけですぐ食べられます。
items.qr: Shouyu de (___) o tsukete oita node, yaku dake de sugu taberaremasu.
items.en: I marinated it in soy sauce beforehand, so it's ready to eat as soon as it's grilled.
items.hi: पहले से सोया सॉस में मैरिनेट कर रखा है, इसलिए ग्रिल करते ही खाया जा सकता है।
items.gu: પહેલેથી સોયા સોસમાં પલાળી રાખ્યું છે, એટલે શેકતાં જ ખાઈ શકાય.

opts.en: a base/primer (wrong domain — cosmetics/grounding, not food seasoning)

items.why: 下味をつける is the specific cooking term for seasoning food before cooking it; 下地 describes a foundational layer in other domains (makeup, skills), not food prep.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 2 · 気長・下火・上の空

items.q: （ ）のない公園で火事が起こった。
items.qr: (___) no nai kouen de kaji ga okotta.
items.en: A fire broke out in a park with no one around.
items.hi: जिस पार्क में कोई नहीं था, वहाँ आग लग गई।
items.gu: જ્યાં કોઈ નહોતું એવા પાર્કમાં આગ લાગી.
items.why: 人気のない (ひとけのない) means "with no sign of anyone around" — the reading trap is that this looks identical to 人気（にんき, "popularity"), but here it's the unrelated word ひとけ.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 2 · 気長・下火・上の空

items.q: 問い合わせに対する（ ）がやっと届いた。
items.qr: Toiawase ni taisuru (___) ga yatto todoita.
items.en: A reply to my inquiry finally arrived.
items.hi: आख़िरकार पूछताछ का जवाब आ गया।
items.gu: છેવટે પૂછપરછનો જવાબ આવી ગયો.
items.why: 回答 is the word for a reply to an inquiry/questionnaire — exactly what's "arrived" here; the others don't fit an inquiry's response.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 2 · 気長・下火・上の空

items.q: さあ、（ ）を入れてがんばろう！
items.qr: Saa, (___) o irete ganbarou!
items.en: Alright, let's psych ourselves up and do our best!
items.hi: चलो, जोश भरकर पूरी मेहनत करें!
items.gu: ચાલો, જુસ્સો ભરીને પૂરી મહેનત કરીએ!
items.why: 気合を入れる is the fixed idiom for psyching oneself up before an effort; the other 気-words don't combine with 入れる this way.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 2 · 気長・下火・上の空

items.q: 日本では少子高齢化が（ ）している。
items.qr: Nihon de wa shoushi-koureika ga (___) shite iru.
items.en: In Japan, the falling birthrate and aging population are progressing.
items.hi: जापान में घटती जन्म-दर और बढ़ती उम्रदराज़ आबादी की समस्या बढ़ती जा रही है।
items.gu: જાપાનમાં ઘટતો જન્મદર અને વધતી વૃદ્ધ વસ્તીની સમસ્યા આગળ વધી રહી છે.
items.why: 進行する describes an abstract trend/process advancing (like demographic change); 行進する is literal marching, e.g. in a parade.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 3 · 目下・大家・万人

items.q: （ ）の共通の願いは、健康であることだ。
items.qr: (___) no kyoutsuu no negai wa, kenkou de aru koto da.
items.en: The common wish of all people is to be healthy.
items.hi: सभी लोगों की एक साझा इच्छा होती है — स्वस्थ रहना।
items.gu: બધા લોકોની એક સામાન્ય ઈચ્છા હોય છે — તંદુરસ્ત રહેવું.

opts.en: a working adult (a narrower group, not "everyone")

items.why: 万人 means literally "all people," fitting a universal wish; 社会人 specifically means working adults, a narrower group than "everyone."
items.unit: Week 4 Day 3 · 目下・大家・万人

items.q: 政府が緊急（ ）を発表した。
items.qr: Seifu ga kinkyuu (___) o happyou shita.
items.en: The government issued an emergency statement.
items.hi: सरकार ने एक आपातकालीन बयान जारी किया।
items.gu: સરકારે એક કટોકટીનું નિવેદન બહાર પાડ્યું.

opts.en: market expansion (wrong meaning, doesn't collocate with 発表する this way)

items.why: 声明を発表する ("to issue a statement") is the fixed collocation; 進出 describes expanding into a market, unrelated to announcements.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 3 · 目下・大家・万人

items.q: 車の中だと（ ）を気にせず大声で歌を歌える。
items.qr: Kuruma no naka da to (___) o ki ni sezu oogoe de uta o utaeru.
items.en: In the car, you can sing loudly without worrying about others' eyes.
items.hi: गाड़ी के अंदर लोगों की नज़रों की परवाह किए बिना ज़ोर से गाना गा सकते हैं।
items.gu: ગાડીની અંદર લોકોની નજરની ચિંતા કર્યા વગર જોરથી ગીત ગાઈ શકાય છે.

opts.en: leniency (wrong meaning — doesn't pair with 気にする)

items.why: 人目を気にする is the set phrase for "worrying about others' eyes/what people think"; 大目 (leniency) doesn't fit this collocation at all.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 3 · 目下・大家・万人

items.q: その件に関して（ ）検討しているところです。
items.qr: Sono ken ni kanshite (___) kentou shite iru tokoro desu.
items.en: Regarding that matter, we are currently examining it.
items.hi: उस मामले पर हम फ़िलहाल विचार कर रहे हैं।
items.gu: એ બાબતે અમે હાલમાં વિચારણા કરી રહ્યા છીએ.

opts.en: the immediate/short-term (describes a scope, not "right now")

items.why: 目下 (もっか) is the adverb for "at present/currently," matching ところです ("in the process of"); 目先 describes short-term scope (like 目先の利益), not the timing of "now."
items.unit: Week 4 Day 3 · 目下・大家・万人

items.q: 私が（ ）に立って改革を成しとげるつもりです。
items.qr: Watashi ga (___) ni tatte kaikaku o nashitogeru tsumori desu.
items.en: I intend to stand at the front and see the reform through.
items.hi: मैं ख़ुद आगे बढ़कर सुधार को अंजाम तक पहुँचाना चाहता हूँ।
items.gu: હું જાતે આગળ રહીને સુધારાને પાર પાડવા માંગું છું.

opts.en: the other party (wrong meaning — refers to someone else, not oneself)

items.why: 先頭に立つ ("to stand at the front/take the lead") is the fixed phrase for leading an effort oneself; 先方 refers to the other party in a discussion, the opposite of "me."
items.unit: Week 4 Day 3 · 目下・大家・万人

items.q: 住宅ローンが我が家の（ ）を圧迫している。
items.qr: Juutaku roon ga wagaya no (___) o appaku shite iru.
items.en: The mortgage is straining our household finances.
items.hi: होम लोन ने हमारे घर के बजट पर दबाव डाल रखा है।
items.gu: હોમ લોનના કારણે અમારા ઘરના બજેટ પર દબાણ આવ્યું છે.
items.why: 家計を圧迫する ("to strain household finances") is the fixed collocation for a loan/expense burdening a family's budget; the others don't fit 圧迫する in this sense.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 3 · 目下・大家・万人

items.q: あの女優は実力より人気が（ ）しているね。
items.qr: Ano joyuu wa jitsuryoku yori ninki ga (___) shite iru ne.
items.en: That actress's popularity is ahead of her actual talent, isn't it.
items.hi: उस अभिनेत्री की लोकप्रियता उसकी असली काबिलियत से कहीं आगे निकल गई है, है ना।
items.gu: એ અભિનેત્રીની લોકપ્રિયતા તેની ખરી કાબેલિયત કરતાં આગળ નીકળી ગઈ છે, ખરું ને.

opts.en: arriving first (for a queue, wrong meaning)

items.why: 人気が実力に先行する describes one quality outpacing another — exactly "popularity ahead of talent"; the other three don't express that kind of comparison.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 3 · 目下・大家・万人

items.q: 嵐のため、電車のダイヤが（ ）乱れた。
items.qr: Arashi no tame, densha no daiya ga (___) midareta.
items.en: Because of the storm, train schedules were disrupted all day.
items.hi: तूफ़ान की वजह से ट्रेनों का समय पूरे दिन गड़बड़ रहा।
items.gu: તોફાનને કારણે ટ્રેનનું ટાઈમટેબલ આખો દિવસ ખોરવાયેલું રહ્યું.

opts.en: day by day (a recurring pattern, wrong for a single day's event)

items.why: 終日 describes something continuing for the entire length of one day — exactly a storm-caused disruption; 日々 describes a recurring daily pattern across many days, not one day's duration.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 4 · 意図・終日・小売り

items.q: これは、業者向けなので（ ）はしません。
items.qr: Kore wa, gyousha-muke na node (___) wa shimasen.
items.en: This is for wholesalers, so we don't sell it retail.
items.hi: यह थोक व्यापारियों के लिए है, इसलिए खुदरा नहीं बेचते।
items.gu: આ જથ્થાબંધ વેપારીઓ માટે છે, એટલે છૂટક વેચતા નથી.

opts.en: advance sale (wrong meaning — about timing, not sales channel)

items.why: 小売り contrasts with 業者向け (wholesale-facing) — the item is only sold wholesale, not retail; 前売り is about buying/selling ahead of an event, an unrelated axis.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 4 · 意図・終日・小売り

items.q: こうなったら（ ）でも完成させてみせよう。
items.qr: Kou nattara (___) de mo kansei sasete miseyou.
items.en: At this point, I'll finish it no matter what it takes.
items.hi: अब तो चाहे कुछ भी हो, मैं इसे पूरा करके दिखाऊँगा।
items.gu: હવે તો ગમે તે થાય, હું આ પૂરું કરીને જ બતાવીશ.

opts.en: intention (doesn't take でも in this idiom)

items.why: 意地でも～ is a fixed idiom meaning "out of sheer stubbornness/no matter what"; 意思 (a stated intention) doesn't appear in this construction.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 4 · 意図・終日・小売り

items.q: 仕事の（ ）にお気に入りのコーヒーショップに立ち寄った。
items.qr: Shigoto no (___) ni okiniiri no koohii shoppu ni tachiyotta.
items.en: During a break at work, I stopped by my favorite coffee shop.
items.hi: काम के बीच थोड़े वक़्त में मैं अपनी पसंदीदा कॉफ़ी शॉप गया।
items.gu: કામ વચ્ચેના સમયમાં હું મારી મનપસંદ કૉફી શોપ પર ગયો.

opts.en: physical space (wrong domain — not about time)

items.why: 仕事の合間に means "during a break between work tasks" (a time gap); 空間 describes physical space, not a gap in time.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 4 · 意図・終日・小売り

items.q: 大雪なので外出するのを（ ）。
items.qr: Ooyuki na node gaishutsu suru no o (___).
items.en: Because of the heavy snow, I decided to postpone going out.
items.hi: भारी बर्फ़बारी की वजह से बाहर जाना टाल दिया।
items.gu: ભારે બરફવર્ષાને કારણે બહાર જવાનું મુલતવી રાખ્યું.
items.why: 見合わせる means "to hold off on/postpone" a planned action; 見通す means "to foresee/see through," a completely different verb despite the shared 見.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 4 · 意図・終日・小売り

items.q: 彼はいまだに親から（ ）できていない。
items.qr: Kare wa imada ni oya kara (___) dekite inai.
items.en: He still hasn't managed to become independent from his parents.
items.hi: वह अब तक अपने माता-पिता से आत्मनिर्भर नहीं हो पाया है।
items.gu: તે હજુ સુધી પોતાના માતા-પિતાથી સ્વાવલંબી બની શક્યો નથી.

opts.en: own initiative (an adjective-like noun, doesn't take から...できる)

items.why: 親から自立する ("to become independent from one's parents") is the fixed collocation; 自主 describes acting on one's own initiative in a task, not achieving independence from a person.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 4 · 意図・終日・小売り

items.q: 湖で（ ）不明の生物が目撃された。
items.qr: Mizuumi de (___) fumei no seibutsu ga mokugeki sareta.
items.en: An unidentified creature was spotted at the lake.
items.hi: झील में एक ऐसा जीव देखा गया जिसकी पहचान नहीं हो सकी।
items.gu: તળાવમાં એક એવું જીવ જોવા મળ્યું જેની ઓળખ થઈ શકી નહીં.

opts.en: an object (too generic for a living creature)

items.why: 正体不明 ("identity unknown") is the fixed idiom for something/someone unidentified; the other three don't combine with 不明 this way.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 4 · 意図・終日・小売り

items.q: 警察はその事件の捜査に（ ）した。
items.qr: Keisatsu wa sono jiken no sousa ni (___) shita.
items.en: The police commenced the investigation into the case.
items.hi: पुलिस ने उस मामले की जाँच शुरू कर दी।
items.gu: પોલીસે એ કેસની તપાસ શરૂ કરી દીધી.
items.why: 捜査に着手する ("to commence an investigation") is the standard collocation; 着工 is reserved for construction breaking ground, a different domain entirely.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 4 · 意図・終日・小売り

items.q: 本日の講演の（ ）はエコロジーです。
items.qr: Honjitsu no kouen no (___) wa ekorojii desu.
items.en: Today's lecture topic is ecology.
items.hi: आज के व्याख्यान का विषय पारिस्थितिकी (इकोलॉजी) है।
items.gu: આજના પ્રવચનનો વિષય પર્યાવરણવિજ્ઞાન (ઇકોલોજી) છે.

opts.en: the main body/core (of a group, not a lecture's topic)

items.why: 主題 is the word for a lecture's/work's theme or subject; 主体 describes the main constituent group of something (like who makes up a workforce), not a topic.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 5 · 世代・本場・作用

items.q: その国は世界有数の石油（ ）国である。
items.qr: Sono kuni wa sekai yuusuu no sekiyu (___) koku de aru.
items.en: That country is one of the world's leading oil-producing nations.
items.hi: वह देश दुनिया के प्रमुख तेल-उत्पादक देशों में से एक है।
items.gu: એ દેશ દુનિયાના મુખ્ય તેલ-ઉત્પાદક દેશોમાંનો એક છે.

opts.en: ownership (doesn't compound with 国 this way)

items.why: 石油産出国 ("an oil-producing nation") is the fixed compound; 所有 describes owning something, not a country's natural output.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 5 · 世代・本場・作用

items.q: 父の（ ）で市役所に介護保険の申請に行った。
items.qr: Chichi no (___) de shiyakusho ni kaigo hoken no shinsei ni itta.
items.en: I went to city hall to apply for nursing-care insurance on my father's behalf.
items.hi: मैं अपने पिता की जगह नगरपालिका कार्यालय देखभाल बीमा के लिए आवेदन करने गया।
items.gu: હું મારા પિતાના વતી નગરપાલિકા ઓફિસ સંભાળ વીમા માટે અરજી કરવા ગયો.

opts.en: substituting an object for another (wrong domain — for things, not acting for a person)

items.why: 父の代理で ("on my father's behalf") is the phrase for representing a person; 代用 is for substituting one object for another, not standing in for a person.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 5 · 世代・本場・作用

items.q: 京都には伝統的な年中（ ）が多くあります。
items.qr: Kyouto ni wa dentouteki na nenjuu (___) ga ooku arimasu.
items.en: Kyoto has many traditional annual events.
items.hi: क्योतो में पारंपरिक वार्षिक आयोजन बहुत होते हैं।
items.gu: ક્યોટોમાં પરંપરાગત વાર્ષિક કાર્યક્રમો ઘણા છે.
items.why: 年中行事 ("annual events") is the fixed compound for recurring festivals/ceremonies; 人事 refers to personnel/HR matters, an unrelated domain.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 5 · 世代・本場・作用

items.q: 彼とは大学を卒業して以来、（ ）不通です。
items.qr: Kare to wa daigaku o sotsugyou shite irai, (___) futsuu desu.
items.en: I've been out of touch with him since we graduated from university.
items.hi: यूनिवर्सिटी से निकलने के बाद उससे मेरा कोई संपर्क नहीं रहा।
items.gu: યુનિવર્સિટીમાંથી નીકળ્યા પછી તેની સાથે મારો કોઈ સંપર્ક રહ્યો નથી.

opts.en: communication/telecommunications (wrong compound — 通信不通 isn't a phrase)

items.why: 音信不通 ("completely out of touch") is a fixed four-character idiom; 通信 means "communication" in general and doesn't combine with 不通 this way.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 5 · 世代・本場・作用

items.q: 会社の繁栄のために、（ ）交代は避けられないだろう。
items.qr: Kaisha no han'ei no tame ni, (___) koutai wa sakerarenai darou.
items.en: For the company's prosperity, generational change is probably unavoidable.
items.hi: कंपनी की तरक़्क़ी के लिए, पीढ़ी बदलाव शायद टाला नहीं जा सकता।
items.gu: કંપનીની સમૃદ્ધિ માટે, પેઢી પરિવર્તન કદાચ ટાળી ન શકાય.

opts.en: society/the world at large (doesn't pair with 交代)

items.why: 世代交代 ("generational handover") is the fixed compound for leadership passing to a younger generation; 世間 means "society/the public" and doesn't combine with 交代.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 5 · 世代・本場・作用

items.q: パイナップルはハワイの（ ）物です。
items.qr: Painappuru wa Hawai no (___) butsu desu.
items.en: Pineapple is a special product of Hawaii.
items.hi: अनानास हवाई का ख़ास उत्पाद है।
items.gu: અનેનાસ હવાઈનું ખાસ ઉત્પાદન છે.

opts.en: peculiar to (an adjective, doesn't take 物 this way)
producing/yielding (a verb, not a noun before 物 this way)
a characteristic (an abstract trait, not a physical product)

items.why: 特産物 is the fixed compound for "a region's special product," matching pineapple and Hawaii exactly.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 5 · 世代・本場・作用

items.q: 薬の（ ）で髪の毛が抜けてしまった。
items.qr: Kusuri no (___) de kami no ke ga nukete shimatta.
items.en: Due to the medicine's side effects, my hair fell out.
items.hi: दवा के साइड इफ़ेक्ट की वजह से मेरे बाल झड़ गए।
items.gu: દવાની આડઅસરના કારણે મારા વાળ ખરી ગયા.

opts.en: defective (for goods/behavior, not a medical cause)
a characteristic (unrelated to a medical cause)

items.why: 副作用 ("side effect") is the specific medical term for an unwanted effect of medicine, exactly matching hair loss from a drug.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 5 · 世代・本場・作用

items.q: 次期社長は田中専務だろうという意見が（ ）だ。
items.qr: Jiki shachou wa Tanaka senmu darou to iu iken ga (___) da.
items.en: The prevailing view is that Managing Director Tanaka will be the next president.
items.hi: ऐसी प्रबल राय है कि अगला अध्यक्ष तनाका होंगे।
items.gu: એવો પ્રબળ મત છે કે આગામી પ્રમુખ તનાકા હશે.

opts.en: net, actual (a quantity word, wrong domain)

items.why: 有力な意見 ("a prevailing/strong opinion") is the fixed collocation; 正味 describes a net quantity (like hours or weight), unrelated to how widely held an opinion is.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 6 · 新入り・本音・発足

items.q: 川の（ ）に沿って道路がある。
items.qr: Kawa no (___) ni sotte douro ga aru.
items.en: There's a road along the riverbank.
items.hi: नदी के किनारे के साथ-साथ एक सड़क है।
items.gu: નદીના કિનારે એક રસ્તો છે.

opts.en: a foundation (of a structure, not a riverside path)

items.why: 土手 specifically means the raised bank alongside a river; 土台 means the foundation of a building or an abstract basis, not a riverside feature.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 6 · 新入り・本音・発足

items.q: 酒の席でつい（ ）を打ち明けてしまった。
items.qr: Sake no seki de tsui (___) o uchiakete shimatta.
items.en: At the drinking party, I ended up revealing my true feelings.
items.hi: शराब की महफ़िल में मैं अपनी असली मंशा बता बैठा।
items.gu: દારૂની મહેફિલમાં હું મારી સાચી લાગણી કહી બેઠો.

opts.en: a tone/timbre (for sound, unrelated to feelings)

items.why: 本音を打ち明ける ("to reveal one's true feelings") is the fixed collocation; 音色 describes a sound's timbre, an unrelated meaning despite sharing 音.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 6 · 新入り・本音・発足

items.q: 今年度の（ ）予算は前年を上回った。
items.qr: Konnendo no (___) yosan wa zennen o uwamawatta.
items.en: This fiscal year's national budget exceeded last year's.
items.hi: इस वित्तीय वर्ष का राष्ट्रीय बजट पिछले साल से ज़्यादा रहा।
items.gu: આ નાણાકીય વર્ષનું રાષ્ટ્રીય બજેટ ગયા વર્ષ કરતાં વધારે રહ્યું.

opts.en: state-owned (describes ownership of property, not a budget)

items.why: 国家予算 ("national budget") is the fixed compound; 国有 describes something being state-owned property, not a government budget.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 6 · 新入り・本音・発足

items.q: 新しいプロジェクトを（ ）させた。
items.qr: Atarashii purojekuto o (___) saseta.
items.en: We launched a new project.
items.hi: हमने एक नई परियोजना शुरू की।
items.gu: અમે નવો પ્રોજેક્ટ શરૂ કર્યો.

opts.en: spontaneous (a manner adjective, doesn't take させる as "launch X")

items.why: プロジェクトを発足させる ("to launch a project") is the transitive causative use of 発足する; 自発 describes doing something of one's own accord, not the launching of an organization/project.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 6 · 新入り・本音・発足

items.q: ツアーは2週間で10ヵ所も回るという（ ）なスケジュールだった。
items.qr: Tsuaa wa nishuukan de jukkasho mo mawaru to iu (___) na sukejuuru datta.
items.en: The tour had a grueling schedule of visiting as many as 10 places in 2 weeks.
items.hi: उस टूर का शेड्यूल बेहद कठिन था — 2 हफ़्तों में 10 जगहें घूमनी थीं।
items.gu: એ ટૂરનું શેડ્યૂલ ખૂબ કપરું હતું — 2 અઠવાડિયામાં 10 જગ્યાએ ફરવાનું હતું.

opts.en: urgent (describes speed of response, not a punishing itinerary)

items.why: 強行なスケジュール describes a schedule pushed through despite being unreasonable/grueling; 早急 describes how quickly something must be done, not how punishing a plan is.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 6 · 新入り・本音・発足

items.q: その銀行は一時（ ）された。
items.qr: Sono ginkou wa ichiji (___) sareta.
items.en: The bank was temporarily nationalized.
items.hi: उस बैंक का अस्थायी रूप से राष्ट्रीयकरण किया गया।
items.gu: એ બેંકનું અસ્થાયી રીતે રાષ્ટ્રીયકરણ કરવામાં આવ્યું.
items.why: 国有化 ("nationalization," from 国有 "state-owned" + 化) is the standard economic term for a bank/company being taken over by the state; the other three combinations aren't real words.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 6 · 新入り・本音・発足

items.q: その家は崖が崩れて大量の（ ）に埋まった。
items.qr: Sono ie wa gake ga kuzurete tairyou no (___) ni umatta.
items.en: The house was buried under a huge amount of earth and sand when the cliff collapsed.
items.hi: पहाड़ी ढहने से वह घर बड़ी मात्रा में मिट्टी-रेत के नीचे दब गया।
items.gu: ટેકરી ધસી પડવાથી એ ઘર મોટા પ્રમાણમાં માટી-રેતી નીચે દટાઈ ગયું.

opts.en: a foundation (a structure part, not loose debris)
a riverbank (a fixed feature, not something one is buried under)

items.why: 土砂に埋まる ("to be buried under earth/sand") is the fixed phrase for landslide damage; the other three don't describe loose collapsed material.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 6 · 新入り・本音・発足

items.q: このバッグは財布を入れるのに（ ）な大きさだ。
items.qr: Kono baggu wa saifu o ireru no ni (___) na ookisa da.
items.en: This bag is just the right size for holding a wallet.
items.hi: यह बैग बटुआ रखने के लिए बिल्कुल सही आकार का है।
items.gu: આ બેગ પાકીટ રાખવા માટે એકદમ યોગ્ય કદની છે.

opts.en: a sign of human presence (wrong meaning)
close at hand (about proximity, not size)

items.why: Day 1's 手ごろ specifically describes a size or price being "just right" — exactly this bag's fit for a wallet.

items.q: その会社は、この春、海外に（ ）するらしい。
items.qr: Sono kaisha wa, kono haru, kaigai ni (___) suru rashii.
items.en: That company is apparently expanding overseas this spring.
items.hi: ऐसा लगता है कि वह कंपनी इस वसंत विदेशों में विस्तार करने वाली है।
items.gu: એવું લાગે છે કે એ કંપની આ વસંતમાં વિદેશમાં વિસ્તરવાની છે.

opts.en: preceding, being ahead (wrong meaning — doesn't fit 海外に)

items.why: Day 3's 海外に進出する is the fixed collocation for a company expanding into overseas markets.

items.q: 彼は（ ）があって、大金持ちの彼女にアプローチした。
items.qr: Kare wa (___) ga atte, oogane mochi no kanojo ni apuroochi shita.
items.en: He had an ulterior motive and approached the wealthy woman.
items.hi: उसके मन में कुछ और था, इसलिए वह उस अमीर महिला के पास गया।
items.gu: તેના મનમાં કંઈક છૂપો ઈરાદો હતો, એટલે તે એ પૈસાદાર સ્ત્રી પાસે ગયો.

opts.en: inwardly (an adverb, not a motive one "has")

items.why: Day 1's 下心がある exactly means "to have an ulterior/hidden motive" — matching approaching someone for a hidden reason (here, her wealth).

items.q: 警察は犯人逮捕の（ ）をつかんだようだ。
items.qr: Keisatsu wa hannin taiho no (___) o tsukanda you da.
items.en: The police seem to have grasped a clue toward the culprit's arrest.
items.hi: ऐसा लगता है कि पुलिस को अपराधी की गिरफ़्तारी का एक सुराग़ मिल गया है।
items.gu: એવું લાગે છે કે પોલીસને ગુનેગારની ધરપકડનો એક સુરાગ મળી ગયો છે.

opts.en: a guess/idea (a mental impression, not something physically "grasped")

items.why: Day 1's 手がかりをつかむ ("to grasp a clue/lead") is the standard idiom for investigative progress; 心当たり is a vaguer personal hunch, not literally "grasped."

items.q: 彼は、親に言われたのではなく、（ ）的に留学したいと言った。
items.qr: Kare wa, oya ni iwareta no de wa naku, (___)teki ni ryuugaku shitai to itta.
items.en: He said he wanted to study abroad on his own initiative, not because his parents told him to.
items.hi: उसने कहा कि वह माता-पिता के कहने पर नहीं, बल्कि अपनी मर्ज़ी से विदेश पढ़ाई करना चाहता है।
items.gu: તેણે કહ્યું કે તે માતા-પિતાના કહેવાથી નહીં, પણ પોતાની ઈચ્છાથી વિદેશમાં ભણવા માંગે છે.

opts.en: stubbornness (wrong meaning, and 意地的 isn't a standard form)
turning oneself in to police (unrelated meaning)

items.why: Day 6's 自発的に is the fixed adverbial form for "on one's own initiative," directly contrasting with being told to do something by someone else.

items.q: この病気（ ）の症状は、下痢と吐き気です。
items.qr: Kono byouki (___) no shoujou wa, geri to hakike desu.
items.en: The symptoms peculiar to this disease are diarrhea and nausea.
items.hi: इस बीमारी के ख़ास लक्षण हैं दस्त और जी मिचलाना।
items.gu: આ બીમારીના ખાસ લક્ષણો છે ઝાડા અને ઉબકા.

opts.en: a distinctive characteristic (for things/places, not medical symptoms)
an effect/reaction (a different grammatical slot — 副作用 would fit, not 作用 alone here)

items.why: Day 5's ～特有の症状 ("symptoms peculiar to ~") is the standard medical collocation; 特色 describes a place/thing's distinctive flavor, not a disease's symptoms.

items.q: 長野県の（ ）はりんごです。
items.qr: Nagano-ken no (___) wa ringo desu.
items.en: Nagano Prefecture's famous local product is apples.
items.hi: नागानो प्रान्त का प्रसिद्ध उत्पाद सेब है।
items.gu: નાગાનો પ્રાંતનું પ્રખ્યાત ઉત્પાદન સફરજન છે.

opts.en: a producing region (Nagano IS a producing region, but "Nagano's 産地 is apples" is backwards phrasing)
producing/yielding (a verb, doesn't fit の...は...です)
a staple food (apples aren't a staple food)

items.why: Day 5's ～の名産は…です ("~'s famous product is...") is the natural way to name a region's signature product; 産地 names the region itself as a producing area, the reverse direction of this sentence.

items.q: 今度の展覧会には、この絵を（ ）しよう。
items.qr: Kondo no tenrankai ni wa, kono e o (___) shiyou.
items.en: Let's submit this painting to the upcoming exhibition.
items.hi: आने वाली प्रदर्शनी में इस पेंटिंग को प्रस्तुत करते हैं।
items.gu: આવનારા પ્રદર્શનમાં આ ચિત્ર રજૂ કરીએ.

opts.en: supplies/goods (a noun, not a verb "to submit")

items.why: Day 2's 展覧会に出品する ("to submit works to an exhibition") is the exact fixed collocation for this sentence.

items.q: リストラされた彼は、今はコンビニのバイトで（ ）を立てている。
items.qr: Risutora sareta kare wa, ima wa konbini no baito de (___) o tatete iru.
items.en: Having been laid off, he now makes a living with a convenience-store part-time job.
items.hi: नौकरी से निकाले जाने के बाद, वह अब कन्वीनियंस स्टोर की पार्ट-टाइम नौकरी से गुज़ारा कर रहा है।
items.gu: નોકરીમાંથી કાઢી મુકાયા પછી, તે હવે કન્વીનિયન્સ સ્ટોરની પાર્ટ-ટાઈમ નોકરીથી ગુજરાન ચલાવે છે.

opts.en: manufacturing (wrong meaning — for goods, not a livelihood)

items.why: Day 5's 生計を立てる ("to make a living") is the fixed idiom for earning enough to live on; 自立 (independence) is a related idea but doesn't take 立てる as its verb.

items.q: この地方では、正月に川で泳ぐという（ ）がある。
items.qr: Kono chihou de wa, shougatsu ni kawa de oyogu to iu (___) ga aru.
items.en: In this region, there's a custom of swimming in the river on New Year's Day.
items.hi: इस इलाक़े में नए साल के दिन नदी में तैरने की एक परंपरा है।
items.gu: આ વિસ્તારમાં નવા વર્ષના દિવસે નદીમાં તરવાનો એક રિવાજ છે.

opts.en: a local specialty product (wrong meaning — for goods, not customs)

items.why: Day 6's 風習がある ("there is a custom of...") is the standard way to describe a region's traditional practice.

items.q: 事情を考えて、実行をやめて様子を見る。 ("Considering the circumstances, to stop carrying something out and watch how things develop.")
items.qr: Jijou o kangaete, jikkou o yamete yousu o miru.

opts.en: to look down on someone (wrong meaning)
to look down from a height (wrong meaning)

items.why: Day 4's 見合わせる (as in 出発を見合わせる) means exactly "to postpone a planned action after reconsidering circumstances."

items.q: どうしようもなくなること。 ("A state of no longer being able to do anything about a situation.")
items.qr: Dou shiyou mo naku naru koto.

opts.en: to go out of contact (wrong meaning)
to be at one's wit's end

items.why: Day 1's お手上げ literally describes throwing up one's hands because nothing more can be done — exactly this definition.

items.q: 公の機関に属さない人。 ("A person who doesn't belong to a public institution.")
items.qr: Ooyake no kikan ni zokusanai hito.

opts.en: not a standard word (国民 already means "citizen")

items.why: Day 6's 民間 ("private, non-governmental") + 人 gives 民間人, the standard word for someone outside government/public institutions; the other three options aren't real compounds.

items.q: 組織や団体などが設立されて活動を始めること。 ("An organization or group being established and beginning its activities.")
items.qr: Soshiki ya dantai nado ga setsuritsu sarete katsudou o hajimeru koto.

opts.en: spontaneous, of one's own accord (wrong meaning)

items.why: This is Day 6's own warm-up definition verbatim — 発足 is the word for an organization being established and beginning activities.

items.q: 恋人同士などが一緒に自殺すること。 ("Lovers, etc., committing suicide together.")
items.qr: Koibito doushi nado ga issho ni jisatsu suru koto.

opts.en: turning oneself in to police (wrong meaning)
in one's grasp (wrong meaning, and wrong reading trap for 心中)

items.why: Day 1's 心中（する）, read しんじゅう (not しんちゅう), means exactly "double suicide with a lover" — the reading trap this week's Day 1 flagged explicitly.

items.q: 彼は、ある現象に注意を向けて、新しい発見をした。
items.u: 注意を向けて / chuui o mukete
items.qr: Kare wa, aru genshou ni chuui o mukete, atarashii hakken o shita.
items.en: He directed his attention to a certain phenomenon and made a new discovery.

opts.en: commencing (wrong meaning — starting an action, not directing attention)

items.why: Day 4's 着目する means precisely "to focus/direct attention on" something, matching 注意を向ける exactly.

items.q: 留学の準備が整っている。
items.qr: Ryuugaku no junbi ga totonotte iru.
items.en: The preparations for studying abroad are in place.
items.why: This is Day 1's own warm-up sentence verbatim — 手はず is the word for "arrangements/preparations," the exact synonym of 準備 tested here.

items.q: 事故の影響でバスのダイヤは一日中乱れた。
items.qr: Jiko no eikyou de basu no daiya wa ichinichijuu midareta.
items.en: Because of the accident's effects, the bus schedule was disrupted all day long.

opts.en: day by day (a recurring pattern, wrong for one day's duration)
during the daytime (excludes night, not "all day")
day and night (describes an ongoing habitual state, not one day's disruption)

items.why: Day 4's 終日（＝一日中）is glossed by the book itself as equal to 一日中 — the exact underlined phrase here.

items.q: その場のもうけに目がくらんで株を売ってしまい、後でたいへん後悔した。
items.u: その場のもうけ / Sono ba no mouke
items.qr: Sono ba no mouke ni me ga kuramde kabu o utte shimai, ato de taihen koukai shita.
items.en: Blinded by the immediate profit at hand, I sold the stock and deeply regretted it afterward.

opts.en: the immediate/short-term (as in 目先の利益)
at present (an adverb of time, not "immediate profit")

items.why: Day 3's 目先の利益 ("immediate/short-term profit") is exactly "the profit right in front of one's eyes" — matching その場のもうけ.

items.q: 学問でもスポーツでも基礎が大事だ。
items.qr: Gakumon de mo supootsu de mo kiso ga daiji da.
items.en: Whether in academics or sports, the foundation is important.
items.why: Day 6's 土台 (literally "the foundation of a house") extends figuratively to mean "the basis/groundwork" of any skill — the exact sense of 基礎 here.

items.q: 下火
items.qr: shitabi

opts.t: 私は彼に好きだと言いたいが、下火がないのでなかなか言えない。
opts.r: Watashi wa kare ni suki da to iitai ga, shitabi ga nai node nakanaka ienai.
opts.en: "I want to tell him I like him, but I have no 下火, so I can't say it" — wrong; should be 勇気 (courage), an unrelated word

opts.t: 気持ちが下火になったので、落ち着いて試験を受けることができた。
opts.r: Kimochi ga shitabi ni natta node, ochitsuite shiken o ukeru koto ga dekita.
opts.en: "My feelings became 下火, so I could calmly take the exam" — wrong register; personal nervousness "settling down" needs 落ち着く, not 下火 (reserved for trends/epidemics/booms)

opts.t: 貯金の額が下火になったので、不安になってきた。
opts.r: Chokin no gaku ga shitabi ni natta node, fuan ni natte kita.
opts.en: "The savings amount became 下火, so I got anxious" — wrong; a shrinking balance needs 減る, not 下火

opts.t: ペットブームが最近下火になってきた。
opts.r: Petto buumu ga saikin shitabi ni natte kita.
opts.en: The pet-ownership boom has recently died down.

items.why: 下火になる describes a trend, fad, epidemic, or popularity dying down — sentence 4 matches Day 2's own example (インフルエンザの流行が下火になってきた) exactly; 1–3 each swap in an unrelated word that happens to fit the same sentence slot.

items.q: 台無し
items.qr: dainashi

opts.t: 味付けを間違えてしまい、せっかくのシチューが台無しになってしまった。
opts.r: Ajitsuke o machigaete shimai, sekkaku no shichuu ga dainashi ni natte shimatta.
opts.en: I got the seasoning wrong, and the stew I'd worked hard on was ruined.

opts.t: 先日買ったDVDプレーヤーは台無しの不良品だった。
opts.r: Senjitsu katta DVD pureeyaa wa dainashi no furyouhin datta.
opts.en: "The DVD player I bought was a 台無し defective item" — wrong; 台無し isn't used as an adjective describing a product's condition when bought, just 不良品 alone

opts.t: 俳優たちの演技のおかげで監督は台無しにならなかった。
opts.r: Haiyuu-tachi no engi no okage de kantoku wa dainashi ni naranakatta.
opts.en: "Thanks to the actors' performances, the director didn't become 台無し" — wrong; 台無し describes an effort/thing being ruined, not a person

opts.t: 一生懸命勉強した結果が台無しで困った。
opts.r: Isshoukenmei benkyou shita kekka ga dainashi de komatta.
opts.en: "The result of studying hard was 台無し and I was troubled" — awkward; the natural phrasing ruins the effort (苦労が台無しになった), not "the result" itself

items.why: 台無しになる describes an effort or thing being spoiled/ruined, typically by an external cause — sentence 1 mirrors Day 6's own example (雨で桜が台無しになる) exactly; 2–4 each misuse it as an adjective for a product, a person, or an abstract result.

items.q: 生かす
items.qr: ikasu

opts.t: 節約をするのは、生活を生かした方法だ。
opts.r: Setsuyaku o suru no wa, seikatsu o ikashita houhou da.
opts.en: "Saving money is a method that 生かした one's life" — wrong; not a natural collocation

opts.t: 自分の意見を生かしたので、みんなに嫌われてしまった。
opts.r: Jibun no iken o ikashita node, minna ni kirawarete shimatta.
opts.en: "Because I 生かした my own opinion, I was disliked" — wrong; pushing one's opinion needs 押し通す, not 生かす

opts.t: この経験を生かして、今後の仕事に役立ててください。
opts.r: Kono keiken o ikashite, kongo no shigoto ni yakudatete kudasai.
opts.en: Please make use of this experience and put it toward your future work.

opts.t: 事業を生かしたから、彼が首になるはずはない。
opts.r: Jigyou o ikashita kara, kare ga kubi ni naru hazu wa nai.
opts.en: "Because he 生かした the business, there's no way he'd be fired" — wrong; not a natural collocation

items.why: 生かす means "to make good use of" something valuable one already has (skill, experience) — sentence 3 mirrors Day 5's own example (経験を生かす) precisely; 1, 2, and 4 all force 生かす onto objects it doesn't naturally combine with.

items.q: 目方
items.qr: mekata

opts.t: 彼の目方が不明なので、連絡することはできない。
opts.r: Kare no mekata ga fumei na node, renraku suru koto wa dekinai.
opts.en: "His 目方 [weight] is unknown, so we can't contact him" — wrong; should be 行方 (whereabouts), an unrelated word

opts.t: 人気歌手が人の目方を避けて裏口から帰っていった。
opts.r: Ninki kashu ga hito no mekata o sakete uraguchi kara kaette itta.
opts.en: "The popular singer avoided people's 目方 [weight] and left by the back door" — wrong; should be 人目 (hitome, "the public eye"), this week's own Day 3 word

opts.t: 今後の政局がどうなるか、目方が付かない状況だ。
opts.r: Kongo no seikyoku ga dou naru ka, mekata ga tsukanai joukyou da.
opts.en: "It's a situation where 目方 [weight] can't be attached to how politics will go" — wrong; should be 見当がつかない ("no way to guess"), a fixed idiom unrelated to weight

opts.t: 容器は商品の目方に含まれていません。
opts.r: Youki wa shouhin no mekata ni fukumarete imasen.
opts.en: The container's weight is not included in the product's weight.

items.why: 目方 literally means "weight" — sentence 4 (net weight excluding packaging) is the only one using it in its real meaning; 1–3 each substitute it for an unrelated word (行方, 人目, 見当) that merely happens to fit the same sentence slot.

items.q: 小売り
items.qr: kouri

opts.t: これは原価は安いのに、小売り価格があまりに高い。
opts.r: Kore wa genka wa yasui noni, kouri kakaku ga amari ni takai.
opts.en: Even though the cost price is cheap, the retail price is far too high.

opts.t: コンサートの小売り券を購入した。
opts.r: Konsaato no kouriken o kounyuu shita.
opts.en: "I bought a 小売り ticket for the concert" — wrong; should be 前売り券 (advance ticket), this week's own Day 4 word

opts.t: 無理な小売りで、もうけがなくなった。
opts.r: Muri na kouri de, mouke ga nakunatta.
opts.en: "Due to unreasonable 小売り, profit disappeared" — wrong; should be 安売り (discount selling), an unrelated word

opts.t: 新築の小売り住宅を購入した。
opts.r: Shinchiku no kouri juutaku o kounyuu shita.
opts.en: "I bought a newly built 小売り house" — wrong; should be 建売り住宅 (a pre-built house for sale), an unrelated word

items.why: 小売り価格 ("retail price," contrasted with 原価/wholesale cost) is a completely standard compound, matching sentence 1 exactly; 2–4 each substitute a different, unrelated 売り-word that happens to fit the same sentence slot.

items.q: 彼は、（a. 前借り b. 前科）があるので、就職は難しいだろう。
items.qr: Kare wa, (a. maegari / b. zenka) ga aru node, shuushoku wa muzukashii darou.
items.en: Since he has a criminal record, finding a job will probably be difficult.
items.hi: उसका आपराधिक रिकॉर्ड होने की वजह से, नौकरी मिलना मुश्किल होगा।
items.gu: તેનો ગુનાહિત રેકોર્ડ હોવાથી, નોકરી મળવી મુશ્કેલ હશે.

opts.en: borrowing in advance (wrong meaning — not a job barrier by itself)

items.why: 前科 ("a criminal record") is the standard reason job-hunting would be difficult; 前借り is just borrowing against one's own salary, unrelated to employability.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 1 · 身近・日取り・前置き

items.q: （a. 正当 b. 根本的）な理由がなく、刃物を持ち歩くことは禁止されている。
items.qr: (a. Seitou / b. Konponteki) na riyuu ga naku, hamono o mochiaruku koto wa kinshi sarete iru.
items.en: Carrying a blade around without a legitimate reason is prohibited.
items.hi: बिना किसी उचित कारण के हथियार लेकर घूमना प्रतिबंधित है।
items.gu: યોગ્ય કારણ વગર હથિયાર લઈને ફરવું પ્રતિબંધિત છે.

opts.en: fundamental (doesn't collocate with 理由 in this legal sense)

items.why: 正当な理由 ("a legitimate/justifiable reason") is the fixed legal phrase for an exception to a rule; 根本的な理由 would describe a root cause, not legal justification.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 1 · 身近・日取り・前置き

items.q: 公園で（a. 身元 b. 生身）のわからない遺体が見つかった。
items.qr: Kouen de (a. mimoto / b. namami) no wakaranai itai ga mitsukatta.
items.en: A body whose identity is unknown was found in the park.
items.hi: पार्क में एक अज्ञात व्यक्ति का शव मिला।
items.gu: પાર્કમાં અજાણ્યા વ્યક્તિનો મૃતદેહ મળ્યો.

opts.en: a living body (wrong meaning — a body found dead is not 生身)

items.why: 身元不明 ("identity unknown") is the standard phrase for an unidentified body; 生身 describes a body that is alive/flesh-and-blood, the opposite context.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 1 · 身近・日取り・前置き

items.q: 大地震が来るというので、とりあえず（a. 身の回り b. 身の上）のものだけを持って避難所に行った。
items.qr: Oo-jishin ga kuru to iu node, toriaezu (a. mi no mawari / b. mi no ue) no mono dake o motte hinanjo ni itta.
items.en: Since word came that a big earthquake was coming, I took only my personal belongings and went to the shelter.
items.hi: बड़े भूकंप की ख़बर सुनकर, फ़िलहाल सिर्फ़ अपना ज़रूरी सामान लेकर शरण स्थल गया।
items.gu: મોટા ધરતીકંપની વાત સાંભળી, હાલ પૂરતો ફક્ત જરૂરી સામાન લઈને આશ્રયસ્થાને ગયો.

opts.en: one's personal circumstances/life story (wrong meaning — not physical items)

items.why: 身の回りのもの ("things around one's body," i.e. personal belongings) is what one physically carries; 身の上 refers to one's life circumstances/story, an abstract idea that can't be "carried."
items.unit: Week 5 Day 1 · 身近・日取り・前置き

items.q: 彼は（a. 表向き b. 前向き）は普通のサラリーマンだが、実は刑事です。
items.qr: Kare wa (a. omotemuki / b. maemuki) wa futsuu no sarariiman da ga, jitsu wa keiji desu.
items.en: Outwardly he's an ordinary office worker, but he's actually a detective.
items.hi: ऊपर से वह एक आम नौकरीपेशा है, पर असल में वह जासूस है।
items.gu: ઉપરથી તે સામાન્ય નોકરિયાત છે, પણ ખરેખર તે જાસૂસ છે.
items.why: 表向き contrasts an outward appearance with a hidden reality, exactly the が...実は structure here; 前向き describes a positive mental attitude, unrelated to concealment.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 1 · 身近・日取り・前置き

items.q: 古い車を（a. 手取り b. 下取り）に出して新車を買いました。
items.qr: Furui kuruma o (a. tedori / b. shitadori) ni dashite shinsha o kaimashita.
items.en: I traded in my old car and bought a new one.
items.hi: पुरानी कार बदलकर नई कार ख़रीदी।
items.gu: જૂની કાર બદલીને નવી કાર ખરીદી.

opts.en: take-home pay (wrong meaning — about salary, not trading a car)

items.why: 下取りに出す is the fixed phrase for trading in an old item toward a new purchase; 手取り only applies to salary after deductions.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 1 · 身近・日取り・前置き

items.q: 新人タレントを売り出すためには、いろいろな（ ）が必要だ。
