items.qr: Shinjin tarento o uridasu tame ni wa, iroiro na (___) ga hitsuyou da.
items.en: To launch a new talent's career, various behind-the-scenes groundwork is necessary.
items.hi: किसी नए कलाकार को लॉन्च करने के लिए, पर्दे के पीछे कई तरह की तैयारी ज़रूरी है।
items.gu: નવા કલાકારને લોન્ચ કરવા માટે, પડદા પાછળ અનેક પ્રકારની તૈયારી જરૂરી છે.
items.why: Launching a new celebrity involves a lot of quiet coordination and lobbying with media/industry contacts — exactly 根回し.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 1 · 身近・日取り・前置き

items.q: あなたの給料は、税金を差し引いて（ ）でこの金額になります。
items.qr: Anata no kyuuryou wa, zeikin o sashihiite (___) de kono kingaku ni narimasu.
items.en: After tax is deducted, your take-home salary comes to this amount.
items.hi: टैक्स काटने के बाद आपकी हाथ में आने वाली तनख़्वाह इतनी होगी।
items.gu: ટેક્સ કાપ્યા પછી તમારો હાથમાં આવતો પગાર આટલો થશે.
items.why: 手取り specifically names the salary amount left after tax/deductions — exactly what "this amount" refers to here.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 1 · 身近・日取り・前置き

items.q: 小さい輪がいくつも（a. 連ねた b. 連なった）ネックレス。
items.qr: Chiisai wa ga ikutsu mo (a. tsuraneta / b. tsuranatta) nekkuresu.
items.en: A necklace made of many small rings strung together in a row.
items.hi: कई छोटे छल्ले एक क़तार में जुड़े हुए हार।
items.gu: અનેક નાની કડીઓ હાર બંધ જોડાયેલો હાર.

opts.en: transitive form (needs an agent doing the stringing, wrong here)

items.why: The necklace itself is being described as a state (rings that "are lined up") — the intransitive 連なる fits a noun-modifying description; 連ねる is transitive and requires a subject actively doing the stringing.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 2 · 和む・指図・公

items.q: 犯人の（a. 予告 b. 口実）どおり、犯行が行われてしまった。
items.qr: Hannin no (a. yokoku / b. koujitsu) doori, hankou ga okonawarete shimatta.
items.en: Just as the culprit had forewarned, the crime was carried out.
items.hi: अपराधी की पूर्व चेतावनी के मुताबिक़, अपराध हो ही गया।
items.gu: ગુનેગારની અગાઉથી આપેલી ચેતવણી મુજબ, ગુનો થઈ જ ગયો.
items.why: 予告どおり ("just as forewarned") matches a criminal's advance warning being fulfilled; 口実 is an excuse for one's own behavior, not a warning about a future act.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 2 · 和む・指図・公

items.q: もらった報酬を全員で（a. 公平に b. 連帯で）分けた。
items.qr: Moratta houshuu o zen'in de (a. kouhei ni / b. rentai de) waketa.
items.en: Everyone divided the reward they received fairly amongst themselves.
items.hi: मिले हुए इनाम को सबने आपस में बराबर बाँट लिया।
items.gu: મળેલા ઈનામને બધાએ સરખા ભાગે વહેંચી લીધું.

opts.en: jointly (describes shared responsibility, not how a division is made)

items.why: 公平に分ける ("to divide fairly/equally") describes the manner of splitting something; 連帯 describes shared/joint liability, a different concept from splitting a reward evenly.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 2 · 和む・指図・公

items.q: その店員は（a. 誠実に b. 真実に）対応をしてくれた。
items.qr: Sono ten'in wa (a. seijitsu ni / b. shinjitsu ni) taiou o shite kureta.
items.en: That store clerk responded to me sincerely/honestly.
items.hi: उस दुकान के कर्मचारी ने ईमानदारी से मेरी मदद की।
items.gu: એ દુકાનના કર્મચારીએ પ્રામાણિકતાથી મદદ કરી.

opts.en: truthfully (真実 is a noun for "the truth," not naturally used as an adverb describing conduct)

items.why: 誠実 describes a person's sincere, honest manner of behaving toward others; 真実 refers to objective truth/facts, not a person's attitude.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 2 · 和む・指図・公

items.q: 彼は母親に万引きをしてしまったことを（a. 告白 b. 告知）した。
items.qr: Kare wa hahaoya ni manbiki o shite shimatta koto o (a. kokuhaku / b. kokuchi) shita.
items.en: He confessed to his mother that he had shoplifted.
items.hi: उसने अपनी माँ को क़बूल किया कि उसने दुकान से चोरी की थी।
items.gu: તેણે તેની માતાને કબૂલ કર્યું કે તેણે દુકાનમાંથી ચોરી કરી હતી.

opts.en: to notify (wrong direction — for delivering news to someone, not admitting one's own wrongdoing)

items.why: 告白する is for confessing one's own secret/wrongdoing (or feelings); 告知する is for a third party (e.g. a doctor) delivering news to someone else.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 2 · 和む・指図・公

items.q: 我々は、自然と（a. 温和 b. 調和）のとれた街作りを目指している。
items.qr: Wareware wa, shizen to (a. onwa / b. chouwa) no toreta machizukuri o mezashite iru.
items.en: We are aiming to build a town that is in harmony with nature.
items.hi: हम प्रकृति के साथ सामंजस्य रखने वाला शहर बनाना चाहते हैं।
items.gu: અમે પ્રકૃતિ સાથે સંવાદિતા ધરાવતું શહેર બનાવવા માંગીએ છીએ.

opts.en: mild/gentle (describes a climate or personality, not a relationship between two things)

items.why: 調和のとれた ("well-balanced/harmonious") describes a good relationship between two things (nature and city here); 温和 describes an inherent mild quality of a single thing, not a relationship.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 2 · 和む・指図・公

items.q: その女優が実は結婚しているということが、先日（ ）になった。
items.qr: Sono joyuu ga jitsu wa kekkon shite iru to iu koto ga, senjitsu (___) ni natta.
items.en: The fact that the actress is actually married became public knowledge the other day.
items.hi: वह अभिनेत्री असल में शादीशुदा है, यह बात हाल ही में सबको पता चल गई।
items.gu: એ અભિનેત્રી ખરેખર પરિણીત છે એ વાત તાજેતરમાં જાહેર થઈ ગઈ.

opts.en: a confession (wrong meaning — this is news becoming known, not her confessing)

items.why: 公になる ("to become public/known") is the exact fixed phrase for private information becoming widely known.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 2 · 和む・指図・公

items.q: 彼は、ガンで入院中に書いた（ ）をまとめて出版した。
items.qr: Kare wa, gan de nyuuinchuu ni kaita (___) o matomete shuppan shita.
items.en: He compiled the notes he wrote while hospitalized with cancer and published them.
items.hi: उसने कैंसर के इलाज के दौरान अस्पताल में लिखे अपने संस्मरण संकलित करके प्रकाशित किए।
items.gu: તેણે કેન્સરની સારવાર દરમિયાન હોસ્પિટલમાં લખેલા સંસ્મરણો ભેગા કરીને પ્રકાશિત કર્યા.

opts.en: a biography (usu. written by someone else about a person, not one's own hospital notes)

items.why: 手記 is exactly a personal written account/memoir of one's own experiences — matching notes he wrote himself during hospitalization; 伝記 is a biography usually written by someone else about a (often famous) person's whole life.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 2 · 和む・指図・公

items.q: 会議で新しい製品の必要性を（a. つかえた b. といた）。
items.qr: Kaigi de atarashii seihin no hitsuyousei o (a. tsukaeta / b. toita).
items.en: At the meeting, he explained persuasively why the new product is necessary.
items.hi: बैठक में उसने नए उत्पाद की ज़रूरत के बारे में समझाकर बताया।
items.gu: મીટિંગમાં તેણે નવા ઉત્પાદનની જરૂરિયાત વિશે સમજાવીને કહ્યું.

opts.en: served (wrong meaning — for serving a lord/God)

items.why: 説く means "to explain persuasively/preach a point" — exactly presenting a case for something's necessity at a meeting; 仕える only means "to serve" a person or deity.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 3 · 砂利・間柄・説得

items.q: これは本物を忠実に（a. 出現 b. 再現）した模型です。
items.qr: Kore wa honmono o chuujitsu ni (a. shutsugen / b. saigen) shita mokei desu.
items.en: This is a model that faithfully recreates the real thing.
items.hi: यह एक ऐसा मॉडल है जो असली चीज़ को हूबहू फिर से पेश करता है।
items.gu: આ એક એવું મોડેલ છે જે અસલી વસ્તુને હૂબહૂ ફરીથી રજૂ કરે છે.

opts.en: appearing (wrong meaning — something appearing for the first time, not recreating an existing thing)

items.why: 再現する ("to recreate/reproduce") fits a model faithfully reproducing a real object; 出現する describes something new appearing/emerging, not a faithful copy.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 3 · 砂利・間柄・説得

items.q: 親に（a. 言い訳 b. 説得）されて進学をあきらめた。
items.qr: Oya ni (a. iiwake / b. settoku) sarete shingaku o akirameta.
items.en: Persuaded by my parents, I gave up going on to higher education.
items.hi: माता-पिता के समझाने पर मैंने आगे पढ़ाई करने का इरादा छोड़ दिया।
items.gu: માતા-પિતાએ સમજાવ્યા પછી મેં આગળ ભણવાનો વિચાર છોડી દીધો.

opts.en: an excuse (wrong meaning — doesn't take a passive form describing being acted on by parents this way)

items.why: 説得される ("to be persuaded [by someone]") is the passive form fitting "convinced by my parents to give something up"; 言い訳 is an excuse one makes oneself, not something done to someone else.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 3 · 砂利・間柄・説得

items.q: 魚市場で新鮮な魚介類を（a. 仕入れた b. 仕上げた）。
items.qr: Uoichiba de shinsen na gyokairui o (a. shiireta / b. shiageta).
items.en: I stocked up on fresh seafood at the fish market.
items.hi: मछली बाज़ार से ताज़ा समुद्री भोजन ख़रीदा।
items.gu: માછલી બજારમાંથી તાજું સીફૂડ ખરીદ્યું.

opts.en: finished/completed (wrong meaning — for completing a piece of work, not buying stock)

items.why: 仕入れる means "to purchase goods (for resale/business use)" — exactly buying seafood at a market; 仕上げる means "to finish/complete" a piece of work, unrelated to purchasing.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 3 · 砂利・間柄・説得

items.q: 彼はまじめで（a. 間柄 b. 人柄）の良い人物です。
items.qr: Kare wa majime de (a. aidagara / b. hitogara) no yoi jinbutsu desu.
items.en: He is a serious person with a good character.
items.hi: वह गंभीर स्वभाव और अच्छे व्यक्तित्व वाला इंसान है।
items.gu: તે ગંભીર સ્વભાવ અને સારા વ્યક્તિત્વ ધરાવતો માણસ છે.

opts.en: a relationship (wrong meaning — between two people, not a single person's own trait)

items.why: 人柄 describes an individual's own personal character; 間柄 always describes the relationship between two or more people, which doesn't fit a single person being described here.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 3 · 砂利・間柄・説得

items.q: 定期預金に少しだけ（a. 利子 b. 有益）がついた。
items.qr: Teiki yokin ni sukoshi dake (a. rishi / b. yuueki) ga tsuita.
items.en: A little interest was added to my time deposit.
items.hi: सावधि जमा पर थोड़ा ब्याज जुड़ा।
items.gu: ટાઈમ ડિપોઝિટ પર થોડું વ્યાજ ઉમેરાયું.

opts.en: beneficial (wrong meaning — an adjective for usefulness, not a noun for interest earned)

items.why: 利子がつく ("interest is added") is the fixed phrase for a bank deposit accruing interest; 有益 only means "beneficial/useful" as a quality, not a sum of money.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 3 · 砂利・間柄・説得

items.q: 彼は失敗するといつも見苦しい（ ）ばかりする。
items.qr: Kare wa shippai suru to itsumo migurushii (___) bakari suru.
items.en: Whenever he fails, he always makes nothing but unseemly excuses.
items.hi: जब भी वह असफल होता है, हमेशा बेतुके बहाने बनाता है।
items.gu: જ્યારે પણ તે નિષ્ફળ જાય છે, હંમેશા બેહૂદા બહાનાં બનાવે છે.
items.why: 見苦しい言い訳をする ("to make unseemly excuses") is the natural collocation for someone who habitually excuses their own failures.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 3 · 砂利・間柄・説得

items.q: 最近は、情報という文字を（ ）学部が多い。
items.qr: Saikin wa, jouhou to iu moji o (___) gakubu ga ooi.
items.en: These days, many university faculties have the word "information" in their name.
items.hi: आजकल कई फ़ैकल्टी के नाम में "सूचना" शब्द शामिल होता है।
items.gu: આજકાલ ઘણી ફેકલ્ટીના નામમાં "માહિતી" શબ્દ સામેલ હોય છે.
items.why: 有する is the formal verb for "to have/hold" a characteristic, exactly describing faculties that "have" the word 情報 in their official name.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 3 · 砂利・間柄・説得

items.q: 彼女は歌手を（a. 志して b. 試して）上京した。
items.qr: Kanojo wa kashu o (a. kokorozashite / b. tameshite) joukyou shita.
items.en: She came to Tokyo aspiring to become a singer.
items.hi: वह गायिका बनने का सपना लेकर तोक्यो आई।
items.gu: તે ગાયિકા બનવાનું સપનું લઈને ટોક્યો આવી.

opts.en: trying out (wrong meaning — for testing a thing, not pursuing a career goal)

items.why: 志す is specifically about aspiring toward a long-term goal/career; 試す means to try something out to see the result, a different sense entirely.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 4 · 試す・営む・損なう

items.q: 年を取っても、彼の腕は（a. 鈍って b. 乱して）いない。
items.qr: Toshi o totte mo, kare no ude wa (a. nibutte / b. midashite) inai.
items.en: Even as he's aged, his skill hasn't dulled.
items.hi: उम्र बढ़ने के बावजूद, उसका हुनर कम नहीं हुआ है।
items.gu: ઉંમર વધવા છતાં, તેની આવડત ઓછી થઈ નથી.

opts.en: disturbed/disordered (wrong meaning and wrong transitivity — needs a direct object, not a skill "going bad" on its own)

items.why: 腕が鈍る ("one's skill dulls") is the fixed phrase for a talent deteriorating with disuse or age; 乱す is transitive and means to actively throw something into disorder, not to lose one's own ability.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 4 · 試す・営む・損なう

items.q: 健康を（a. 損なわない b. 病まない）ように注意してください。
items.qr: Kenkou o (a. sokonawanai / b. yamanai) you ni chuui shite kudasai.
items.en: Please be careful not to harm your health.
items.hi: कृपया अपनी सेहत को नुक़सान न पहुँचाने का ध्यान रखें।
items.gu: કૃપા કરીને તમારી તબિયતને નુકસાન ન થાય તેનું ધ્યાન રાખો.

opts.en: not fall ill (wrong grammar here — 健康を病む isn't natural; 病む takes the illness itself as object, e.g. 肺を病む)

items.why: 健康を損なう ("to damage/harm one's health") is the standard collocation for advice about avoiding harm to health; 病む pairs with a specific illness or organ (肺を病む), not the abstract word 健康 itself.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 4 · 試す・営む・損なう

items.q: この失敗については、彼が全責任を（a. 保つ b. 負う）そうだ。
items.qr: Kono shippai ni tsuite wa, kare ga zensekinin o (a. tamotsu / b. ou) sou da.
items.en: I hear he's going to bear full responsibility for this failure.
items.hi: सुना है इस असफलता की पूरी ज़िम्मेदारी वह ख़ुद लेगा।
items.gu: સાંભળ્યું છે કે આ નિષ્ફળતાની બધી જવાબદારી તે પોતે લેશે.

opts.en: to keep/maintain (wrong meaning — doesn't collocate with 責任)

items.why: 責任を負う ("to bear responsibility") is the fixed collocation; 保つ is used for maintaining a state (cleanliness, a position), not for taking on a duty.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 4 · 試す・営む・損なう

items.q: 我が社の製品はすべて安全基準を（a. 果たして b. 満たして）います。
items.qr: Waga sha no seihin wa subete anzen kijun o (a. hatashite / b. mitashite) imasu.
items.en: All of our company's products meet the safety standards.
items.hi: हमारी कंपनी के सभी उत्पाद सुरक्षा मानकों पर खरे उतरते हैं।
items.gu: અમારી કંપનીના તમામ ઉત્પાદનો સલામતી ધોરણોને પૂર્ણ કરે છે.

opts.en: achieving (a purpose/duty — wrong meaning for meeting a standard)

items.why: 基準を満たす ("to meet/satisfy a standard") is the standard collocation; 果たす is for achieving a goal or fulfilling a duty/role, not "meeting" a numeric or regulatory standard.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 4 · 試す・営む・損なう

items.q: この子には芸術の才能が（a. 備わっている b. 恵んでいる）。
items.qr: Kono ko ni wa geijutsu no sainou ga (a. sonawatte iru / b. megunde iru).
items.en: This child is naturally endowed with artistic talent.
items.hi: इस बच्चे में कला की प्रतिभा जन्मजात है।
items.gu: આ બાળકમાં કલાની પ્રતિભા જન્મજાત છે.

opts.en: is bestowing (wrong subject/voice — 恵む is a transitive act of giving charity, this sentence needs a state of possessing a quality)

items.why: 才能が備わっている ("talent is inherently present in someone") describes a quality someone naturally possesses; 恵む describes someone actively giving charity to another, a completely different grammatical structure.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 4 · 試す・営む・損なう

items.q: リサイクルして物を作るのには、実はかなりのエネルギーを（ ）らしい。
items.qr: Risaikuru shite mono o tsukuru no ni wa, jitsu wa kanari no enerugii o (___) rashii.
items.en: Apparently, making things through recycling actually consumes quite a lot of energy.
items.hi: रीसाइकल करके चीज़ें बनाने में असल में काफ़ी ऊर्जा ख़र्च होती है, ऐसा कहा जाता है।
items.gu: રિસાયકલ કરીને વસ્તુઓ બનાવવામાં ખરેખર ઘણી ઊર્જા ખર્ચાય છે, એવું કહેવાય છે.
items.why: エネルギーを費やす ("to spend/consume energy") is the fixed collocation matching the sentence's meaning about resource consumption.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 4 · 試す・営む・損なう

items.q: 我が国もかつては天然資源に（ ）。
items.qr: Waga kuni mo katsute wa tennen shigen ni (___).
items.en: Our country, too, was once rich in natural resources.
items.hi: हमारा देश भी कभी प्राकृतिक संसाधनों से समृद्ध था।
items.gu: અમારો દેશ પણ ક્યારેક કુદરતી સંસાધનોથી સમૃદ્ધ હતો.

opts.en: had been conducting/running (wrong meaning — takes a business/life as object, not a resource)

items.why: 資源に富む ("to be rich/abundant in resources") is the fixed collocation for a place having abundant natural resources.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 4 · 試す・営む・損なう

items.q: 夕焼けで赤みを（a. 暮れた b. 帯びた）空がきれいだ。
items.qr: Yuuyake de akami o (a. kureta / b. obita) sora ga kirei da.
items.en: The sky, tinged red by the sunset, is beautiful.
items.hi: शाम की लालिमा से रंगा आसमान बहुत ख़ूबसूरत है।
items.gu: સાંજની લાલાશથી રંગાયેલું આકાશ ખૂબ સુંદર છે.

opts.en: grew dark (wrong meaning — doesn't take 赤みを as an object)

items.why: 赤みを帯びる ("to be tinged with a reddish color") is the fixed collocation for describing a color tint; 暮れる only describes the sun setting/day ending, and doesn't take 赤み as a direct object.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 5 · 背く・経る・値する

items.q: 父は料理の面白さに（a. 目覚めた b. 転じた）らしく、毎日台所に立っている。
items.qr: Chichi wa ryouri no omoshirosa ni (a. mezameta / b. tenjita) rashiku, mainichi daidokoro ni tatte iru.
items.en: My father seems to have discovered how enjoyable cooking is, and now stands in the kitchen every day.
items.hi: पिताजी को खाना बनाने में मज़ा आने लगा है, लगता है, अब वे रोज़ रसोई में रहते हैं।
items.gu: પપ્પાને રસોઈ બનાવવામાં મજા આવવા લાગી છે, લાગે છે, હવે તેઓ રોજ રસોડામાં હોય છે.

opts.en: shifted/changed (wrong meaning — describes a situation changing, not a person discovering an interest)

items.why: ～の面白さに目覚める ("to awaken to how interesting ~ is") is the fixed phrase for discovering a new passion; 転じる describes an external situation changing direction, not a personal realization.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 5 · 背く・経る・値する

items.q: 彼女は毎日異国で暮らす息子の健康を（a. 案じている b. 報じている）。
items.qr: Kanojo wa mainichi ikoku de kurasu musuko no kenkou o (a. anjite iru / b. houjite iru).
items.en: She worries every day about the health of her son living abroad.
items.hi: वह हर दिन विदेश में रहने वाले अपने बेटे की सेहत की चिंता करती है।
items.gu: તે રોજ વિદેશમાં રહેતા પોતાના દીકરાની તબિયતની ચિંતા કરે છે.

opts.en: is reporting (wrong meaning — for news media, not a mother's feelings)

items.why: 健康を案じる ("to worry about someone's health") describes personal concern; 報じる is exclusively for media reporting news, an unrelated register.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 5 · 背く・経る・値する

items.q: 我がチームはやっと最下位から（a. 脱する b. 準じる）ことができた。
items.qr: Waga chiimu wa yatto saikai kara (a. dassuru / b. junjiru) koto ga dekita.
items.en: Our team was finally able to escape from last place.
items.hi: हमारी टीम आख़िरकार आख़िरी स्थान से बाहर निकल पाई।
items.gu: અમારી ટીમ છેવટે છેલ્લા સ્થાનેથી બહાર નીકળી શકી.

opts.en: to conform to a standard (wrong meaning — doesn't fit "escaping" a rank)

items.why: 最下位から脱する ("to escape from last place") is the natural collocation for climbing out of a bad ranking; 準じる describes matching/following an existing standard, unrelated to escaping a position.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 5 · 背く・経る・値する

items.q: 最近この地方に大きい地震が（a. 相次いで b. 震わせて）起こっている。
items.qr: Saikin kono chihou ni ookii jishin ga (a. aitsuide / b. furuwasete) okotte iru.
items.en: Large earthquakes have been occurring one after another in this region recently.
items.hi: हाल ही में इस इलाक़े में लगातार बड़े भूकंप आ रहे हैं।
items.gu: તાજેતરમાં આ વિસ્તારમાં સતત મોટા ધરતીકંપ આવી રહ્યા છે.

opts.en: making (something) tremble (wrong meaning/grammar — needs an object being shaken, not describing frequency of events)

items.why: 相次いで起こる ("to occur one after another") is the standard way to describe a series of repeated events like earthquakes; 震わせる is a transitive causative verb needing a direct object being shaken, not a description of event frequency.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 5 · 背く・経る・値する

items.q: 兄は、土日はマージャンに（a. 重んじている b. 興じている）。
items.qr: Ani wa, dojitsu wa maajan ni (a. omonjite iru / b. kyoujite iru).
items.en: My older brother spends his weekends enjoying mahjong.
items.hi: मेरा बड़ा भाई सप्ताहांत में माह-जोंग खेलने में मशग़ूल रहता है।
items.gu: મારો મોટો ભાઈ સપ્તાહાંતમાં માહજોંગ રમવામાં મશગૂલ રહે છે.

opts.en: is placing importance on (wrong meaning — for values/principles, not a leisure activity)

items.why: ～に興じる ("to enjoy oneself doing ~") fits a leisure activity like mahjong; 重んじる means to hold something in high regard/value it, a completely different sense.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 5 · 背く・経る・値する

items.q: 彼は親の教えに（ ）、不良になってしまった。
items.qr: Kare wa oya no oshie ni (___), furyou ni natte shimatta.
items.en: He went against his parents' teachings and became delinquent.
items.hi: उसने माता-पिता की सीख के ख़िलाफ़ जाकर बिगड़ैल बन गया।
items.gu: તેણે માતા-પિતાની શીખની વિરુદ્ધ જઈને બગડી ગયો.

opts.en: conforming to (wrong meaning — the opposite of what happens here)

items.why: 教えに背く ("to go against/disobey a teaching") is the fixed collocation for defying guidance; 準じる would mean the opposite — following a standard.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 5 · 背く・経る・値する

items.q: 彼は父親が（ ）財産を次々と売ってしまった。
items.qr: Kare wa chichioya ga (___) zaisan o tsugitsugi to utte shimatta.
items.en: He sold off, one after another, the fortune his father had built.
items.hi: उसने अपने पिता द्वारा बनाई गई संपत्ति एक-एक करके बेच डाली।
items.gu: તેણે તેના પિતાએ બનાવેલી સંપત્તિ એક પછી એક વેચી નાખી.

opts.en: set up, positioned (wrong meaning here — for a shop/stance, not accumulated wealth)
prospered (wrong meaning — describes a place/nation flourishing, not building a fortune)

items.why: 財産を築く ("to build up a fortune") is the fixed collocation for accumulating wealth over time; 栄える describes a place/nation prospering in general, not one person's personal wealth.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 5 · 背く・経る・値する

items.q: 朝の電車は（a. 過密な b. 独自の）ダイヤで運行している。
items.qr: Asa no densha wa (a. kamitsu na / b. dokuji no) daiya de unkou shite iru.
items.en: Morning trains run on an extremely packed schedule.
items.hi: सुबह की ट्रेनें बेहद भरे-पूरे समय-सारणी पर चलती हैं।
items.gu: સવારની ટ્રેનો ખૂબ ભરચક સમયપત્રક પર દોડે છે.

opts.en: one's own, unique (wrong meaning — a schedule can't be "unique," it can be "densely packed")

items.why: 過密なダイヤ ("an overly packed timetable") is the standard collocation for frequent, tightly-spaced train schedules; 独自 describes originality, unrelated to schedule density.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 6 · 最寄り・気配・手際

items.q: 株の売買は（a. 自己 b. 自我）責任で行うものです。
items.qr: Kabu no baibai wa (a. jiko / b. jiga) sekinin de okonau mono desu.
items.en: Stock trading is something one does at one's own responsibility.
items.hi: शेयर ख़रीदना-बेचना अपनी ज़िम्मेदारी पर किया जाता है।
items.gu: શેરની ખરીદી-વેચાણ પોતાની જવાબદારી પર કરવામાં આવે છે.

opts.en: the ego (a psychological concept, not a fixed compound with 責任)

items.why: 自己責任 ("at one's own responsibility") is the fixed legal/financial phrase; 自我 refers to the psychological "ego" and doesn't combine with 責任 as a set phrase.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 6 · 最寄り・気配・手際

items.q: チラシの30日（土）は（a. 誤り b. 過ち）です。正しくは30日（日）です。
items.qr: Chirashi no sanjuunichi (do) wa (a. ayamari / b. ayamachi) desu. Tadashiku wa sanjuunichi (nichi) desu.
items.en: The flyer's "30th (Sat)" is an error. The correct date is 30th (Sun).
items.hi: पर्चे में "30 तारीख़ (शनि)" ग़लत है। सही तारीख़ "30 (रवि)" है।
items.gu: પત્રિકામાં "30 તારીખ (શનિ)" ભૂલ છે. સાચી તારીખ "30 (રવિ)" છે.

opts.en: a mistake/wrongdoing (moral — wrong register for a printing error)

items.why: 誤り describes a simple factual/typographical error, exactly a wrong date printed on a flyer; 過ち carries a moral weight (a wrongdoing one regrets), which doesn't fit a printing mistake.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 6 · 最寄り・気配・手際

items.q: この切手は将来（a. 意欲 b. 値打ち）が出るかもしれない。
items.qr: Kono kitte wa shourai (a. iyoku / b. neuchi) ga deru kamoshirenai.
items.en: This stamp might become valuable in the future.
items.hi: हो सकता है यह टिकट भविष्य में क़ीमती हो जाए।
items.gu: આ ટિકિટ ભવિષ્યમાં કિંમતી બની શકે છે.

opts.en: eagerness/motivation (wrong meaning — a stamp can't have "motivation")

items.why: 値打ちが出る ("to gain value") is the fixed phrase for an item becoming valuable over time; 意欲 only applies to a living being's motivation/eagerness, never an object.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 6 · 最寄り・気配・手際

items.q: フリーズしたパソコンを（a. 無茶に b. 強制的に）終了させた。
items.qr: Furiizu shita pasokon o (a. mucha ni / b. kyouseiteki ni) shuuryou saseta.
items.en: I force-quit the computer that had frozen.
items.hi: जो कंप्यूटर अटक गया था, उसे ज़बरदस्ती बंद कर दिया।
items.gu: જે કમ્પ્યુટર અટકી ગયું હતું, તેને બળજબરીથી બંધ કરી દીધું.

opts.en: recklessly (wrong meaning — describes reckless behavior, not a forced technical shutdown)

items.why: 強制的に終了させる ("to force-quit/forcibly shut down") is the standard IT phrase for ending an unresponsive program; 無茶 describes reckless/unreasonable behavior in a general sense, not this specific technical action.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 6 · 最寄り・気配・手際

items.q: 彼は知事選に立候補する（a. 作戦 b. 決意）を固めたようです。
items.qr: Kare wa chijisen ni rikkouho suru (a. sakusen / b. ketsui) o katameta you desu.
items.en: He seems to have firmed up his resolve to run in the gubernatorial election.
items.hi: लगता है उसने राज्यपाल चुनाव में उम्मीदवारी का पक्का इरादा कर लिया है।
items.gu: લાગે છે તેણે ગવર્નર ચૂંટણીમાં ઉમેદવારીનો દૃઢ નિર્ણય કરી લીધો છે.

opts.en: a strategy/tactics (wrong meaning here — 固める pairs with resolve, not a plan)

items.why: 決意を固める ("to firm up one's resolve") is the fixed collocation for someone committing to a decision; 作戦を練る (not 固める) is the phrase used with "strategy."
items.unit: Week 5 Day 6 · 最寄り・気配・手際

items.q: 事故の現場を（ ）にして、恐ろしかった。
items.qr: Jiko no genba o (___) ni shite, osoroshikatta.
items.en: Witnessing the accident scene firsthand, I was terrified.
items.hi: दुर्घटना का दृश्य अपनी आँखों के सामने देखकर, मैं दहशत में आ गया।
items.gu: અકસ્માતનું દ્રશ્ય પોતાની આંખો સામે જોઈને, હું ડરી ગયો.

opts.en: hearing for the first time (wrong meaning — this is about seeing, not hearing)

items.why: 目の当たりにする ("to witness with one's own eyes") is the fixed phrase for directly seeing something shocking, exactly an accident scene.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 6 · 最寄り・気配・手際

items.q: これは我が社が開発した（ ）新技術です。
items.qr: Kore wa waga sha ga kaihatsu shita (___) shingijutsu desu.
items.en: This is an epoch-making new technology our company developed.
items.hi: यह हमारी कंपनी द्वारा विकसित एक युगांतरकारी नई तकनीक है।
items.gu: આ અમારી કંપની દ્વારા વિકસાવેલી એક યુગપરિવર્તક નવી ટેકનોલોજી છે.

opts.en: objective (wrong meaning — describes a viewpoint, not a technology's significance)

items.why: 画期的な発明/技術 ("an epoch-making invention/technology") is the standard collocation for praising a major breakthrough.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 6 · 最寄り・気配・手際

items.q: 新薬の効果をまず動物で（ ）研究しています。
items.qr: Shinyaku no kouka o mazu doubutsu de (___) kenkyuu shite imasu.
items.en: We are researching the new drug's effects by first testing it on animals.
items.hi: हम नई दवा के असर की जाँच पहले जानवरों पर करके शोध कर रहे हैं।
items.gu: અમે નવી દવાની અસર પહેલા પ્રાણીઓ પર ચકાસીને સંશોધન કરી રહ્યા છીએ.
items.why: Day 4's 試す ("to try out/test") is exactly what animal testing of a new drug's effects is.

items.q: 兄弟でもめないように、ケーキを（ ）に切り分けた。
items.qr: Kyoudai de momenai you ni, keeki o (___) ni kiriwaketa.
items.en: So the siblings wouldn't fight, the cake was cut into equal, fair portions.
items.hi: भाई-बहनों में झगड़ा न हो, इसलिए केक बराबर-बराबर बाँटा गया।
items.gu: ભાઈ-બહેનો વચ્ચે ઝઘડો ન થાય એટલે કેક સરખા ભાગે વહેંચી.

opts.en: fair (about dealings/processes, not literally dividing food)

items.why: Day 2's 公平に分ける is precisely "to divide equally/fairly" — matching cutting a cake into equal shares.

items.q: （ ）だけでささやかな結婚式を挙げた。
items.qr: (___) dake de sasayaka na kekkonshiki o ageta.
items.en: We held a modest wedding with just family present.
items.hi: सिर्फ़ परिवार वालों के साथ एक छोटी-सी शादी की।
items.gu: ફક્ત કુટુંબીજનો સાથે એક નાનકડું લગ્ન કર્યું.

opts.en: close/familiar (an adjective, not a group of people)
alone, by oneself (wrong meaning — a wedding needs at least two people)

items.why: Day 1's 身内だけで祝う ("to celebrate with only family present") is the exact fixed phrase for a small family-only event.

items.q: 隣人は変わっているが、このあたりは環境に（ ）地域です。
items.qr: Rinjin wa kawatte iru ga, kono atari wa kankyou ni (___) chiiki desu.
items.en: The neighbor is a bit odd, but this area is a region blessed with a good environment.
items.hi: पड़ोसी थोड़ा अजीब है, पर यह इलाक़ा अच्छे माहौल से नवाज़ा हुआ है।
items.gu: પડોશી થોડો વિચિત્ર છે, પણ આ વિસ્તાર સારા વાતાવરણથી નવાજાયેલો છે.

opts.en: troubled/plagued by (wrong meaning — the sentence is positive about the environment)
is put at ease (wrong meaning — for a feeling, not an environment being described as blessed)

items.why: Day 4's 恵む, in its passive form 恵まれている, is the standard way to describe a place as "blessed with" (a good climate/environment).

items.q: この新しい装置は自動車産業にとって、（ ）な発明である。
items.qr: Kono atarashii souchi wa jidousha sangyou ni totte, (___) na hatsumei de aru.
items.en: This new device is an epoch-making invention for the automobile industry.
items.hi: यह नया उपकरण ऑटोमोबाइल उद्योग के लिए एक युगांतरकारी आविष्कार है।
items.gu: આ નવું ઉપકરણ ઓટોમોબાઈલ ઉદ્યોગ માટે એક યુગપરિવર્તક શોધ છે.

opts.en: not a standard word (正当 doesn't normally take 的)
fundamental (wrong meaning — describes a root cause, not a breakthrough)

items.why: Day 6's 画期的な発明/発見 is the fixed phrase for praising a groundbreaking invention.

items.q: 彼の推理は、はなはだしく（ ）違いだ。
items.qr: Kare no suiri wa, hanahadashiku (___) chigai da.
items.en: His reasoning is way off the mark.
items.hi: उसका अनुमान बिल्कुल ग़लत दिशा में है।
items.gu: તેનું અનુમાન સાવ ખોટી દિશામાં છે.

opts.en: actual situation (wrong meaning — doesn't combine with 違い this way)
a guess (見当違い = "wide of the mark")

items.why: Day 1's 見当 combines with 違い as the fixed idiom 見当違い ("a mistaken guess, wide of the mark") — none of the other options form a real compound with 違い.

items.q: 彼はまだ高校1年生だが、将来（ ）な野球選手になるだろう。
items.qr: Kare wa mada koukou ichinensei da ga, shourai (___) na yakyuu senshu ni naru darou.
items.en: He's still only a high school first-year, but he'll probably become a promising baseball player.
items.hi: वह अभी हाई स्कूल के पहले साल में है, पर आगे चलकर एक होनहार बेसबॉल खिलाड़ी बनेगा।
items.gu: તે હજુ હાઈસ્કૂલના પહેલા વર્ષમાં છે, પણ ભવિષ્યમાં એક આશાસ્પદ બેઝબોલ ખેલાડી બનશે.

opts.en: useful/beneficial (wrong meaning — for things, not a person's future prospects)
influential (wrong meaning — for someone with power now, not future promise)
epoch-making (wrong meaning — for inventions, not a person's career)

items.why: Day 3's 有望な研究者-type usage extends naturally to 有望な野球選手 ("a promising baseball player") — describing someone's future potential.

items.q: 仕事をサボって、マージャンに（ ）いたところを上司に見つかってしまった。
items.qr: Shigoto o sabotte, maajan ni (___) ita tokoro o joushi ni mitsukatte shimatta.
items.en: I skipped work, and my boss caught me right in the middle of enjoying a game of mahjong.
items.hi: काम से बचकर माह-जोंग खेलने में मशग़ूल था, तभी बॉस ने पकड़ लिया।
items.gu: કામમાંથી છટકીને માહજોંગ રમવામાં મશગૂલ હતો, ત્યાં જ બોસે પકડી પાડ્યો.
items.why: Day 5's ～に興じる ("to enjoy oneself doing ~") is the exact fit for being absorbed in a game of mahjong.

items.q: （ ）通りのやり方ではだめだ。別の対策を考えなければならない。
items.qr: (___) doori no yarikata de wa dame da. Betsu no taisaku o kangaenakereba naranai.
items.en: Doing it the same way as always won't work. We have to think of another approach.
items.hi: हमेशा की तरह करना अब काम नहीं करेगा। कोई और उपाय सोचना होगा।
items.gu: હંમેશની જેમ કરવાથી નહીં ચાલે. બીજો કોઈ ઉપાય વિચારવો પડશે.
items.why: Day 6's 従来通り ("as has always been done") is the exact fixed phrase for the old, conventional way of doing something.

items.q: 彼女の家がゴミだらけだという（ ）を誰も知らない。
items.qr: Kanojo no ie ga gomi darake da to iu (___) o dare mo shiranai.
items.en: No one knows the actual reality that her house is full of garbage.
items.hi: यह सच्चाई कि उसका घर कचरे से भरा है, किसी को पता नहीं।
items.gu: તેનું ઘર કચરાથી ભરેલું છે એ ખરી હકીકત કોઈને ખબર નથી.

opts.en: outward appearance (wrong meaning — this is a hidden reality, not a stated official reason)

items.why: Day 2's 実態 ("the actual state of affairs") fits a hidden, unpleasant reality that "no one knows" — exactly this sentence's structure.

items.q: 道具や言葉をうまく使う。 ("To skillfully use a tool or language.")
items.qr: Dougu ya kotoba o umaku tsukau.

opts.en: to be equipped with (wrong meaning — a state, not an action of using)

items.why: Day 4's 操る (as in 機械を上手に操る) means precisely "to skillfully handle/operate" a tool, machine, or even a language.

items.q: どうもそうらしいと感覚的に感じる様子。 ("The state of sensing, on a gut level, that something seems to be the case.")
items.qr: Doumo sou rashii to kankakuteki ni kanjiru yousu.
items.why: Day 6's 気配 (as in 人の気配がする) is exactly the sense of perceiving, without seeing directly, that something/someone is present.

items.q: りっぱに見えたりして、目立つ。 ("To look impressive and stand out.")
items.qr: Rippa ni mietari shite, medatsu.

opts.en: to prosper (wrong meaning — about a place/nation flourishing over time, not visually standing out)
to be set off attractively, stand out
to grow/sprout (wrong meaning — an unrelated homophone-like word for plants/hair)

items.why: Day 5's 映える (as in 夕日に映える) describes something being set off beautifully and standing out visually — exactly this definition; 栄える describes prosperity/flourishing over time, and 生える means "to grow" (plants, hair), an unrelated word that happens to share the reading はえる.

items.q: どれもこれもすべて。 ("Each and every one, without exception.")
items.qr: Dore mo kore mo subete.

opts.en: each individual, separately (wrong nuance — this is about examining items one by one, not "all alike")
across the board, every single one

items.why: Day 6's 軒並み (as in 軒並み値上がりする) means exactly "each and every one, all alike" — this week's own warm-up definition verbatim.

items.q: 中心となって適切に物事を処理する。 ("To take charge as the central figure and handle matters appropriately.")
items.qr: Chuushin to natte tekisetsu ni monogoto o shori suru.

opts.en: to devote oneself entirely to a role (wrong meaning — describes staying purely in one role, not taking charge)
to take charge and run (an event)
to handle personally (wrong meaning — for working directly on something, not being the central organizer)

items.why: Day 3's 仕切る (as in 宴会を仕切る) means exactly "to be the central figure who runs/manages things appropriately."

items.q: この電球は高いが、大幅な電気代の節約になるというメリットがある。
items.qr: Kono denkyuu wa takai ga, oohaba na denkidai no setsuyaku ni naru to iu meritto ga aru.
items.en: This lightbulb is expensive, but it has the merit of significantly cutting electricity costs.

opts.en: beneficial (close, but describes a general quality of usefulness, not a specific named advantage)
interest, a false-friend trap sharing 利 with 利点 (wrong meaning)

items.why: Day 3's 利点 is the direct Japanese equivalent of "merit/advantage," exactly matching メリット here.

items.q: 成績でずっと一位を維持するのは難しいことです。
items.qr: Seiseki de zutto ichii o iji suru no wa muzukashii koto desu.
items.en: Maintaining first place in grades all the time is difficult.

opts.en: to devote oneself entirely to (wrong meaning)
to build (wrong meaning — for constructing something new, not sustaining an existing state)

items.why: Day 4's 保つ (as in 部屋を清潔に保つ) is the direct synonym of 維持する ("to maintain, keep up") a state over time.

items.q: 彼は用事を言いつけてばかりで、自分では何もしない。
items.qr: Kare wa youji o iitsukete bakari de, jibun de wa nani mo shinai.
items.en: He's always ordering people around with errands and never does anything himself.

opts.en: making excuses (wrong meaning — a false-friend trap sharing 言い with 言いつける)
leaving (a task) to someone (close, but describes delegating trust, not the act of barking orders)

items.why: Day 2's 指図する ("to give orders/directions") is the direct synonym of 言いつける in the sense of constantly telling others what to do.

items.q: そちらに伺いたいのですが、一番近い駅はどこでしょうか。
items.qr: Sochira ni ukagaitai no desu ga, ichiban chikai eki wa doko deshou ka.
items.en: I'd like to visit you — where is the nearest station?

opts.en: close/familiar (wrong meaning — for everyday familiarity, not physical proximity of a place)
around oneself (wrong meaning — for belongings, not the nearest station)

items.why: Day 6's 最寄り is the direct, standard word for "the nearest" (station, store) — exactly matching 一番近い here.

items.q: 父の命令を聞かないで、大学をやめた。
items.u: 命令を聞かないで / meirei o kikanai de
items.qr: Chichi no meirei o kikanai de, daigaku o yameta.
items.en: Without listening to/obeying his father's order, he quit university.

opts.en: devoting oneself entirely to an order (wrong meaning — the opposite sense)

items.why: Day 5's 命令に背く ("to disobey an order") is the exact standard phrase for not listening to/going against an order.

items.q: 和む
items.qr: nagomu

opts.t: 朝から気持ちが悪かったが、少し寝たら和みました。
opts.r: Asa kara kimochi ga warukatta ga, sukoshi netara nagomimashita.
opts.en: "I felt sick since morning, but after sleeping a bit I 和みました" — wrong; recovering from feeling ill/nauseated needs 治る/よくなる, not 和む

opts.t: 日本の国旗が空に和んでいた。
opts.r: Nihon no kokki ga sora ni nagonde ita.
opts.en: "The Japanese flag was 和んでいた in the sky" — wrong; a flag waving in the sky needs はためく, not 和む

opts.t: 彼のジョークのおかげで、固かった雰囲気が一気に和んだ。
opts.r: Kare no jooku no okage de, katakatta fun'iki ga ikki ni nagonda.
opts.en: Thanks to his joke, the tense atmosphere relaxed all at once.

opts.t: 彼とは古くから和んだ友達です。
opts.r: Kare to wa furuku kara nagonda tomodachi desu.
opts.en: "He's a longtime 和んだ friend" — wrong; a longtime, easy-going friend needs 気心の知れた, not 和んだ as a noun modifier

items.why: 和む describes an atmosphere/feeling being softened and put at ease — sentence 3 matches Day 2's own example (心が和む extended to 雰囲気が和む) exactly; 1, 2, and 4 each swap in a meaning (recovering from illness, a flag fluttering, an old friendship) that a different word actually covers.

items.q: 勝手
items.qr: katte

opts.t: 勝手に決めないで、私にも相談してください。
opts.r: Katte ni kimenaide, watashi ni mo soudan shite kudasai.
opts.en: Don't decide on your own without asking — consult me too.

opts.t: 秋になって気温が勝手に下がってきた。
opts.r: Aki ni natte kion ga katte ni sagatte kita.
opts.en: "The temperature dropped 勝手に as autumn came" — wrong; a natural, automatic process needs 自然に/ひとりでに, not 勝手に which implies willful human agency

opts.t: あなたの意見を聞けないのは、私勝手です。
opts.r: Anata no iken o kikenai no wa, watashi katte desu.
opts.en: Grammatically malformed — the fixed phrase is 自分勝手／身勝手, not "私勝手"

opts.t: 勝手の結果で、不合格になってしまった。
opts.r: Katte no kekka de, fugoukaku ni natte shimatta.
opts.en: "As a result of 勝手, I failed" — wrong; doesn't make sense as a cause for failing an exam

items.why: 勝手に決める ("to decide arbitrarily/selfishly, without consulting others") is the standard usage — sentence 1 matches Day 6's own example (勝手な行動をとる) exactly; 2–4 each misuse it for a natural process, a malformed compound, or an unrelated cause.

items.q: 値しない
items.qr: ataishinai

opts.t: その製品は値しない評判がある。
opts.r: Sono seihin wa ataishinai hyouban ga aru.
opts.en: "That product has a reputation that 値しない" — grammatically malformed; 値する needs a specific に-marked object (e.g. 信頼に値する), not a vague noun modifier

opts.t: 彼女の行動は問題があるから、私に値しない人物だ。
opts.r: Kanojo no koudou wa mondai ga aru kara, watashi ni ataishinai jinbutsu da.
opts.en: "Her behavior is problematic, so she's a person who 私に値しない" — wrong/malformed; 値する needs an abstract standard like 尊敬 (respect), not a personal pronoun

opts.t: この本は内容に値しないと言われている。
opts.r: Kono hon wa naiyou ni ataishinai to iwarete iru.
opts.en: "This book is said to 内容に値しない" — wrong/unclear referent; doesn't parse against a standard the way the book's own example does

opts.t: 社員を大事にしない会社は、信頼に値しない。
opts.r: Shain o daiji ni shinai kaisha wa, shinrai ni ataishinai.
opts.en: A company that doesn't value its employees isn't worthy of trust.

items.why: ～に値する／値しない ("to be worth/not worth ~") always takes a specific abstract standard marked by に (信頼, 尊敬, 一読) — sentence 4 matches Day 5's own example (この本は一読に値する) exactly in structure; 1–3 each attach 値する to the wrong kind of object.

items.q: 根回し
items.qr: nemawashi

opts.t: 今度は、根回さないようにしたから大丈夫です。
opts.r: Kondo wa, nemawasanai you ni shita kara daijoubu desu.
opts.en: Grammatically malformed — 根回し is a noun that pairs with する (根回しする), not a plain verb "根回す"

opts.t: 選挙での根回しが失敗して、彼は落選したと言われている。
opts.r: Senkyo de no nemawashi ga shippai shite, kare wa rakusen shita to iwarete iru.
opts.en: It's said that his behind-the-scenes groundwork for the election failed, and he lost.

opts.t: 大至急この書類を根回ししておいてください。
opts.r: Daishikyuu kono shorui o nemawashi shite oite kudasai.
opts.en: "Please urgently 根回し this document" — wrong; 根回し targets people/support one lobbies, not a document itself

opts.t: 根回しで会社をやめたけれど、後悔している。
opts.r: Nemawashi de kaisha o yameta keredo, koukai shite iru.
opts.en: "I quit the company because of 根回し, but I regret it" — wrong; quitting isn't something 根回し (groundwork/lobbying) causes

items.why: 根回し names the quiet, behind-the-scenes work of building support among the people who matter for a decision — sentence 2 matches Day 1's own example (関係者に根回しする) in spirit exactly, describing pre-election lobbying; 1, 3, and 4 each misuse the word's grammar or target.

items.q: 実入り
items.qr: miiri

opts.t: 今年は会社に三人の実入りが来た。
opts.r: Kotoshi wa kaisha ni sannin no miiri ga kita.
opts.en: "This year, three people's 実入り came to the company" — wrong; should be 新入り (newcomers), an unrelated word

opts.t: 今度の仕事はかなり実入りがよい。
opts.r: Kondo no shigoto wa kanari miiri ga yoi.
opts.en: This next job pays quite well.

opts.t: 彼は若いが、とても実入りがよい。
opts.r: Kare wa wakai ga, totemo miiri ga yoi.
opts.en: "He's young, but very 実入りがいい" — wrong register; 実入り describes a job/business's profitability, not a person's own trait out of context

opts.t: 彼女は初心者ながら、立派に実入りを果たした。
opts.r: Kanojo wa shoshinsha nagara, rippa ni miiri o hatashita.
opts.en: "Though a beginner, she splendidly 実入りを果たした" — wrong; not a real collocation, 役目を果たす ("fulfill a role") is the standard phrase with 果たす

items.why: 実入りがいい ("to pay well, be profitable") describes a job or business venture — sentence 2 matches Day 2's own example (実入りのいい商売) exactly; 1, 3, and 4 each misapply the word to a person or force it into a non-existent collocation.

items.q: 彼のギャグは、全然（a.つながらなかった b.うけなかった）。
items.qr: Kare no gyagu wa, zenzen (a. tsunagaranakatta b. ukenakatta).
items.en: His joke didn't land at all.
items.hi: उसका मज़ाक बिल्कुल पसंद नहीं आया।
items.gu: તેની મજાક બિલકુલ ન ગમી.

opts.en: didn't connect (wrong meaning — a joke can't "connect")

items.why: 受ける in the "be well-received" sense is exactly what a joke either does or doesn't do with an audience.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 1 · 受ける・滑る・つながる

items.q: パンにハムを（a.はさんで b.つなげて）食べました。
items.qr: Pan ni hamu o (a. hasande b. tsunagete) tabemashita.
items.en: I ate bread with ham sandwiched inside.
items.hi: मैंने ब्रेड में हैम रखकर खाया।
items.gu: મેં બ્રેડમાં હેમ મૂકીને ખાધું.

opts.en: connecting (wrong verb — ham isn't "connected" to bread)

items.why: 挟む is the exact verb for putting a filling between two slices of bread.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 1 · 受ける・滑る・つながる

items.q: つい口を（a.はさんで b.すべらせて）、彼の秘密をばらしてしまった。
items.qr: Tsui kuchi o (a. hasande b. suberasete), kare no himitsu o barashite shimatta.
items.en: I accidentally let it slip and gave away his secret.
items.hi: अनजाने में मुँह से निकल गया और उसका राज़ खुल गया।
items.gu: અજાણતાં મોઢામાંથી નીકળી ગયું ને તેનું રહસ્ય ખૂલી ગયું.
items.why: 口を滑らせる ("to let one's mouth slip") is the fixed idiom for accidentally blurting out a secret.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 1 · 受ける・滑る・つながる

items.q: そのときの経験が、今の自信に（a.うけている b.つながっている）。
items.qr: Sono toki no keiken ga, ima no jishin ni (a. ukete iru b. tsunagatte iru).
items.en: That experience is connected to my confidence today.
items.hi: उस समय का अनुभव आज के आत्मविश्वास से जुड़ा हुआ है।
items.gu: તે વખતનો અનુભવ આજના આત્મવિશ્વાસ સાથે જોડાયેલો છે.
items.why: ～につながる describes an abstract cause leading to/feeding into a later result — exactly "past experience → present confidence."
items.unit: Week 6 Day 1 · 受ける・滑る・つながる

items.q: 彼女が結婚するといううわさを耳に（a.はさんだ b.受けた）。
items.qr: Kanojo ga kekkon suru to iu uwasa o mimi ni (a. hasanda b. uketa).
items.en: I happened to hear a rumor that she's getting married.
items.hi: यूँ ही कानों में पड़ा कि वह शादी करने वाली है।
items.gu: અફવા કાને પડી કે તે લગ્ન કરવાની છે.
items.why: 耳に挟む is the fixed idiom for overhearing a rumor by chance.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 1 · 受ける・滑る・つながる

items.q: ドアを開けるとき、手が（a.すべって b.はさんで）持っていた本を落としてしまった。
items.qr: Doa o akeru toki, te ga (a. subette b. hasande) motte ita hon o otoshite shimatta.
items.en: When I opened the door, my hand slipped and I dropped the book I was holding.
items.hi: दरवाज़ा खोलते समय हाथ फिसल गया और पकड़ी हुई किताब गिर गई।
items.gu: બારણું ખોલતી વખતે હાથ લપસ્યો ને પકડેલું પુસ્તક પડી ગયું.

opts.en: sandwiching (wrong verb — nothing was inserted between two things)

items.why: 手が滑る describes a hand physically slipping and losing its grip on something.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 1 · 受ける・滑る・つながる

items.q: 彼と彼女は戸籍上は兄弟だが、血は（ ）いない。
items.qr: Kare to kanojo wa koseki-jou wa kyoudai da ga, chi wa (___) inai.
items.en: Officially they're registered as siblings, but they're not related by blood.
items.hi: काग़ज़ों में वे भाई-बहन हैं, पर उनमें ख़ून का रिश्ता नहीं है।
items.gu: સત્તાવાર રીતે તેઓ ભાઈ-બહેન છે, પણ તેમની વચ્ચે લોહીનો સંબંધ નથી.

opts.en: connecting (something) — wrong, needs the intransitive form since 血が is the subject

items.why: 血がつながっている ("to be related by blood") needs the intransitive つながる, matching 血が as its subject — not the transitive つなげる.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 1 · 受ける・滑る・つながる

items.q: 彼の家は、うちの前の道路を（ ）向こう側にある。
items.qr: Kare no ie wa, uchi no mae no douro o (___) mukougawa ni aru.
items.en: His house is across the road from mine.
items.hi: उसका घर हमारे घर के सामने वाली सड़क के उस पार है।
items.gu: તેનું ઘર અમારા ઘર સામેના રસ્તાની સામી બાજુ છે.

opts.en: connecting (wrong meaning — a road isn't described as "connecting" two houses this way)

items.why: ～を挟んで向こう側 ("across ~, with it in between") is the standard way to describe a location on the far side of a road/river/table.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 1 · 受ける・滑る・つながる

items.q: 会議で反対意見が出ないよう、事前に手を（a.引いて b.回して）おいた。
items.qr: Kaigi de hantai iken ga denai you, jizen ni te o (a. hiite b. mawashite) oita.
items.en: To prevent objections at the meeting, I arranged things behind the scenes beforehand.
items.hi: बैठक में विरोध न हो, इसलिए पहले से गुप्त रूप से व्यवस्था कर रखी।
items.gu: મીટિંગમાં વિરોધ ન થાય એ માટે અગાઉથી છૂપી ગોઠવણ કરી રાખી.
items.why: 手を回す ("to work behind the scenes") is the fixed idiom for quietly arranging things before a meeting.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 2 · 通る・引く・回す

items.q: こんなに遅い時間まで子どもを（a.連れ回す b.連れ引く）のは、非常識だ。
items.qr: Konna ni osoi jikan made kodomo o (a. tsuremawasu b. tsurehiku) no wa, hijoushiki da.
items.en: Dragging a child around this late is thoughtless.
items.hi: इतनी देर रात तक बच्चे को इधर-उधर घुमाना समझदारी नहीं है।
items.gu: આટલી મોડી રાત સુધી બાળકને આમતેમ ફેરવવું અવિવેકી છે.
items.why: 連れ回す is the standard compound for dragging someone along from place to place.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 2 · 通る・引く・回す

items.q: 桜の花びらが風に（a.通って b.乗って）運ばれてきた。
items.qr: Sakura no hanabira ga kaze ni (a. tootte b. notte) hakobarete kita.
items.en: Cherry blossom petals were carried along by the wind.
items.hi: चेरी के फूलों की पंखुड़ियाँ हवा के सहारे उड़ती हुई आईं।
items.gu: ચેરીના ફૂલોની પાંખડીઓ પવનની સાથે ઊડીને આવી.
items.why: 風に乗る ("to ride/be carried on the wind") is the exact phrase for something drifting along on air currents — the book's own example uses pollen the same way.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 2 · 通る・引く・回す

items.q: この肉はまだ火がじゅうぶんに（a.乗って b.通って）ないから、もう一度焼いてください。
items.qr: Kono niku wa mada hi ga juubun ni (a. notte b. tootte) nai kara, mou ichido yaite kudasai.
items.en: This meat isn't cooked through yet, so please grill it again.
items.hi: यह मांस अभी अच्छी तरह पका नहीं है, इसलिए इसे दोबारा भूनिए।
items.gu: આ માંસ હજુ બરાબર ચડ્યું નથી, તેથી ફરી શેકો.
items.why: 火が通る ("heat passes through") is the set phrase for meat being properly cooked all the way through.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 2 · 通る・引く・回す

items.q: 彼女は泣いてみんなの注意を（a.引いた b.回した）。
items.qr: Kanojo wa naite minna no chuui o (a. hiita b. mawashita).
items.en: She cried and drew everyone's attention.
items.hi: वह रोकर सबका ध्यान खींच लाई।
items.gu: તે રડીને બધાનું ધ્યાન ખેંચી ગઈ.
items.why: 注意を引く ("to draw attention") is the fixed collocation; attention isn't "turned" (回す).
items.unit: Week 6 Day 2 · 通る・引く・回す

items.q: 彼はイギリスではかなり名の（a.乗った b.通った）作家です。
items.qr: Kare wa Igirisu de wa kanari na no (a. notta b. tootta) sakka desu.
items.en: He's quite a well-known writer in England.
items.hi: वह इंग्लैंड में काफ़ी नामी लेखक हैं।
items.gu: તે ઇંગ્લેન્ડમાં ખૂબ જાણીતા લેખક છે.
items.why: 名の通った is the fixed phrase for "well-known, famous" — matching today's list's 名の通った医師.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 2 · 通る・引く・回す

items.q: 気が（ ）けれど、上司に飲みに誘われたら断れない。
items.qr: Ki ga (___) keredo, joushi ni nomi ni sasowaretara kotowarenai.
items.en: I don't feel like it, but when my boss invites me for drinks I can't refuse.
items.hi: मन नहीं है, फिर भी बॉस जब पीने के लिए बुलाते हैं तो मना नहीं कर पाता।
items.gu: મન નથી થતું, છતાં બોસ પીવા બોલાવે તો ના પાડી શકાતી નથી.

opts.en: cannot withdraw (wrong verb for 気が)
doesn't pass (wrong verb for 気が)
doesn't pass (printed identically to option 2 in the book's own scan — likely a printing duplicate)

items.why: 気が乗らない ("not in the mood, not feeling it") is the fixed idiom from today's 乗る group; 気が引ける (a different idiom meaning "to feel awkward/hesitant") and 気が通る aren't standard phrases here.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 2 · 通る・引く・回す

items.q: 彼の提案は筋が（ ）が、実現するには難しいだろう。
items.qr: Kare no teian wa suji ga (___) ga, jitsugen suru ni wa muzukashii darou.
items.en: His proposal makes sense, but it'll probably be hard to actually carry out.
items.hi: उसका प्रस्ताव तर्कसंगत तो है, पर उसे लागू करना मुश्किल होगा।
items.gu: તેની દરખાસ્ત તાર્કિક છે, પણ અમલમાં મૂકવી અઘરી હશે.
items.why: 筋が通る ("to be logical, make sense") is the fixed collocation, matching today's own example 彼の言うことは筋が通っている.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 2 · 通る・引く・回す

items.q: 彼とは固い友情で（a.結ばれて b.結んで）いる。
items.qr: Kare to wa katai yuujou de (a. musubarete b. musunde) iru.
items.en: We are bound by a strong friendship.
items.hi: उसके साथ मेरी गहरी दोस्ती का बंधन है।
items.gu: તેની સાથે મારે ગાઢ મિત્રતાનું બંધન છે.

opts.en: tying (active — wrong voice for describing a mutual state)

items.why: 結ばれている (the passive/stative form) describes two people being bound together by a relationship, matching today's own example 二人は信頼感で結ばれている.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 3 · はる・送る・飛ぶ

items.q: 結婚して数年間は幸せな日々を（a.はって b.送って）いた。
items.qr: Kekkon shite suunenkan wa shiawase na hibi o (a. hatte b. okutte) ita.
items.en: For the first few years of marriage, I lived happy days.
items.hi: शादी के बाद कुछ सालों तक मैं ख़ुशहाल दिन बिता रहा था।
items.gu: લગ્ન પછી થોડાં વર્ષો સુધી હું સુખી દિવસો પસાર કરી રહ્યો હતો.
items.why: 日々を送る ("to spend one's days") is the fixed collocation for describing how one lives over a period of time.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 3 · はる・送る・飛ぶ

items.q: 努力が実を（a.結んで b.解けて）、実験に成功した。
items.qr: Doryoku ga mi o (a. musunde b. tokete), jikken ni seikou shita.
items.en: The effort bore fruit, and the experiment succeeded.
items.hi: मेहनत रंग लाई और प्रयोग सफल हुआ।
items.gu: મહેનત ફળી ને પ્રયોગ સફળ થયો.
items.why: 実を結ぶ ("to bear fruit," figuratively "to pay off") is the fixed idiom for effort finally producing results.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 3 · はる・送る・飛ぶ

items.q: 私は、胸を（a.はって b.とんで）、この作品には自信があると言えます。
items.qr: Watashi wa, mune o (a. hatte b. tonde), kono sakuhin ni wa jishin ga aru to iemasu.
items.en: I can proudly say I'm confident about this work.
items.hi: मैं सीना तानकर कह सकता हूँ कि मुझे इस रचना पर भरोसा है।
items.gu: હું છાતી કાઢીને કહી શકું છું કે મને આ કૃતિ પર વિશ્વાસ છે.
items.why: 胸を張る ("to puff up one's chest, be proud") is the fixed idiom for speaking with confidence.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 3 · はる・送る・飛ぶ

items.q: パソコンがフリーズして一瞬でデータが（a.とんで b.とけて）しまった。
items.qr: Pasokon ga furiizu shite isshun de deeta ga (a. tonde b. tokete) shimatta.
items.en: The computer froze and the data vanished in an instant.
items.hi: कंप्यूटर हैंग हो गया और पल भर में डेटा उड़ गया।
items.gu: કમ્પ્યુટર ફ્રીઝ થયું ને એક ક્ષણમાં ડેટા ઊડી ગયો.
items.why: データが飛ぶ ("data vanishes/is lost") uses 飛ぶ's "disappear suddenly" sense, matching today's own ボーナスが飛ぶ example.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 3 · はる・送る・飛ぶ

items.q: 彼女の誤解が（a.むすぶ b.とける）には時間がかかるだろう。
items.qr: Kanojo no gokai ga (a. musubu b. tokeru) ni wa jikan ga kakaru darou.
items.en: It will probably take time for her misunderstanding to be resolved.
items.hi: उसकी ग़लतफ़हमी दूर होने में समय लगेगा।
items.gu: તેની ગેરસમજ દૂર થવામાં સમય લાગશે.
items.why: 誤解が解ける ("a misunderstanding is resolved/dissolves") is the fixed phrase, matching today's own example.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 3 · はる・送る・飛ぶ

items.q: パチンコで一万円札が（ ）いった。
items.qr: Pachinko de ichiman-en-satsu ga (___) itta.
items.en: I lost a 10,000-yen bill playing pachinko.
items.hi: पचिंको खेलते हुए दस हज़ार येन उड़ गए।
items.gu: પચિન્કો રમતાં દસ હજાર યેન ઊડી ગયા.
items.why: お金が飛ぶ ("money vanishes/disappears") uses the same figurative sense of 飛ぶ as ボーナスが飛ぶ in today's list.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 3 · はる・送る・飛ぶ

items.q: その2社は、合併の契約を（ ）。
items.qr: Sono nisha wa, gappei no keiyaku o (___).
items.en: The two companies signed a merger agreement.
items.hi: उन दो कंपनियों ने विलय का अनुबंध किया।
items.gu: તે બે કંપનીઓએ મર્જરનો કરાર કર્યો.

opts.en: connected (wrong verb — used for physical/relational links, not signing a document)

items.why: 契約を結ぶ ("to conclude/sign a contract") is the fixed collocation, matching today's own example.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 3 · はる・送る・飛ぶ

items.q: これからのローンの返済を考えると気が（a.暗い b.重い）。
items.qr: Kore kara no roon no hensai o kangaeru to ki ga (a. kurai b. omoi).
items.en: Thinking about the loan repayments ahead makes me feel gloomy.
items.hi: आगे की लोन की किस्तों के बारे में सोचकर मन भारी हो जाता है।
items.gu: આગળની લોનની ચુકવણી વિચારીને મન ભારે થાય છે.

opts.en: dark (wrong word — 気が暗い isn't a standard phrase)

items.why: 気が重い is the fixed idiom for feeling gloomy/reluctant about something looming, matching today's own example about turning down a job.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 4 · 甘い・かたい・重い

items.q: この仕事を（a.まずく b.あまく）見ていると、あとで大変だよ。
items.qr: Kono shigoto o (a. mazuku b. amaku) mite iru to, ato de taihen da yo.
items.en: If you take this job too lightly, you'll be in trouble later.
items.hi: इस काम को हल्के में लोगे तो बाद में मुश्किल होगी।
items.gu: આ કામને હલકામાં લેશો તો પછી મુશ્કેલી થશે.
items.why: 甘く見る ("to underestimate, not take seriously") is the fixed collocation, matching today's own 仕事を甘く見る example.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 4 · 甘い・かたい・重い

items.q: 彼にそのように言ったのは非常に（a.重かった b.まずかった）。
items.qr: Kare ni sono you ni itta no wa hijou ni (a. omokatta b. mazukatta).
items.en: Saying that to him was a really bad move.
items.hi: उससे ऐसा कहना बहुत ग़लत था।
items.gu: તેને એવું કહેવું બહુ ખોટું હતું.
items.why: まずい in its "inadvisable, ill-judged" sense describes an action that was badly handled or unwise.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 4 · 甘い・かたい・重い

items.q: 不況を脱して今後の景気の見通しは（a.かたい b.明るい）。
items.qr: Fukyou o dasshite kongo no keiki no mitooshi wa (a. katai b. akarui).
items.en: Having come out of the recession, the economic outlook is bright.
items.hi: मंदी से उबरकर आगे की आर्थिक स्थिति उज्ज्वल है।
items.gu: મંદીમાંથી બહાર આવીને ભવિષ્યની આર્થિક સ્થિતિ ઉજ્જવળ છે.
items.why: 見通しが明るい ("the outlook is bright") is the fixed phrase for good prospects, matching today's own example.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 4 · 甘い・かたい・重い

items.q: タバコをやめようと（a.かたく b.重く）決心をした。
items.qr: Tabako o yameyou to (a. kataku b. omoku) kesshin o shita.
items.en: I made a firm decision to quit smoking.
items.hi: सिगरेट छोड़ने का दृढ़ निश्चय किया।
items.gu: સિગારેટ છોડવાનો મક્કમ નિર્ણય કર્યો.
items.why: かたく決心する ("to firmly resolve") is the fixed collocation for a strong resolution.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 4 · 甘い・かたい・重い

items.q: 「大もうけできますよ」という（a.甘い b.明るい）誘いにのって、全財産を失ってしまった。
items.qr: "Oomouke dekimasu yo" to iu (a. amai b. akarui) sasoi ni notte, zenzaisan o ushinatte shimatta.
items.en: Tempted by the sweet talk of "you'll make a fortune," I lost my entire fortune.
items.hi: "बहुत मुनाफ़ा होगा" जैसे लुभावने झांसे में आकर मैंने अपनी पूरी जमा-पूँजी गँवा दी।
items.gu: "ખૂબ કમાણી થશે" જેવી લોભામણી વાતમાં આવીને મેં મારી બધી મૂડી ગુમાવી.
items.why: 甘い誘い ("a tempting/sweet-sounding offer") describes an offer designed to lure someone in — exactly a get-rich-quick scheme.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 4 · 甘い・かたい・重い

items.q: 彼は、頭が（ ）から、自分の意見を変えないでしょう。
items.qr: Kare wa, atama ga (___) kara, jibun no iken o kaenai deshou.
items.en: He's stubborn, so he probably won't change his opinion.
items.hi: वह ज़िद्दी है, इसलिए अपनी राय नहीं बदलेगा।
items.gu: તે હઠીલો છે, તેથી પોતાનો મત નહીં બદલે.

opts.en: heavy/foggy-headed (wrong sense — describes tiredness, not stubbornness)

items.why: 頭がかたい ("hard-headed, stubborn") is the fixed idiom, matching today's own 父は頭がかたい example.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 4 · 甘い・かたい・重い

items.q: 我が社は今回の事故を（ ）受け止め、再発防止に努めます。
items.qr: Wagasha wa konkai no jiko o (___) uketome, saihatsu boushi ni tsutomemasu.
items.en: Our company takes this accident seriously and will work to prevent recurrence.
items.hi: हमारी कंपनी इस दुर्घटना को गंभीरता से लेती है और भविष्य में इसे रोकने का प्रयास करेगी।
items.gu: અમારી કંપની આ અકસ્માતને ગંભીરતાથી લે છે અને પુનરાવર્તન અટકાવવાનો પ્રયાસ કરશે.
items.why: 重く受け止める ("to take something seriously/gravely") is the standard corporate-apology phrase, matching today's own 今日の会議の内容は重かった sense of "serious."
items.unit: Week 6 Day 4 · 甘い・かたい・重い

items.q: 長い人生には、良いときと悪いときの（a.根 b.波）がある。
items.qr: Nagai jinsei ni wa, yoi toki to warui toki no (a. ne b. nami) ga aru.
items.en: In a long life, there are ups and downs.
items.hi: लंबी ज़िंदगी में अच्छे और बुरे वक़्त की लहरें आती रहती हैं।
items.gu: લાંબા જીવનમાં સારા-ખરાબ સમયનાં મોજાં આવતાં રહે છે.
items.why: 波がある ("to have waves/ups and downs") describes fluctuation over time, matching 感情に波がある in today's list.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 5 · 強い・ばか・あと

items.q: 今日の授業は（a.重く b.ばかに）難しかったね。
items.qr: Kyou no jugyou wa (a. omoku b. baka ni) muzukashikatta ne.
items.en: Today's class was awfully difficult, wasn't it.
items.hi: आज की क्लास बेहद मुश्किल थी, है ना।
items.gu: આજનો વર્ગ ખૂબ જ અઘરો હતો, નહીં?
items.why: ばかに + adjective means "extremely," matching today's own 今日はばかに寒い example.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 5 · 強い・ばか・あと

items.q: ホテルを（a.後に回して b.後にして）駅へ向かった。
items.qr: Hoteru o (a. ato ni mawashite b. ato ni shite) eki e mukatta.
items.en: I left the hotel and headed for the station.
items.hi: होटल छोड़कर स्टेशन की ओर निकल पड़ा।
items.gu: હોટેલ છોડીને સ્ટેશન તરફ ગયો.

opts.en: postponing (wrong meaning — you can't "postpone" a hotel)

items.why: ～を後にする means "to leave (a place)," matching today's own 故郷を後にする example.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 5 · 強い・ばか・あと

items.q: 通うのはいいが、交通費がバカに（a.ならない b.なる）。
items.qr: Kayou no wa ii ga, koutsuuhi ga baka ni (a. naranai b. naru).
items.en: Commuting is fine, but the transportation cost isn't negligible.
items.hi: आना-जाना ठीक है, पर किराया कोई मामूली रक़म नहीं है।
items.gu: અવરજવર ઠીક છે, પણ ભાડું નજીવું નથી.

opts.en: becomes (wrong — this would flip the meaning to "the cost becomes negligible")

items.why: バカにならない (negative form) is the fixed idiom for a cost/effect that turns out to be more significant than expected.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 5 · 強い・ばか・あと

items.q: その病原菌の（a.ばか力 b.息の根）を止める新薬が発明された。
items.qr: Sono byougenkin no (a. baka-jikara b. iki no ne) o tomeru shinyaku ga hatsumei sareta.
items.en: A new drug was invented that completely wipes out that pathogen.
items.hi: उस रोगाणु का पूरी तरह ख़ात्मा करने वाली नई दवा बनाई गई।
items.gu: તે રોગાણુનો સંપૂર્ણ નાશ કરતી નવી દવા શોધાઈ.

opts.en: the root of breath — "to completely finish off"

items.why: 息の根を止める ("to stop the root of one's breath") is the fixed idiom for completely destroying/eliminating something, extended here to wiping out a pathogen.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 5 · 強い・ばか・あと

items.q: 昔のことをいつまでも（a.根に持つ b.後を継ぐ）のはやめましょう。
items.qr: Mukashi no koto o itsu made mo (a. ne ni motsu b. ato o tsugu) no wa yamemashou.
items.en: Let's stop holding onto grudges about the past forever.
items.hi: पुरानी बातों का बदला हमेशा मन में रखना बंद करें।
items.gu: જૂની વાતોનો કાયમ મનમાં ડંખ રાખવાનું બંધ કરીએ.
items.why: 根に持つ is the fixed idiom for holding onto a grudge, matching today's own example.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 5 · 強い・ばか・あと

items.q: 警官はその不審な男の（ ）。
items.qr: Keikan wa sono fushin na otoko no (___).
items.en: The police officer tailed the suspicious man.
items.hi: पुलिस अधिकारी ने उस संदिग्ध आदमी का पीछा किया।
items.gu: પોલીસ અધિકારીએ તે શંકાસ્પદ માણસનો પીછો કર્યો.
items.why: 後をつける ("to tail/secretly follow") is the fixed idiom for surveillance, matching today's own 彼の後をつける example.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 5 · 強い・ばか・あと

items.q: 正直者が（ ）社会であるべきだ。
items.qr: Shoujiki-mono ga (___) shakai de aru beki da.
items.en: Society should be one where honest people don't end up as the ones who lose out.
items.hi: समाज ऐसा होना चाहिए जहाँ ईमानदार लोगों को नुक़सान न उठाना पड़े।
items.gu: સમાજ એવો હોવો જોઈએ જ્યાં પ્રામાણિક લોકોને નુકસાન ન થાય.

opts.en: becomes useless/stripped (wrong meaning — that's for screws, not people)
loses out (wrong polarity — the sentence needs the negative)

items.why: バカを見る ("to end up as the loser/sucker") negated as バカを見ない fits "a society where honest people AREN'T the ones who lose out" — matching today's own 自分だけがばかを見る example.
items.unit: Week 6 Day 5 · 強い・ばか・あと

items.q: 首相はきちんと（a.筋の入った b.筋の通った）説明をした。
items.qr: Shushou wa kichinto (a. suji no haitta b. suji no tootta) setsumei o shita.
items.en: The prime minister gave a properly logical explanation.
items.hi: प्रधानमंत्री ने ठीक ढंग से तर्कसंगत स्पष्टीकरण दिया।
items.gu: વડાપ્રધાને બરાબર તાર્કિક ખુલાસો આપ્યો.

opts.en: having a streak/line in it (wrong meaning — a physical streak, not logic)

items.why: 筋が通る ("to be logical") is the fixed idiom for a coherent explanation.

items.q: 工事はだいぶ（a.先へ b.道を）進んだ。
items.qr: Kouji wa daibu (a. saki e b. michi o) susunda.
items.en: Construction has progressed quite far.
items.hi: निर्माण कार्य काफ़ी आगे बढ़ गया है।
items.gu: બાંધકામ ઘણું આગળ વધ્યું છે.

opts.en: wrong particle/word — 道を進む needs no 先 competing here, and idiomatically "progress" uses 先へ進む

items.why: 先へ進む ("to advance forward") is the fixed phrase for progress, matching today's own 目的地を目指して先へ進む example.

items.q: （a.話の先 b.話の種）に、新しくできたレストランに食べに行ってみた。
items.qr: (a. Hanashi no saki b. Hanashi no tane) ni, atarashiku dekita resutoran ni tabe ni itte mita.
items.en: As something to talk about, I went to try the newly opened restaurant.
items.hi: बातचीत के लिए एक विषय बनाने की ख़ातिर, नए खुले रेस्तराँ में खाना खाने गया।
items.gu: વાતચીતનો વિષય બનાવવા, નવી ખૂલેલી રેસ્ટોરાંમાં જમવા ગયો.

opts.en: the rest/continuation of a story (wrong meaning)

items.why: 話の種に ("as conversation material/a topic to talk about") describes doing something specifically to have something to talk about later — see Confusion Pairs for how this differs from 話の先.

items.q: 犯人の（a.筋 b.当たり）をつけて、捜査を開始した。
items.qr: Hannin no (a. suji b. atari) o tsukete, sousa o kaishi shita.
items.en: They made a guess about the culprit and began the investigation.
items.hi: अपराधी का अंदाज़ा लगाकर जाँच शुरू की।
items.gu: ગુનેગારનો અંદાજ લગાવીને તપાસ શરૂ કરી.
items.why: 当たりをつける ("to make a guess/get a lead") is the fixed idiom for narrowing in on a suspect before confirming.

items.q: 君は（a.筋 b.人当たり）がいいから、すぐに試合に出ることができるだろう。
items.qr: Kimi wa (a. suji b. hitoatari) ga ii kara, sugu ni shiai ni deru koto ga dekiru darou.
items.en: You've got talent, so you'll probably be able to compete soon.
items.hi: तुम्हारे अंदर प्रतिभा है, इसलिए जल्द ही मुक़ाबले में उतर पाओगे।
items.gu: તારામાં આવડત છે, તેથી જલદી હરીફાઈમાં ભાગ લઈ શકીશ.

opts.en: a friendly manner (wrong meaning — describes personality, not sporting talent)

items.why: 筋がいい ("to have natural aptitude") describes talent at a skill; 人当たりがいい describes being pleasant to interact with — unrelated qualities that both use "がいい."

items.q: 一人前の医者になるまでの（a.道 b.筋）は長いですよ。
items.qr: Ichininmae no isha ni naru made no (a. michi b. suji) wa nagai desu yo.
items.en: The road to becoming a full-fledged doctor is long.
items.hi: एक पूरा डॉक्टर बनने तक का रास्ता लंबा है।
items.gu: પૂરેપૂરો ડૉક્ટર બનવા સુધીનો રસ્તો લાંબો છે.
items.why: ～への道 ("the path to ~") is the standard metaphor for the process/journey toward a long-term goal.

items.q: ラッシュアワーの時間、乗客は（ ）を争って電車に乗ったり降りたりしている。
items.qr: Rasshu awaa no jikan, joukyaku wa (___) o arasotte densha ni nottari oritari shite iru.
items.en: During rush hour, passengers compete to be first getting on and off the train.
items.hi: व्यस्त समय में यात्री सबसे पहले चढ़ने-उतरने की होड़ में लगे रहते हैं।
items.gu: ભીડના સમયે મુસાફરો સૌથી પહેલાં ચઢવા-ઊતરવાની હોડમાં હોય છે.
items.why: 先を争う ("to compete to be first") is the fixed idiom, matching today's own 先を争って電車から降りる example.

items.q: 彼は、麻薬に手を出すという人の（ ）に外れたことをした。
items.qr: Kare wa, mayaku ni te o dasu to iu hito no (___) ni hazureta koto o shita.
items.en: He did something that strayed from the path of humanity — using drugs.
items.hi: उसने नशीली दवाओं का सेवन करके इंसानियत की राह से भटकने वाला काम किया।
items.gu: તેણે ડ્રગ્સનો ઉપયોગ કરીને માનવતાના માર્ગથી ભટકી જવાનું કામ કર્યું.
items.why: 人の道に外れる ("to stray from the path of humanity/morality") is the fixed idiom, matching today's own example.

items.q: 彼は芸能界の話題にとても（ ）。
items.qr: Kare wa geinoukai no wadai ni totemo (___).
items.en: He's very knowledgeable about entertainment-industry topics.
items.hi: वह मनोरंजन जगत की बातों की गहरी जानकारी रखता है।
items.gu: તે મનોરંજન જગતની બાબતોની ઊંડી જાણકારી ધરાવે છે.
items.why: Day 4's 彼は政治に明るい(＝詳しい) shows 明るい's "well-informed about" sense, extending naturally here to entertainment topics.

items.q: 彼女は口は悪いけど（ ）はやさしい人ですよ。
items.qr: Kanojo wa kuchi wa warui kedo (___) wa yasashii hito desu yo.
items.en: She's got a sharp tongue, but deep down she's a kind person.
items.hi: उसकी ज़ुबान तीखी है, पर दिल से वह बहुत भली है।
items.gu: તેની જીભ તીખી છે, પણ મૂળભૂત રીતે તે દયાળુ છે.
items.why: Day 5's 彼は根(＝本来の性質)は正直だ shows 根's "true underlying nature" sense, matching exactly this contrast between outward manner and inner character.

items.q: 息子は頭が少し（ ）。頑固な父親にそっくりだ。
items.qr: Musuko wa atama ga sukoshi (___). Ganko na chichioya ni sokkuri da.
items.en: My son is a bit stubborn — just like his stubborn father.
items.hi: बेटा थोड़ा ज़िद्दी है, बिल्कुल अपने ज़िद्दी पिता जैसा।
items.gu: દીકરો થોડો હઠીલો છે, બિલકુલ પોતાના હઠીલા પિતા જેવો.
items.why: Day 4's 頭がかたい(＝頑固だ) is the exact idiom for stubbornness, and 頑固な父親 in the second sentence confirms it.

items.q: うまい話に（ ）ように気をつけよう。
items.qr: Umai hanashi ni (___) you ni ki o tsukeyou.
items.en: Let's be careful not to fall for offers that sound too good.
items.hi: लुभावने प्रस्तावों के झांसे में न आने का ध्यान रखें।
items.gu: લોભામણી ઑફરની જાળમાં ન ફસાવાનું ધ્યાન રાખીએ.
items.why: Day 2's その手には乗らない shows 乗る's "fall for/buy into" sense, extending naturally to a suspiciously good offer.

items.q: 何回も振り込みをすると、手数料が（ ）。
items.qr: Nankai mo furikomi o suru to, tesuuryou ga (___).
items.en: If you make transfers many times, the fees add up to a non-negligible amount.
items.hi: बार-बार पैसे ट्रांसफ़र करने पर, शुल्क कोई मामूली रक़म नहीं बनता।
items.gu: વારંવાર ટ્રાન્સફર કરવાથી, ફી નજીવી રકમ નથી રહેતી.

opts.en: strips/wears out (wrong sense — for screws, not fees)
ends up losing out (wrong sense — for people, not fees)

items.why: Day 5's 交通費がバカにならない is the exact same construction, now with 手数料 (fees) instead of 交通費 (transport costs).

items.q: もう遅いので、後は明日に（ ）今日は帰りましょう。
items.qr: Mou osoi node, ato wa ashita ni (___) kyou wa kaerimashou.
items.en: It's already late, so let's leave the rest for tomorrow and head home today.
items.hi: काफ़ी देर हो गई है, इसलिए बाक़ी काम कल के लिए टालकर आज घर चलते हैं।
items.gu: ઘણું મોડું થયું છે, તેથી બાકીનું કામ કાલ પર ઠેલીને આજે ઘરે જઈએ.
items.why: Day 2's 仕事を明日に回す is the exact idiom for postponing a task, matching "後は明日に回す" here.

items.q: もう少しスピードを出していたら、大事故に（ ）ところだった。
items.qr: Mou sukoshi supiido o dashite itara, daijiko ni (___) tokoro datta.
items.en: If I had driven a bit faster, it would have led to a serious accident.
items.hi: थोड़ी और तेज़ रफ़्तार होती तो बड़ी दुर्घटना हो सकती थी।
items.gu: થોડી વધુ ઝડપ હોત તો મોટો અકસ્માત થઈ શકતો હતો.
items.why: Day 1's 事件につながる人物 and もうけにつながる話 show つながる's "lead to (a bad/notable outcome)" sense, exactly matching a near-miss leading to a serious accident.

items.q: 妻は、私が昔、浮気をしたことを、いまだに（ ）に持っているようだ。
items.qr: Tsuma wa, watashi ga mukashi, uwaki o shita koto o, imada ni (___) ni motte iru you da.
items.en: It seems my wife still holds a grudge about my affair from long ago.
items.hi: लगता है पत्नी को अब भी मेरे पुराने विश्वासघात की बात का मलाल है।
items.gu: લાગે છે કે પત્નીને હજુ પણ મારા જૂના બેવફાઈના કિસ્સાનો ડંખ છે.
items.why: Day 5's 彼は昔のことを根に持っている is the exact fixed idiom for holding a long-term grudge.

items.q: 子どもの学費の支払いでボーナスが（ ）しまった。
items.qr: Kodomo no gakuhi no shiharai de boonasu ga (___) shimatta.
items.en: My bonus vanished paying for my child's school fees.
items.hi: बच्चे की फ़ीस भरने में बोनस उड़ गया।
items.gu: બાળકની ફી ભરવામાં બોનસ ઊડી ગયો.
items.why: Day 3's ローンの返済でボーナスが飛ぶ(＝消えてなくなる) is the exact same idiom, now with school fees instead of loan repayments.

items.q: 社長が逮捕されてしまって、とてもショックを（ ）。
items.qr: Shachou ga taiho sarete shimatte, totemo shokku o (___).
items.en: I was very shocked that the company president was arrested.
items.hi: अध्यक्ष के गिरफ़्तार होने से मुझे बहुत सदमा लगा।
items.gu: પ્રમુખની ધરપકડ થવાથી મને ખૂબ આઘાત લાગ્યો.
items.why: Day 1's ショックを受ける is the fixed collocation for "to be shocked."

items.q: 素質がいい。 ("To have good natural aptitude.")
items.qr: Soshitsu ga ii.

opts.en: not a standard phrase in this sense (wrong word)

items.why: Day 6's 筋(＝素質)がいい is precisely "to have good natural aptitude/talent."

items.q: 方法。 ("A method/way of doing something.")
items.qr: Houhou.
items.why: Day 6's お金の使い道(＝使う方法) shows 道's "method/way" sense exactly.

items.q: 次々に起こる。 ("To happen one after another.")
items.qr: Tsugitsugi ni okoru.
items.why: Day 5's 事故が後を絶たない(＝次々に起こる) is this week's exact definition, word for word.

items.q: よい結果が表れる。 ("A good result appears/comes to fruition.")
items.qr: Yoi kekka ga arawareru.

opts.en: to bear fruit, to pay off
not a real phrase in this sense (wrong word)

items.why: Day 3's 長年の努力が実を結ぶ(＝形になる) is the fixed idiom for effort finally producing a good result.

items.q: 見た目などを実際以上によく見せようとする。 ("To try to make one's appearance look better than it really is.")
items.qr: Mitame nado o jissai ijou ni yoku miseyou to suru.

opts.en: to be proud (wrong meaning — pride, not fake appearance)

items.why: Day 3's 見栄を張る is precisely "to make things look better/grander than they really are."

items.q: ここでは都合が悪いから、別の場所で話そう。
items.u: 都合が悪い / tsugou ga warui
items.qr: Koko de wa tsugou ga warui kara, betsu no basho de hanasou.
items.en: It's inconvenient here, so let's talk somewhere else.
items.why: Day 4's まずい(＝都合が悪い) is the exact match for "inconvenient/awkward."

items.q: 彼は、自分からやめて、後輩に仕事を譲った。
items.u: 自分からやめて / jibun kara yamete
items.qr: Kare wa, jibun kara yamete, kouhai ni shigoto o yuzutta.
items.en: He resigned on his own and handed the work to his junior.
items.why: Day 2's 身を引く(＝退く) is the exact match for voluntarily stepping back from a position.

items.q: 手品の仕掛けがばれた。
items.qr: Tejina no shikake ga bareta.
items.en: The trick behind the magic was found out.
items.why: Day 6's 手品の種(＝仕掛け) is the exact match for the hidden mechanism behind a magic trick.

items.q: わがチームの優勝は間違いないでしょう。
items.qr: Waga chiimu no yuushou wa machigainai deshou.
items.en: Our team's victory is certain.
items.why: Day 4's 彼の合格はかたい(＝確実だ) shows かたい's "certain, sure to happen" sense, matching "victory is certain" here.

items.q: 授業料のことを考えると憂うつだ。
items.qr: Jugyouryou no koto o kangaeru to yuuutsu da.
items.en: Thinking about the tuition fees makes me feel gloomy.

opts.en: foggy-headed (wrong meaning — physical grogginess, not emotional gloom)
weighs on one's mind (close, but describes lingering worry, not the specific idiom tested)

items.why: Day 4's その仕事を断るのは気が重い(＝憂うつだ) is this week's own definition of 気が重い as "gloomy/reluctant," matching 憂うつ directly.

items.q: 波
items.qr: nami

opts.t: 彼は授業の波に乗って、すらすら答えた。
opts.r: Kare wa jugyou no nami ni notte, surasura kotaeta.
opts.en: "He rode the wave of class and answered smoothly" — nonsensical collocation; 波に乗る doesn't pair with "class"

opts.t: その会社は不況の波を受けてついに倒産してしまった。
opts.r: Sono kaisha wa fukyou no nami o ukete tsui ni tousan shite shimatta.
opts.en: That company was hit by the wave of the recession and finally went bankrupt.

opts.t: セールスマンの波に乗らないように気をつけてください。
opts.r: Seerusuman no nami ni noranai you ni ki o tsukete kudasai.
opts.en: "Be careful not to ride the salesman's wave" — wrong; a salesman's pitch needs 誘いに乗る, not 波に乗る

opts.t: 台風の被害には波がいろいろある。
opts.r: Taifuu no higai ni wa nami ga iroiro aru.
opts.en: "There are various waves to typhoon damage" — wrong; different kinds/degrees of damage need 種類, not 波

items.why: 不況の波を受ける ("to be hit by the wave of a recession") extends this week's own 国際化の波に乗る(＝傾向に従う) pattern to a company being swept up by an economic downturn; 1, 3, and 4 each force 波 into a collocation it doesn't take.

items.q: すべる
items.qr: suberu

opts.t: コップを手ですべって、落としてしまった。
opts.r: Koppu o te de subette, otoshite shimatta.
opts.en: "The cup slipped with the hand and I dropped it" — grammatically malformed; 滑る is intransitive and needs 手が滑って (the hand as subject), not 手で

opts.t: つい舌がすべってしまい、うそがばれてしまった。
opts.r: Tsui shita ga subette shimai, uso ga barete shimatta.
opts.en: My tongue accidentally slipped and my lie was found out.

opts.t: 湖水の上を白鳥がすべるように泳いでいる。
opts.r: Kosui no ue o hakuchou ga suberu you ni oyoide iru.
opts.en: Grammatically fine as a simile ("gliding smoothly"), but doesn't test any of this week's taught senses of 滑る the way the other options do

opts.t: 試験の時間にすべるように、落ち着いてください。
opts.r: Shiken no jikan ni suberu you ni, ochitsuite kudasai.
opts.en: Self-contradictory — should be すべらないように ("so that you DON'T fail"), not すべるように

items.why: つい舌が滑る ("one's tongue slips") is a natural everyday variant of Day 1's つい口が滑ってしまった — both describe accidentally blurting something out; 1 breaks the verb's grammar, 4 says the opposite of what it means, and 3, while valid Japanese, is a decorative simile rather than one of this week's core taught senses.

items.q: 通る
items.qr: tooru

opts.t: 彼の主張は、一応、筋が通っている。
opts.r: Kare no shuchou wa, ichiou, suji ga tootte iru.
opts.en: His argument is, at least, logically coherent.

opts.t: 彼は恋人の肩に手を通した。
opts.r: Kare wa koibito no kata ni te o tooshita.
opts.en: "He passed his hand through his girlfriend's shoulder" — wrong verb; putting an arm around someone needs 回した (Day 2's 肩に手を回す), not 通した

opts.t: 車で駅まで通っていきましょう。
opts.r: Kuruma de eki made tootte ikimashou.
opts.en: "Let's commute by car to the station" — wrong verb; a one-time drive needs 行きましょう or 送っていきましょう, not 通う (regular commuting)

opts.t: わからなかった問題がやっと通った。
opts.en: "The problem I couldn't understand finally passed" — wrong verb; solving a problem needs 解けた (Day 3's とける group), not 通った

items.why: 筋が通る ("to be logically coherent") is Day 2's own example (彼の言うことは筋が通っている) verbatim; 2, 3, and 4 each substitute 通る for a different verb that's actually correct in that context (回す, 行く/送る, 解ける).

items.q: 飛ぶ
items.qr: tobu

opts.t: 扇風機で風が飛んで、涼しくなった。
opts.r: Senpuuki de kaze ga tonde, suzushiku natta.
opts.en: "The fan's wind flew and it got cool" — wrong verb; a fan needs 風を送る (Day 3's 送る group), not 風が飛ぶ

opts.t: 暑さで氷が一気に飛んでしまった。
opts.r: Atsusa de koori ga ikki ni tonde shimatta.
opts.en: "The ice flew away all at once from the heat" — wrong verb; ice needs 溶けて (melted), not 飛んで

opts.t: 年とともに髪の毛が飛んで、はげてきた。
opts.r: Toshi to tomo ni kaminoke ga tonde, hagete kita.
opts.en: "Hair flew away with age, and he went bald" — wrong verb; hair falling out needs 抜けて, not 飛んで

opts.t: ブレーキランプのヒューズが飛んでしまった。
opts.r: Bureeki ranpu no hyuuzu ga tonde shimatta.

items.why: ヒューズが飛ぶ ("a fuse blows") is Day 3's own example verbatim; 1, 2, and 3 each misuse 飛ぶ for wind, melting, and hair loss, which are each covered by a different verb.

items.q: 明るい
items.qr: akarui

opts.t: 彼はとても責任感の明るい人です。
opts.r: Kare wa totemo sekininkan no akarui hito desu.
opts.en: "He's a person with a very bright sense of responsibility" — wrong word; a strong sense of responsibility needs 責任感が強い, not 明るい

opts.t: 父は世界の地理に明るい。
opts.r: Chichi wa sekai no chiri ni akarui.
opts.en: My father is very knowledgeable about world geography.
"This calculation is bright" — nonsensical; a calculation can't be 明るい

opts.t: おじいちゃん、おばあちゃんは孫に明るいものだ。
opts.r: Ojiichan, obaachan wa mago ni akarui mono da.
opts.en: "Grandparents are bright toward their grandchildren" — wrong word; being indulgent toward grandchildren needs 甘い (Day 4's 孫に甘い-type usage), not 明るい

items.why: 政治に明るい-type usage from Day 4 (彼は政治に明るい＝詳しい) extends directly to 世界の地理に明るい ("well-informed about world geography"); 1, 3, and 4 each substitute 明るい where 強い, no adjective at all, and 甘い actually belong.

items.q: 彼が（a.カンニング b.マンネリ）したのは明白だ。
items.qr: Kare ga (a. kanningu b. manneri) shita no wa meihaku da.
items.en: It's obvious that he cheated (on the test).
items.hi: यह साफ़ है कि उसने नक़ल की।
items.gu: એ સ્પષ્ટ છે કે તેણે ચોરી કરી.
items.why: カンニング is the fixed word for exam cheating; マンネリ describes something growing stale through repetition, not dishonest behavior.

items.q: 会議でパソコンを使って（a.カンパ b.プレゼン）をした。
items.qr: Kaigi de pasokon o tsukatte (a. kanpa b. purezen) o shita.
items.en: I gave a presentation using a computer at the meeting.
items.hi: मीटिंग में कंप्यूटर का इस्तेमाल करके प्रस्तुति दी।
items.gu: મીટિંગમાં કમ્પ્યુટરનો ઉપયોગ કરીને પ્રેઝન્ટેશન આપ્યું.
items.why: プレゼン (presentation) is what one does with a computer in a meeting; カンパ is about collecting money, unrelated here.

items.q: これは（a.エコ b.バイオ）の技術を利用して作った害虫に強い野菜です。
items.qr: Kore wa (a. eko b. baio) no gijutsu o riyou shite tsukutta gaichuu ni tsuyoi yasai desu.
items.en: This is a pest-resistant vegetable made using bio-technology.
items.hi: यह जैव-तकनीक का उपयोग करके बनाई गई कीट-प्रतिरोधी सब्ज़ी है।
items.gu: આ બાયો-ટેકનોલોજીનો ઉપયોગ કરીને બનાવેલી જીવાત-પ્રતિરોધક શાકભાજી છે.

opts.en: eco-friendly (wrong field — about environment, not genetics)

items.why: Making a pest-resistant vegetable is a genetic/bio-engineering feat (バイオ), not simply an environmental one (エコ).

items.q: 会社を（a.セクハラ b.リストラ）されたらどうしよう。
items.qr: Kaisha o (a. sekuhara b. risutora) saretara dou shiyou.
items.en: What will I do if I get laid off from the company?
items.hi: अगर कंपनी से निकाल दिया गया तो क्या करूँगा?
items.gu: જો કંપનીમાંથી કાઢી મુકાય તો શું કરીશ?
items.why: 会社をリストラされる is the fixed pattern for being laid off due to restructuring; セクハラ is unrelated to job loss.

items.q: 彼はとても時間に（a.スムーズ b.ルーズ）だ。
items.qr: Kare wa totemo jikan ni (a. sumuuzu b. ruuzu) da.
items.en: He's very unpunctual about time.
items.hi: वह समय के मामले में बहुत लापरवाह है।
items.gu: તે સમય બાબતે ખૂબ બેદરકાર છે.
items.why: 時間にルーズ is the fixed phrase for being unpunctual; スムーズ describes how smoothly something proceeds, not a person's habits.

items.q: エコカーには（a.ゼネコン b.ハイテク）技術がたくさん使われている。
items.qr: Ekokaa ni wa (a. zenekon b. haiteku) gijutsu ga takusan tsukawarete iru.
items.en: A lot of high-tech technology is used in eco-friendly cars.
items.hi: पर्यावरण-अनुकूल कारों में बहुत-सी उच्च-तकनीक का इस्तेमाल होता है।
items.gu: પર્યાવરણ-અનુકૂળ કારમાં ઘણી ઉચ્ચ-ટેકનોલોજીનો ઉપયોગ થાય છે.

opts.en: a general contractor (wrong meaning — a company, not a technology)

items.why: ハイテク技術 ("high-tech technology") is the natural collocation; ゼネコン names a type of construction company, not a kind of technology.

items.q: いいマンションだが、交通の便の悪さが（ ）になって、借り手がいない。
items.qr: Ii manshon da ga, koutsuu no ben no warusa ga (___) ni natte, karite ga inai.
items.en: It's a nice apartment, but poor transport access is the sticking point, so there are no tenants.
items.hi: फ़्लैट अच्छा है, पर आने-जाने की असुविधा ही सबसे बड़ी रुकावट बनी हुई है, इसलिए कोई किराएदार नहीं मिल रहा।
items.gu: ફ્લેટ સારો છે, પણ અવરજવરની અગવડ જ સૌથી મોટો અવરોધ બની છે, એટલે કોઈ ભાડુઆત મળતું નથી.

opts.en: a handicap (close in feel, but not the fixed word for "the one problem holding something back")
