items.why: ～がネックになる ("~ becomes the bottleneck") is the fixed idiom for the one factor blocking otherwise-good conditions.

items.q: ハリウッドスターの（ ）はとても高い。
items.qr: Hariuddo sutaa no (___) wa totemo takai.
items.en: A Hollywood star's fee is very high.
items.hi: हॉलीवुड स्टार की फ़ीस बहुत ज़्यादा होती है।
items.gu: હોલિવૂડ સ્ટારની ફી ખૂબ ઊંચી હોય છે.
items.why: ギャラ is the fixed word for a performer's pay/fee — exactly what's high for a Hollywood star.

items.q: 彼女は顔と声にずいぶん（a.シャープ b.ギャップ）があるね。
items.qr: Kanojo wa kao to koe ni zuibun (a. shaapu b. gyappu) ga aru ne.
items.en: There's quite a gap between her face and her voice, isn't there.
items.hi: उसके चेहरे और आवाज़ में काफ़ी फ़र्क़ है, है ना।
items.gu: તેના ચહેરા અને અવાજ વચ્ચે ઘણો ફરક છે, ખરું ને.
items.why: ギャップ describes a mismatch between two impressions (here: face vs. voice); シャープ describes clarity/sharpness, unrelated to contrast.

items.q: （a.バブルがはじけて b.ブレイクして）、経済は落ち込んだ。
items.qr: (a. Baburu ga hajikete b. Bureiku shite), keizai wa ochikonda.
items.en: The bubble burst, and the economy declined.
items.hi: बुलबुला फूटा और अर्थव्यवस्था गिर गई।
items.gu: પરપોટો ફૂટ્યો અને અર્થતંત્ર કથળ્યું.

opts.en: had a hit (wrong meaning — describes success, not a crash)

items.why: バブルがはじける is the fixed idiom for an economic bubble collapsing; ブレイク describes a breakthrough hit, the opposite of decline.

items.q: （a.タイトな b.ラフな）格好で行ってもいいでしょうか。
items.qr: (a. Taito na b. Rafu na) kakkou de itte mo ii deshou ka.
items.en: Would it be okay to go in casual clothes?
items.hi: क्या मैं कैज़ुअल कपड़ों में जा सकता/सकती हूँ?
items.gu: શું હું કેઝ્યુઅલ કપડાંમાં જઈ શકું?
items.why: ラフな格好 is the fixed phrase for casual attire; タイト describes fit/tightness, not formality level.

items.q: 優勝のかかった最後の試合だから、かなりの（a.トラウマ b.プレッシャー）だ。
items.qr: Yuushou no kakatta saigo no shiai da kara, kanari no (a. torauma b. puresshaa) da.
items.en: Since it's the final match with the championship on the line, it's quite a lot of pressure.
items.hi: चूँकि यह चैंपियनशिप तय करने वाला आख़िरी मुक़ाबला है, इसका दबाव काफ़ी ज़्यादा है।
items.gu: આ ચેમ્પિયનશિપ નક્કી કરતી છેલ્લી મેચ છે, એટલે તેનું દબાણ ઘણું છે.

opts.en: trauma (wrong meaning — describes a past wound, not present stress)

items.why: プレッシャーがかかる describes the stress of a high-stakes situation happening now; トラウマ describes lasting psychological damage from a past event.

items.q: （a.セキュリティー b.アフターサービス）対策は十分にしてあります。
items.qr: (a. Sekyuritii b. Afutaa-saabisu) taisaku wa juubun ni shite arimasu.
items.en: Security measures are thoroughly in place.
items.hi: सुरक्षा के इंतज़ाम पूरी तरह से किए गए हैं।
items.gu: સુરક્ષાની વ્યવસ્થા સંપૂર્ણ રીતે કરવામાં આવી છે.
items.why: セキュリティー対策 ("security measures") is the fixed collocation; アフターサービス is about post-purchase support, unrelated to protection/safety.

items.q: ふかふかで（a.アットホーム b.ソフト）な肌触りの毛布を買った。
items.qr: Fukafuka de (a. atto hoomu b. sofuto) na hadazawari no moufu o katta.
items.en: I bought a fluffy, soft-textured blanket.
items.hi: मैंने एक मुलायम/नर्म बनावट वाला रोएँदार कंबल ख़रीदा।
items.gu: મેં એક નરમ સ્પર્શવાળું રુવાંટીદાર ધાબળો ખરીદ્યો.

opts.en: cozy/homey (wrong sense — describes atmosphere, not texture)

items.why: ソフトな肌触り describes a physically soft texture; アットホーム describes the feel of a place/atmosphere, not fabric.

items.q: 新型の車両は、より（ ）なデザインになった。
items.qr: Shingata no sharyou wa, yori (___) na dezain ni natta.
items.en: The new model has a sharper design.
items.hi: नए मॉडल की डिज़ाइन ज़्यादा तीखी/शार्प हो गई है।
items.gu: નવા મોડેલની ડિઝાઇન વધુ શાર્પ બની છે.
items.why: シャープなデザイン ("a sharp/crisp design") is the natural collocation for a sleek, refined product look.

items.q: （ ）があまりにもきつかったので、営業の仕事をやめました。
items.qr: (___) ga amari ni mo kitsukatta node, eigyou no shigoto o yamemashita.
items.en: The quota was too tough, so I quit my sales job.
items.hi: कोटा बहुत सख़्त था, इसलिए मैंने सेल्स की नौकरी छोड़ दी।
items.gu: ક્વોટા બહુ કડક હતો, એટલે મેં સેલ્સની નોકરી છોડી દીધી.
items.why: ノルマがきつい ("the quota is tough") is the natural fit for a sales job someone quit; the others don't fit "quitting because of a demand placed on you at work."

items.q: 注意したら、彼は突然（a.キレた b.サボった）。
items.qr: Chuui shitara, kare wa totsuzen (a. kireta b. sabotta).
items.en: When I warned him, he suddenly snapped/lost his temper.
items.hi: जब मैंने उसे टोका, तो वह अचानक भड़क उठा।
items.gu: મેં તેને ટોક્યો ત્યારે તે અચાનક ભડકી ઊઠ્યો.
items.why: キレる describes a sudden emotional outburst — exactly what happens when someone reacts badly to being warned; サボる is about avoiding a duty, unrelated to anger.

items.q: ワープロのソフトを1.0から2.0に（a.グレードアップ b.バージョンアップ）した。
items.qr: Waapuro no sofuto o 1.0 kara 2.0 ni (a. gureedo appu b. baajon appu) shita.
items.en: I upgraded the word-processing software from version 1.0 to 2.0.
items.hi: मैंने वर्ड-प्रोसेसिंग सॉफ़्टवेयर को 1.0 से 2.0 में अपग्रेड किया।
items.gu: મેં વર્ડ-પ્રોસેસિંગ સોફ્ટવેરને 1.0 થી 2.0 માં અપગ્રેડ કર્યું.

opts.en: upgrading to pricier items (wrong meaning for software versions)

items.why: バージョンアップ specifically describes a software/version upgrade; グレードアップ is about moving up to a higher-grade/pricier item, not version numbers.

items.q: スリーサイズを計って（a.ワンパターン b.オーダーメイド）のスーツを作った。
items.qr: Surii saizu o hakatte (a. wanpataan b. oodaa meido) no suutsu o tsukutta.
items.en: I had a custom-made suit made after measuring my three sizes.
items.hi: तीनों माप लेकर एक कस्टम-मेड सूट बनवाया।
items.gu: ત્રણેય માપ લઈને એક કસ્ટમ-મેડ સૂટ બનાવડાવ્યો.

opts.en: one-track/repetitive (wrong meaning — describes a personality trait, not tailoring)

items.why: Measuring someone's sizes to make a suit is the definition of オーダーメイド (custom tailoring); ワンパターン describes a lack of variation in behavior/thinking.

items.q: 私は不運な経験が多いせいか、物事を（a.プラス b.マイナス）に考えられなくなっています。
items.qr: Watashi wa fu'un na keiken ga ooi sei ka, monogoto o (a. purasu b. mainasu) ni kangaerarenaku natte imasu.
items.en: Perhaps because I've had so many unlucky experiences, I've become unable to think of things positively.
items.hi: शायद इतने सारे बदक़िस्मत अनुभवों की वजह से, मैं चीज़ों को सकारात्मक ढंग से सोच नहीं पा रहा/रही।
items.gu: કદાચ ઘણા બધા કમનસીબ અનુભવોના કારણે, હું બાબતોને હકારાત્મક રીતે વિચારી શકતો/શકતી નથી.
items.why: 考えられなくなっている ("have become unable to think ~") signals loss of a previous positive ability — so the blank names the ability lost: プラスに考える ("to think positively"), not マイナス.

items.q: 雑誌に彼女が2歳年下の医師と来春（a.Uターン b.ゴールイン）するという記事が載っていた。
items.qr: Zasshi ni kanojo ga nisai toshishita no ishi to raishun (a. yuu taan b. gooru in) suru to iu kiji ga notte ita.
items.en: A magazine ran an article saying she'll marry a doctor two years her junior next spring.
items.hi: पत्रिका में यह ख़बर छपी थी कि वह अगले वसंत में अपने से 2 साल छोटे डॉक्टर से शादी करेगी।
items.gu: મેગેઝિનમાં એવા સમાચાર છપાયા હતા કે તે આવતી વસંતમાં પોતાનાથી 2 વર્ષ નાના ડૉક્ટર સાથે લગ્ન કરશે.

opts.en: a U-turn/return to one's hometown (wrong meaning here)

items.why: ゴールインする used with a romantic partner is the fixed figurative expression for getting married; Uターン is about geographic return, unrelated to marriage.

items.q: 私は休日に、パソコンを使う（a.フリーター b.サイドビジネス）をしています。
items.qr: Watashi wa kyuujitsu ni, pasokon o tsukau (a. furiitaa b. saido bijinesu) o shite imasu.
items.en: On my days off, I run a computer-based side business.
items.hi: मैं छुट्टी के दिन कंप्यूटर के ज़रिए एक साइड बिज़नेस करता/करती हूँ।
items.gu: હું રજાના દિવસે કમ્પ્યુટર દ્વારા એક સાઇડ બિઝનેસ કરું છું.

opts.en: a job-hopping part-timer (a person, not an activity — grammatically wrong here)

items.why: サイドビジネスをする ("to run/do a side business") fits the verb する; フリーター names a type of worker, not an activity one "does" this way.

items.q: ご購入いただいた方には、さらに（ ）の特典が付きますよ。
items.qr: Gokounyuu itadaita kata ni wa, sarani (___) no tokuten ga tsukimasu yo.
items.en: Customers who purchase will also get an extra bonus on top.
items.hi: जो ग्राहक ख़रीदेंगे, उन्हें अतिरिक्त बोनस भी मिलेगा।
items.gu: જે ગ્રાહકો ખરીદશે તેમને વધારાનું બોનસ પણ મળશે.

opts.en: lip service (wrong meaning — implies insincerity, not a real bonus)

items.why: プラスアルファの特典 ("a little something extra as a perk") is exactly the promotional phrase for a bonus added on top of a purchase.

items.q: 同じ本を2冊（ ）買ってしまった。
items.qr: Onaji hon o nisatsu (___) katte shimatta.
items.en: I ended up buying two copies of the same book by mistake.
items.hi: ग़लती से एक ही किताब की दो कॉपियाँ ख़रीद लीं।
items.gu: ભૂલથી એક જ પુસ્તકની બે નકલો ખરીદાઈ ગઈ.

opts.en: duplicating, ending up with two of the same
seriously/for real (an adverb, not a verb — grammatically wrong here)

items.why: ダブる describes accidentally ending up with a duplicate of something — exactly buying two copies of the same book unintentionally.

items.q: 花火を（a.打ち明けた b.打ち上げた）。
items.qr: Hanabi o (a. uchiaketa b. uchiageta).
items.en: We set off fireworks.
items.hi: हमने आतिशबाज़ी छोड़ी।
items.gu: અમે ફટાકડા છોડ્યા.
items.why: 打ち上げる is the fixed verb for launching fireworks or a rocket into the sky; 打ち明ける is about revealing a secret.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 4 · 組み合わせの言葉①

items.q: 借金を強引に（a.取り立てられた b.引き立てられた）。
items.qr: Shakkin o gouin ni (a. toritaterareta b. hikitaterareta).
items.en: The debt was forcibly collected from me.
items.hi: ज़बरदस्ती मुझसे क़र्ज़ वसूला गया।
items.gu: બળજબરીથી મારી પાસેથી દેવું વસૂલવામાં આવ્યું.
items.why: 取り立てる is the fixed verb for aggressively collecting a debt/tax; 引き立てる means to promote or make someone/something look good — unrelated to money collection.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 4 · 組み合わせの言葉①

items.q: 昨日、その通りで酔っ払い運転の（a.追い出し b.取り締まり）をしていた。
items.qr: Kinou, sono toori de yopparai unten no (a. oidashi b. torishimari) o shite ita.
items.en: Yesterday, they were cracking down on drunk driving on that street.
items.hi: कल उस सड़क पर शराब पीकर गाड़ी चलाने के ख़िलाफ़ कार्रवाई हो रही थी।
items.gu: ગઈકાલે તે રસ્તા પર દારૂ પીને ડ્રાઇવિંગ સામે કડક કાર્યવાહી ચાલી રહી હતી.

opts.en: kicking out (wrong verb — not what police do to drivers on a street)

items.why: 取り締まり is the fixed word for police enforcement operations like drunk-driving checkpoints.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 4 · 組み合わせの言葉①

items.q: 北海道から評判のチョコレート菓子を（a.受けとめた b.取り寄せた）。
items.qr: Hokkaidou kara hyouban no chokoreeto kashi o (a. uketometa b. toriyoseta).
items.en: I ordered some famous chocolate confections from Hokkaido.
items.hi: होक्काइदो से मशहूर चॉकलेट मिठाई मँगवाई।
items.gu: હોક્કાઇડોથી પ્રખ્યાત ચોકલેટ મીઠાઈ મંગાવી.
items.why: 取り寄せる is the fixed verb for ordering a product from a distant place to be delivered; 受け止める is about catching or psychologically accepting something.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 4 · 組み合わせの言葉①

items.q: 友人に悩みを（a.打ち明けた b.申し入れた）。
items.qr: Yuujin ni nayami o (a. uchiaketa b. moushiireta).
items.en: I confided my worries to a friend.
items.hi: मैंने दोस्त को अपनी परेशानी दिल खोलकर बताई।
items.gu: મેં મિત્રને મારી ચિંતા ખુલ્લા મનથી કહી.

opts.en: formally proposed/lodged (wrong register — too formal for confiding in a friend)

items.why: 打ち明ける is the natural verb for opening up about personal troubles to someone; 申し入れる is for formal proposals/protests, not personal confessions.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 4 · 組み合わせの言葉①

items.q: 一人の中年女性が列に（a.割り当て b.割り込んで）きた。
items.qr: Hitori no chuunen josei ga retsu ni (a. wariate b. warikonde) kita.
items.en: A middle-aged woman cut into the line.
items.hi: एक अधेड़ महिला लाइन में घुस आई।
items.gu: એક આધેડ સ્ત્રી લાઇનમાં ઘૂસી ગઈ.

opts.en: assignment (a noun, not a verb form fitting here)

items.why: 列に割り込む is the fixed phrase for cutting into a line/queue.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 4 · 組み合わせの言葉①

items.q: その選手は事件を起こして、引退に（ ）。
items.qr: Sono senshu wa jiken o okoshite, intai ni (___).
items.en: That athlete caused an incident and was driven into retirement.
items.hi: उस खिलाड़ी ने एक विवाद खड़ा किया और उसे संन्यास लेने पर मजबूर कर दिया गया।
items.gu: તે ખેલાડીએ વિવાદ સર્જ્યો અને તેને નિવૃત્તિ લેવા મજબૂર કરવામાં આવ્યો.

opts.en: was discontinued (wrong subject — careers aren't "discontinued" this way)
was interrogated (wrong verb — about being questioned, not being forced into retirement)

items.why: 引退に追い込まれる ("be driven/forced into retirement") is the fixed pattern for someone being pressured out of their career by scandal.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 4 · 組み合わせの言葉①

items.q: ゴマ油がこの料理の味を（ ）いる。
items.qr: Gomaabura ga kono ryouri no aji o (___) iru.
items.en: Sesame oil brings out the flavour of this dish.
items.hi: तिल का तेल इस व्यंजन के स्वाद को उभारता है।
items.gu: તલનું તેલ આ વાનગીના સ્વાદને ઉભારે છે.

opts.en: raising (wrong verb — for prices/rates, not flavour)
causing (wrong verb — for problems, not flavour)

items.why: 味を引き立てる is the fixed phrase for an ingredient enhancing a dish's flavour.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 4 · 組み合わせの言葉①

items.q: 首相は政権を途中で（a.抜け出した b.投げ出した）。
items.qr: Shushou wa seiken o tochuu de (a. nukedashita b. nagedashita).
items.en: The prime minister abandoned power midway through his term.
items.hi: प्रधानमंत्री ने कार्यकाल बीच में ही छोड़ दिया।
items.gu: વડાપ્રધાને પોતાનો કાર્યકાળ અધવચ્ચે જ છોડી દીધો.

opts.en: slipped out (wrong nuance — implies sneaking away quietly, not abandoning a duty)

items.why: 投げ出す describes giving up a responsibility partway through; 抜け出す describes physically/quietly leaving a place, not relinquishing a duty.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 5 · 組み合わせの言葉②

items.q: （a.出っ張った b.突っ張った）釘で服が破けてしまった。
items.qr: (a. Deppatta b. Tsuppatta) kugi de fuku ga yaburete shimatta.
items.en: My clothes got torn on a nail that was sticking out.
items.hi: बाहर निकली हुई कील से कपड़ा फट गया।
items.gu: બહાર નીકળેલી ખીલીથી કપડું ફાટી ગયું.

opts.en: tight/tensed (wrong meaning — describes muscle tension, not a protruding object)

items.why: 出っ張る describes something physically protruding/sticking out (like a nail); 突っ張る describes a muscle or surface becoming taut/stretched — see confusion notes below.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 5 · 組み合わせの言葉②

items.q: 売り上げがどんどん（a.引っ込んで b.落ち込んで）いる。
items.qr: Uriage ga dondon (a. hikkonde b. ochikonde) iru.
items.en: Sales are steadily declining.
items.hi: बिक्री लगातार गिरती जा रही है।
items.gu: વેચાણ સતત ઘટી રહ્યું છે.

opts.en: withdrawing/retreating (wrong meaning — describes a person moving away, not numbers declining)

items.why: 落ち込む is the fixed verb for numbers/figures like sales or grades dropping; 引っ込む describes a person withdrawing to somewhere, unrelated to statistics.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 5 · 組み合わせの言葉②

items.q: 名前を呼ばれて（a.折り返したら b.振り返ったら）、山田さんだった。
items.qr: Namae o yobarete (a. orikaeshitara b. furikaettara), Yamada-san datta.
items.en: When I was called by name and turned around, it was Mr./Ms. Yamada.
items.hi: नाम पुकारे जाने पर मुड़कर देखा तो यामादा-सान थे।
items.gu: નામ બોલાવવાથી પાછળ ફરીને જોયું તો યામાડા-સાન હતા.

opts.en: turned back/called back (wrong verb for physically turning around)

items.why: 振り返る is the verb for physically turning to look behind oneself when called; 折り返す is for turning back partway along a route, or calling someone back.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 5 · 組み合わせの言葉②

items.q: ガムを口に（a.持ち込んだ b.放り込んだ）。
items.qr: Gamu o kuchi ni (a. mochikonda b. hourikonda).
items.en: I tossed a piece of gum into my mouth.
items.hi: च्युइंगम मुँह में डाल दिया।
items.gu: ચ્યુઇંગમ મોઢામાં નાખી દીધો.

opts.en: brought in (wrong nuance — implies carrying something into a restricted place, too formal here)

items.why: 放り込む fits the quick, casual motion of popping gum into one's mouth; 持ち込む implies deliberately carrying something into a place, an odd fit for a small casual action like this.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 5 · 組み合わせの言葉②

items.q: 夜中にこっそり家を（a.抜け出して b.放り出して）、遊びに行った。
items.qr: Yonaka ni kossori ie o (a. nukedashite b. houridashite), asobi ni itta.
items.en: I secretly slipped out of the house at midnight and went out to play.
items.hi: आधी रात को चुपके से घर से निकलकर घूमने चला गया।
items.gu: મધરાતે છાનેમાને ઘરેથી નીકળીને રખડવા ગયો.

opts.en: abandoning (wrong meaning — you can't "abandon" a house this way)

items.why: 抜け出す is exactly the verb for secretly slipping away from a place, matching こっそり ("stealthily"); 放り出す means to abandon a duty or throw something out, not to sneak out.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 5 · 組み合わせの言葉②

items.q: 彼はギターの練習に（ ）いる。
items.qr: Kare wa gitaa no renshuu ni (___) iru.
items.en: He's devoting himself wholeheartedly to guitar practice.
items.hi: वह गिटार अभ्यास में पूरी लगन से जुटा है।
items.gu: તે ગિટાર પ્રેક્ટિસમાં પૂરા મનથી ડૂબેલો છે.

opts.en: incorporating (wrong verb — for plans/budgets, not personal effort)
blending in (wrong verb — for fitting into a group, not devoting effort)

items.why: ～に打ち込む is the fixed phrase for pouring one's heart and soul into an activity like guitar practice.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 5 · 組み合わせの言葉②

items.q: このあたりは、海を（ ）作った土地だ。
items.qr: Kono atari wa, umi o (___) tsukutta tochi da.
items.en: This area is land created by reclaiming it from the sea.
items.hi: यह इलाक़ा समुद्र को पाटकर बनाई गई ज़मीन है।
items.gu: આ વિસ્તાર સમુદ્રને પૂરીને બનાવેલી જમીન છે.

opts.en: extending a rail line into (wrong verb)

items.why: 海を埋め立てる is the fixed term for reclaiming land from the sea by filling it in.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 5 · 組み合わせの言葉②

items.q: 彼は、絶対やってないと（a.言い込んだ b.言い張った）。
items.qr: Kare wa, zettai yattenai to (a. iikonda b. iihatta).
items.en: He insisted that he absolutely didn't do it.
items.hi: उसने ज़िद पकड़ ली कि उसने बिल्कुल नहीं किया।
items.gu: તેણે જીદ પકડી કે તેણે બિલકુલ કર્યું નથી.
items.why: 言い張る is the fixed verb for stubbornly maintaining a claim despite doubt from others.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 6 · 組み合わせの言葉③

items.q: 詐欺にあって、店を（a.乗っ取られた b.差し出された）。
items.qr: Sagi ni atte, mise o (a. nottorareta b. sashidasareta).
items.en: I was defrauded and had my shop taken over.
items.hi: धोखाधड़ी का शिकार होकर मेरी दुकान छीन ली गई।
items.gu: છેતરપિંડીનો ભોગ બનીને મારી દુકાન પડાવી લેવાઈ.

opts.en: was handed over (wrong voice/nuance — implies the owner voluntarily gave it up)

items.why: 乗っ取られる (passive of 乗っ取る) fits being the victim of a hostile takeover through fraud; 差し出す implies willingly handing something over, which contradicts "被害にあって" (being a fraud victim).
items.unit: Week 7 Day 6 · 組み合わせの言葉③

items.q: イルカが2匹、仲良く（a.寄せ集めて b.寄り添って）泳いでいる。
items.qr: Iruka ga nihiki, nakayoku (a. yoseatsumete b. yorisotte) oyoide iru.
items.en: Two dolphins are swimming closely side by side.
items.hi: दो डॉल्फ़िन आपस में सटकर तैर रही हैं।
items.gu: બે ડોલ્ફિન એકબીજાને અડીને તરી રહી છે.

opts.en: gathering together (wrong verb — for collecting objects, not two animals swimming)

items.why: 寄り添う describes two living beings staying affectionately close together; 寄せ集める is for gathering scattered objects into one place.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 6 · 組み合わせの言葉③

items.q: 開店したら、大勢のお客さんが（a.押し込んで b.押し寄せて）きた。
items.qr: Kaiten shitara, oozei no okyakusan ga (a. oshikonde b. oshiyosete) kita.
items.en: As soon as the shop opened, a huge crowd of customers surged in.
items.hi: दुकान खुलते ही बड़ी संख्या में ग्राहक उमड़ पड़े।
items.gu: દુકાન ખૂલતાં જ મોટી સંખ્યામાં ગ્રાહકો ધસી આવ્યા.

opts.en: being pushed/crammed in (wrong voice — implies someone forcing them in, not customers arriving on their own)

items.why: 押し寄せる describes a crowd surging toward/into a place on its own momentum (like waves); 押し込む implies someone actively cramming people/things into a space.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 6 · 組み合わせの言葉③

items.q: 彼は医師の忠告を（a.押し切って b.言い張って）試合に出てしまった。
items.qr: Kare wa ishi no chuukoku o (a. oshikitte b. iihatte) shiai ni dete shimatta.
items.en: He went ahead and played in the match, disregarding the doctor's advice.
items.hi: उसने डॉक्टर की सलाह को नज़रअंदाज़ करते हुए मुक़ाबले में हिस्सा ले ही लिया।
items.gu: તેણે ડૉક્ટરની સલાહને અવગણીને મેચમાં ભાગ લઈ જ લીધો.

opts.en: insisting verbally (wrong verb — needs an object you act against, not just assert)

items.why: ～を押し切って ("pushing through ~ / overriding ~") is the fixed pattern for acting against someone else's advice or objection; 言い張る describes making a verbal claim, not overriding another's advice with action. See confusion notes below.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 6 · 組み合わせの言葉③

items.q: 客がいなければ商売は（a.待ち望めない b.成り立たない）。
items.qr: Kyaku ga inakereba shoubai wa (a. machinozomenai b. naritatanai).
items.en: Without customers, a business can't be sustained.
items.hi: ग्राहक न हों तो व्यवसाय टिक नहीं सकता।
items.gu: ગ્રાહકો ન હોય તો ધંધો ટકી શકતો નથી.

opts.en: cannot be longed for (wrong verb — grammatically odd here)

items.why: 商売が成り立つ／成り立たない is the fixed phrase for whether a business is financially viable; 待ち望む is about longing for something, unrelated to viability.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 6 · 組み合わせの言葉③

items.q: ついに問題集を丸々一冊（ ）。
items.qr: Tsui ni mondaishuu o marumaru issatsu (___).
items.en: I finally finished an entire practice workbook cover to cover.
items.hi: आख़िरकार पूरी अभ्यास पुस्तिका खत्म कर ही दी।
items.gu: આખરે આખી અભ્યાસ પુસ્તિકા પૂરી કરી જ દીધી.

opts.en: gathered together (wrong verb — for objects, not finishing a book)
reached/arrived at (wrong verb — for a destination, not completing work)
completed, saw through to the end

items.why: やり遂げる is the fixed verb for completing a demanding task all the way through, exactly fitting "finishing an entire workbook."
items.unit: Week 7 Day 6 · 組み合わせの言葉③

items.q: 気持ちを（ ）、さあ、また一から出直した。
items.qr: Kimochi o (___), saa, mata ichi kara denaoshita.
items.en: Switching my mindset, I started all over again from scratch.
items.hi: मन बदलकर, अब फिर से शुरुआत की।
items.gu: મન બદલીને, ફરી શરૂઆતથી કર્યું.

opts.en: mastering (the use of something — wrong object, doesn't fit 気持ち)
erasing completely (too strong — you switch your mood, not erase it entirely)
turning back/calling back (wrong verb, unrelated to mindset)

items.why: 気持ちを切り替える ("switch one's mindset/mood") is the fixed idiom for resetting one's emotional state before trying again.
items.unit: Week 7 Day 6 · 組み合わせの言葉③

items.q: そのバンドはデビュー10年目で（ ）した。
items.qr: Sono bando wa debyuu juu-nen-me de (___) shita.
items.en: That band had a monster hit in their 10th year since debut.
items.hi: उस बैंड को अपने डेब्यू के 10वें साल में ज़बरदस्त हिट मिली।
items.gu: તે બેન્ડને પોતાના ડેબ્યુના 10મા વર્ષે જબરદસ્ત હિટ મળી.

opts.en: layoffs (wrong meaning — bands don't "restructure" this way)

items.why: Day 2's その曲は去年大ブレイクした shows ブレイク's "become a sudden hit" sense, exactly matching a band's breakout after years of work.

items.q: 私は、ふだんお酒を飲むと（ ）があがるが、今日はまったく気分がよくならない。
items.qr: Watashi wa, fudan osake o nomu to (___) ga agaru ga, kyou wa mattaku kibun ga yoku naranai.
items.en: Normally my mood/energy lifts when I drink, but today I don't feel good at all.
items.hi: आमतौर पर शराब पीने से मेरा उत्साह बढ़ जाता है, पर आज बिल्कुल अच्छा महसूस नहीं हो रहा।
items.gu: સામાન્ય રીતે દારૂ પીવાથી મારો ઉત્સાહ વધે છે, પણ આજે બિલકુલ સારું નથી લાગતું.
items.why: Day 2's テンションが上がる is exactly "one's excitement level rises" — the false-friend callout on that page warns it doesn't mean English "tension."

items.q: 警察は誘拐犯と人質を解放させるための（ ）をした。
items.qr: Keisatsu wa yuukaihan to hitojichi o kaihou saseru tame no (___) o shita.
items.en: The police negotiated a deal with the kidnapper to get the hostage released.
items.hi: पुलिस ने अपहरणकर्ता के साथ बंधक को छुड़ाने के लिए सौदा किया।
items.gu: પોલીસે અપહરણકારો સાથે બંધકને છોડાવવા માટે સોદો કર્યો.

opts.en: a crackdown (wrong verb — for enforcing rules broadly, not one negotiation)
an interrogation (wrong verb — questioning, not a deal)

items.why: Day 4's 会社と取り引きする shows 取り引き's "deal/negotiation" sense, matching a hostage negotiation exactly.

items.q: 人気番組もあまり長く続くと（ ）化してくるものだ。
items.qr: Ninki bangumi mo amari nagaku tsuzuku to (___) ka shite kuru mono da.
items.en: Even a popular show tends to become stale/repetitive if it runs too long.
items.hi: लोकप्रिय शो भी अगर बहुत लंबा चले तो एक ढर्रे में फँस जाता है।
items.gu: લોકપ્રિય શો પણ જો બહુ લાંબો ચાલે તો એક ઢાંચામાં ફસાઈ જાય છે.
items.why: Day 1's マンネリ化する is the exact idiom for something losing its freshness through repetition.

items.q: 最近の携帯電話は機能が多くて、（ ）のは大変です。
items.qr: Saikin no keitai denwa wa kinou ga ookute, (___) no wa taihen desu.
items.en: Recent mobile phones have so many functions that mastering them is tough.
items.hi: आजकल के मोबाइल फ़ोन में इतने सारे फ़ीचर होते हैं कि उन्हें अच्छी तरह इस्तेमाल करना मुश्किल है।
items.gu: આજકાલના મોબાઇલ ફોનમાં એટલાં બધાં ફીચર્સ હોય છે કે તેમને સારી રીતે વાપરવું અઘરું છે.

opts.en: install (wrong verb — for fixtures, not skill mastery)

items.why: Day 6's 3ヵ国語を使いこなす shows 使いこなす's "master the use of something complex" sense, exactly fitting a feature-packed phone.

items.q: 今週はスケジュールが（ ）なので、映画に行くのは来週にしよう。
items.qr: Konshuu wa sukejuuru ga (___) na node, eiga ni iku no wa raishuu ni shiyou.
items.en: My schedule is tight this week, so let's go to the movies next week.
items.hi: इस हफ़्ते शेड्यूल बहुत व्यस्त है, इसलिए फ़िल्म देखने अगले हफ़्ते चलते हैं।
items.gu: આ અઠવાડિયે શેડ્યૂલ ખૂબ ટાઈટ છે, એટલે ફિલ્મ જોવા આવતા અઠવાડિયે જઈએ.
items.why: Day 2's タイトなスケジュール is the fixed collocation for a packed/tight schedule.

items.q: お近くにお越しの際は、ぜひ（ ）ください。
items.qr: Ochikaku ni okoshi no sai wa, zehi (___) kudasai.
items.en: If you're ever in the area, please be sure to drop by.
items.hi: अगर आप आसपास आएँ, तो ज़रूर हमारे यहाँ आइए।
items.gu: જો તમે નજીકમાં આવો, તો જરૂર અમારે ત્યાં આવજો.
items.why: Day 4's 友人の家に立ち寄る shows 立ち寄る is exactly the polite invitation verb for someone dropping by casually.

items.q: そのマラソン選手は、なぜか中間地点を（ ）ところでコースを外れた。
items.qr: Sono marason senshu wa, naze ka chuukan chiten o (___) tokoro de koosu o hazureta.
items.en: For some reason, that marathon runner left the course right after turning back at the halfway point.
items.hi: पता नहीं क्यों, वह मैराथन धावक बीच के पड़ाव पर मुड़ने के बाद रास्ते से भटक गया।
items.gu: ખબર નહીં કેમ, તે મેરેથોન દોડવીર અડધા મુકામે વળ્યા પછી રસ્તા પરથી ભટકી ગયો.

opts.en: reached (wrong verb — implies arriving at a final destination)

items.why: Day 5's 折り返す ("turn back") is the natural verb for a runner reversing direction at a marathon's halfway turnaround point.

items.q: 彼が変なことを言って（ ）ので、楽しいパーティーが台無しになった。
items.qr: Kare ga hen na koto o itte (___) node, tanoshii paatii ga dainashi ni natta.
items.en: He said something odd and stirred up trouble, so the fun party was ruined.
items.hi: उसने कुछ अजीब कहकर माहौल बिगाड़ दिया, जिससे मज़ेदार पार्टी बर्बाद हो गई।
items.gu: તેણે કંઈક વિચિત્ર કહીને માહોલ ખરાબ કરી નાખ્યો, જેથી મજાની પાર્ટી બગડી ગઈ.
items.why: Day 5's 会議がかき回された shows かき回す's figurative "throw into chaos/disrupt" sense, exactly matching someone ruining a party's mood.

items.q: 予算が（ ）になって、その企画は会議を通らなかった。
items.qr: Yosan ga (___) ni natte, sono kikaku wa kaigi o toorananakatta.
items.en: The budget became the sticking point, and the plan didn't pass in the meeting.
items.hi: बजट ही सबसे बड़ी रुकावट बना, और वह योजना मीटिंग में पास नहीं हो पाई।
items.gu: બજેટ જ સૌથી મોટો અવરોધ બન્યું, અને તે યોજના મીટિંગમાં પાસ ન થઈ.
items.why: Day 1's 予算がネックになっている is the exact idiom for budget being the one obstacle blocking a plan.

items.q: 特定の個人に一方的な恋愛感情やうらみを持って、しつこく追いかけたりする人。 ("A person who develops one-sided romantic feelings or resentment toward a specific individual and persistently follows them.")
items.qr: Tokutei no kojin ni ippouteki na ren'ai kanjou ya urami o motte, shitsukoku oikaketari suru hito.
items.why: Day 2's ストーカーに悩む names exactly this kind of obsessive, unwanted pursuit.

items.q: 爆発的に売れる。 ("To sell explosively, become a huge hit.")
items.qr: Bakuhatsuteki ni ureru.

opts.en: not a real verb form (wrong word)

items.why: Day 2's その曲は去年大ブレイクした is exactly "sold/became popular explosively."

items.q: 並んでいる列に強引に入ること。 ("To forcibly cut into a line of people waiting.")
items.qr: Narande iru retsu ni gouin ni hairu koto.
items.why: Day 4's 列に割り込む is this week's exact definition of cutting into a queue.

items.q: 一つのことに心を集中させる。 ("To focus one's heart/mind entirely on one thing.")
items.qr: Hitotsu no koto ni kokoro o shuuchuu saseru.

opts.en: complete (wrong word — about finishing, not focusing)

items.why: Day 5's 仕事に打ち込む is this week's own definition of devoting one's heart and soul to something.

items.q: もう少し付け加えること、またその付け加えられたもの。 ("Something extra added on top, or the thing that was added.")
items.qr: Mou sukoshi tsukekuwaeru koto, mata sono tsukekuwaerareta mono.
items.why: Day 3's 報酬は10万円プラスアルファになるだろう is this week's own definition of "extra added on top."

items.q: 新型の携帯電話のデザインをおおまかに手書きで書いてみました。
items.qr: Shingata no keitai denwa no dezain o oomaka ni tegaki de kaite mimashita.
items.en: I roughly sketched out the design of the new phone model by hand.
items.why: Day 2's ラフな図面 (a rough draft) is the exact match for "sketched roughly/unfinished."

items.q: 彼は病気で入院していたので、一年留年した。
items.qr: Kare wa byouki de nyuuin shite ita node, ichinen ryuunen shita.
items.en: Since he was hospitalized due to illness, he repeated a year of school.

opts.en: blundered (wrong meaning — not in this week's list, and doesn't fit)
skipped class (wrong meaning — implies choice, not illness)

items.why: Day 3's 単位を落として1年ダブる(＝留年する) directly equates ダブる with 留年する.

items.q: 始まったばかりのドラマがもう終了になってしまった。
items.qr: Hajimatta bakari no dorama ga mou shuuryou ni natte shimatta.
items.en: The drama that had just started has already been discontinued.

opts.en: giving up (close, but describes abandoning a task oneself, not a show being cancelled by its producers)

items.why: Day 4's 雑誌の販売を打ち切る is the exact match for something being discontinued/cancelled.

items.q: デパートの開店と同時に、客がどっと入ってきた。
items.qr: Depaato no kaiten to douji ni, kyaku ga dotto haitte kita.
items.en: The moment the department store opened, customers surged in.
items.why: Day 6's 波が押し寄せる extends naturally to a crowd surging into a store the moment it opens.

items.q: 彼女に新しいドラマへの出演のオファーが来た。
items.qr: Kanojo ni atarashii dorama e no shutsuen no ofaa ga kita.
items.en: She received an offer to appear in a new drama.

opts.en: acceptance (wrong meaning — she's receiving the offer, not accepting yet)

items.why: Day 4's 抗議を申し入れる shows 申し入れ's "formal proposal made to someone" sense, matching a professional offer extended to an actress.

items.q: 持ち込む
items.qr: mochikomu

opts.t: それは日本に持ち込むことはできないんじゃないの。
opts.r: Sore wa Nihon ni mochikomu koto wa dekinai n ja nai no.
opts.en: Isn't it true that you can't bring that into Japan?

opts.t: パソコンに音符を持ち込んで作曲をした。
opts.r: Pasokon ni onpu o mochikonde sakkyoku o shita.
opts.en: "I brought musical notes into the computer and composed" — wrong verb; inputting data needs 打ち込んで (Day 5), not 持ち込んで

opts.t: 苦い薬を無理やり口に持ち込んだ。
opts.r: Nigai kusuri o muriyari kuchi ni mochikonda.
opts.en: "Forcibly brought bitter medicine into my mouth" — wrong verb; a small, forceful action into the mouth needs 放り込んだ (Day 5), not 持ち込んだ

opts.t: バナナやミカンをバッグに持ち込んで、旅に出かけた。
opts.r: Banana ya mikan o baggu ni mochikonde, tabi ni dekaketa.
opts.en: "Brought bananas and mikans into my bag and went on a trip" — odd; simply packing fruit in one's own bag just needs 入れて, since 持ち込む implies carrying something into a separate, often restricted, place

items.why: 持ち込む describes bringing something from outside into a bounded place — a country, a venue, a hotel room; option 1's customs/import context (日本に持ち込む) is the textbook use. Options 2, 3, and 4 each substitute 持ち込む for a verb that actually fits better: 打ち込む, 放り込む, and simple 入れる.

items.q: トラウマ
items.qr: torauma

opts.t: 彼は上司のトラウマが原因で出世できなかった。
opts.r: Kare wa joushi no torauma ga gen'in de shusse dekinakatta.
opts.en: "He couldn't get promoted because of his boss's trauma" — nonsensical; someone else's trauma doesn't explain your own career stagnation

opts.t: すぐに落ち込むのは、トラウマになるからだ。
opts.r: Sugu ni ochikomu no wa, torauma ni naru kara da.
opts.en: "Getting depressed easily is because it becomes trauma" — backwards causality; trauma CAUSES lasting distress, it isn't caused BY easily feeling down

opts.t: 私は、震災で被害を受けたことがトラウマになっている。
opts.r: Watashi wa, shinsai de higai o uketa koto ga torauma ni natte iru.
opts.en: Having suffered damage from the earthquake has become a trauma for me.

opts.t: 小さいころのトラウマがいい状況になってきました。
opts.r: Chiisai koro no torauma ga ii joukyou ni natte kimashita.
opts.en: "The trauma of my childhood has come into a good situation" — nonsensical; trauma doesn't "become good"

items.why: Day 2's 子どもの頃の体験がトラウマになる is the exact pattern for a painful past event leaving lasting psychological damage; 1, 2, and 4 each misuse the causality or imply trauma can improve.

items.q: ハンデ
items.qr: hande

opts.t: 大学での研究は、ハンデがついたのでスムーズに進んでいない。
opts.r: Daigaku de no kenkyuu wa, hande ga tsuita node sumuuzu ni susunde inai.
opts.en: "University research isn't going smoothly because it got a handicap" — odd; research doesn't "acquire a handicap" the way a person does

opts.t: 彼は体が不自由であるというハンデを乗り越えて、国立大学に合格した。
opts.r: Kare wa karada ga fujiyuu de aru to iu hande o norikoete, kokuritsu daigaku ni goukaku shita.
opts.en: He overcame the handicap of having a physical disability and got into a national university.

opts.t: プロの彼にはハンデをあげたほうがいいよ。
opts.r: Puro no kare ni wa hande o ageta hou ga ii yo.
opts.en: "It's better to give a handicap to him since he's a pro" — backwards; a pro should GIVE a handicap to a weaker opponent, not receive one

opts.t: 彼女の考え方はハンデがあるので、あまり参考にならない。
opts.r: Kanojo no kangaekata wa hande ga aru node, amari sankou ni naranai.
opts.en: "Her way of thinking has a handicap" — odd collocation; a way of thinking doesn't "have" a handicap

items.why: Day 1's ハンデを克服する is the natural collocation for overcoming a genuine disadvantage; 1, 3, and 4 each misuse ハンデ in contexts it doesn't fit, or reverse who should give/receive it.

items.q: 取り戻す
items.qr: torimodosu

opts.t: 住民たちは、災害を取り戻して、立ち直った。
opts.r: Juumin-tachi wa, saigai o torimodoshite, tachinaotta.
opts.en: "The residents recovered the disaster and got back on their feet" — nonsensical; you cannot "regain" a disaster itself

opts.t: 父が意識を取り戻してまた話ができることを願っています。
opts.r: Chichi ga ishiki o torimodoshite mata hanashi ga dekiru koto o negatte imasu.
opts.en: I hope my father regains consciousness and can talk again.

opts.t: 事件の内容をじっくり取り戻してみた。
opts.r: Jiken no naiyou o jikkuri torimodoshite mita.
opts.en: "I carefully retrieved the content of the incident" — odd verb choice; reviewing details needs 調べて/思い出して, not 取り戻して

opts.t: 病気の症状がいくらか取り戻してきた。
opts.r: Byouki no shoujou ga ikuraka torimodoshite kita.
opts.en: "The illness's symptoms have recovered somewhat" — backwards; a person's HEALTH recovers, symptoms themselves don't "get regained"

items.why: Day 4's 遅れを取り戻す shows 取り戻す's "regain/recover" sense; 意識を取り戻す ("regain consciousness") is a standard fixed idiom, while 1, 3, and 4 each apply the verb to something that can't logically be "regained" this way.

items.q: ギャップ
items.qr: gyappu

opts.t: 最近の不況でついにギャップができてしまった。
opts.r: Saikin no fukyou de tsui ni gyappu ga dekite shimatta.
opts.en: "The recent recession finally created a gap" — vague/unnatural; a recession creates 格差 (disparity), not typically described as ギャップ forming

opts.t: 年をとったせいか、最近の若者とのギャップを感じる。
opts.r: Toshi o totta sei ka, saikin no wakamono to no gyappu o kanjiru.
opts.en: Perhaps because I've gotten older, I feel a gap with today's youth.

opts.t: 天候のギャップを気にしないで、日夜練習に励んだ。
opts.r: Tenkou no gyappu o ki ni shinaide, nichiya renshuu ni hagenda.
opts.en: "Not minding the gap in weather" — nonsensical; weather doesn't have a "gap," it has 変化 (changes)

opts.t: あなたと私のギャップの違いに驚いてしまった。
opts.r: Anata to watashi no gyappu no chigai ni odoroite shimatta.
opts.en: "Surprised by the difference of the gap between you and me" — redundant; "the gap's difference" doubles up on the same meaning

items.why: Day 2's 世代間のギャップ extends naturally to feeling a gap with younger generations due to aging; 1, 3, and 4 each force ギャップ into a collocation it doesn't naturally take, or double up redundantly.

items.q: 熱いなべを手で（a.じかに b.いかに）つかんで、やけどをしてしまった。
items.qr: Atsui nabe o te de (a. jikani b. ikani) tsukande, yakedo o shite shimatta.
items.en: I grabbed the hot pot directly with my bare hand and got burned.
items.hi: मैंने गरम बर्तन को सीधे हाथ से पकड़ लिया और जल गया।
items.gu: મેં ગરમ વાસણને સીધું હાથથી પકડ્યું અને દાઝી ગયો.

opts.en: how (wrong word — needs a question or ～ても, not this slot)

items.why: じかに describes touching/dealing with something with nothing in between (bare hand on a hot pot); いかに means "how" and grammatically can't fill this manner-adverb slot.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 1 · 似ている言葉①

items.q: かゆいので肌をかきむしったら、血が（a.しみて b.にじんで）きた。
items.qr: Kayui node hada o kakimushittara, chi ga (a. shimite b. nijinde) kita.
items.en: Since it was itchy, I scratched my skin raw until blood started to seep out.
items.hi: खुजली होने के कारण त्वचा को नोच डाला, तो खून रिसने लगा।
items.gu: ખંજવાળ આવવાથી ત્વચા ખોતરી નાખી, તો લોહી નીકળવા લાગ્યું.

opts.en: stinging/soaking in (wrong verb — for smoke or sweat, not blood appearing)

items.why: にじむ is exactly the verb for a liquid (blood, tears, ink) slowly welling up to the surface; しみる describes a stinging sensation or a liquid soaking into fabric, not blood emerging from broken skin.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 1 · 似ている言葉①

items.q: 最近お酒を飲む量を減らそうと（a.心がけて b.心得て）います。
items.qr: Saikin osake o nomu ryou o herasou to (a. kokorogakete b. kokoroete) imasu.
items.en: Lately I've been making a conscious effort to cut down on how much I drink.
items.hi: आजकल मैं शराब पीने की मात्रा कम करने की सोच-समझकर कोशिश कर रहा हूँ।
items.gu: આજકાલ હું દારૂ પીવાનું પ્રમાણ ઘટાડવાનો સભાનપણે પ્રયત્ન કરું છું.

opts.en: understanding/grasping (wrong verb — a fact/skill one already knows, not a goal one strives toward)

items.why: 心がける means "to make it a habit/goal to try to ~," matching an ongoing resolution; 心得る means "to have understood/grasped" something, like manners or one's position, not a future intention.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 1 · 似ている言葉①

items.q: 転んだら、腰の骨に（a.あざ b.ひび）が入ってしまった。
items.qr: Korondara, koshi no hone ni (a. aza b. hibi) ga haitte shimatta.
items.en: When I fell, I ended up with a hairline crack in my hip bone.
items.hi: गिरने पर, कूल्हे की हड्डी में दरार आ गई।
items.gu: પડી જવાથી, થાપાના હાડકામાં તિરાડ પડી ગઈ.

opts.en: a bruise (wrong noun — a surface discoloration, not a break in the bone)

items.why: ひびが入る is the fixed phrase for a crack forming in something solid — a wall, dish, or bone; あざ is a bruise mark on the skin's surface, unrelated to a broken bone underneath.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 1 · 似ている言葉①

items.q: 私は（a.一粒の b.小粒の）納豆が好きです。
items.qr: Watashi wa (a. hitotsubu no b. kotsubu no) nattou ga suki desu.
items.en: I like small-grain natto.
items.hi: मुझे छोटे दानों वाला नत्तो पसंद है।
items.gu: મને નાના દાણાવાળું નાત્તો ગમે છે.

opts.en: of one single grain (wrong meaning — describes a count of one, not a size variety)

items.why: 小粒 describes a whole food as being the small-grain variety (小 = small + 粒 = grain), the natural way to describe a preference for natto's grain size; 一粒の literally means "of a single grain," which doesn't describe an entire dish.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 1 · 似ている言葉①

items.q: （a.しなびた b.枯れた）白菜があったが、スープにしたらおいしかった。
items.qr: (a. Shinabita b. Kareta) hakusai ga atta ga, suupu ni shitara oishikatta.
items.en: I had some wilted napa cabbage, but it turned out delicious made into soup.
items.hi: मुरझाई हुई पत्ता गोभी थी, पर सूप बनाकर स्वादिष्ट बनी।
items.gu: ચીમળાયેલી કોબી હતી, પણ સૂપ બનાવીને સ્વાદિષ્ટ બની.

opts.en: died/withered (wrong verb — too final for a vegetable still fit to cook)

items.why: しなびる describes a vegetable losing moisture/firmness while still edible — exactly cabbage headed for soup; 枯れる describes a plant dying outright, like a tree, and wouldn't describe something you then cook and enjoy.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 1 · 似ている言葉①

items.q: 彼は（ ）政治家らしい口調で話す。
items.qr: Kare wa (___) seijika rashii kuchou de hanasu.
items.en: He speaks in a tone that really does sound just like a politician.
items.hi: वह बिल्कुल एक राजनेता जैसे लहजे में बोलता है।
items.gu: તે બિલકુલ રાજકારણી જેવા લહેકામાં બોલે છે.

opts.en: how (wrong word — needs a question, not らしい)

items.why: いかにも＋～らしい is the fixed pattern for "looking/sounding exactly like the stereotype of ~"; いかに alone means "how" and needs a question word or ～ても, not らしい.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 1 · 似ている言葉①

items.q: 靴のひもが（ ）いるよ。
items.qr: Kutsu no himo ga (___) iru yo.
items.en: Your shoelace has come untied.
items.hi: तुम्हारे जूते का फीता खुल गया है।
items.gu: તારા બૂટની દોરી છૂટી ગઈ છે.

opts.en: coming apart at the seam (wrong verb — for stitching, not a tied bow)

items.why: ほどける is exactly "to come untied" for a knot or bow, like a shoelace; ほころびる is reserved for stitching/a seam coming apart, a different kind of unraveling.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 1 · 似ている言葉①

items.q: スリを追いかけたが、途中で（a.見失って b.見落として）しまった。
items.qr: Suri o oikaketa ga, tochuu de (a. miushinatte b. miotoshite) shimatta.
items.en: I chased the pickpocket, but lost sight of him partway through.
items.hi: मैं जेबकतरे का पीछा कर रहा था, पर बीच में उसे खो बैठा।
items.gu: હું ખિસ્સાકાતરુની પાછળ દોડ્યો, પણ વચ્ચે તેને ગુમાવી દીધો.

opts.en: overlooked (wrong verb — for a stationary detail, not a fleeing person)

items.why: 見失う describes losing track of something moving that one was following — exactly a pickpocket vanishing mid-chase; 見落とす means failing to notice something that was there in front of you the whole time, like an error on a page.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 2 · 似ている言葉②

items.q: 全社員に（a.一連 b.一斉）にメールを送った。
items.qr: Zen shain ni (a. ichiren b. issei) ni meeru o okutta.
items.en: An email was sent to all employees all at once.
items.hi: सभी कर्मचारियों को एक साथ ईमेल भेजा गया।
items.gu: બધા કર્મચારીઓને એકસાથે ઈમેલ મોકલવામાં આવ્યો.

opts.en: a connected series (wrong meaning — for events, not simultaneity)

items.why: 一斉に describes many people/things acting or being acted on at the exact same moment — a mass email hitting every inbox together; 一連 describes a chain of connected events (a series of crimes), not simultaneous timing.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 2 · 似ている言葉②

items.q: 古い家がリフォームで（a.見違える b.見計らう）ようになった。
items.qr: Furui ie ga rifoomu de (a. michigaeru b. mihakarau) you ni natta.
items.en: The old house was renovated until it became unrecognizably better.
items.hi: पुराना घर मरम्मत से इतना बदल गया कि पहचान में नहीं आता।
items.gu: જૂનું ઘર સમારકામથી એટલું બદલાઈ ગયું કે ઓળખાય જ નહીં.

opts.en: judge the right timing (wrong verb — unrelated to physical transformation)

items.why: 見違える describes something changing so dramatically for the better that it looks like a different thing entirely — the perfect fit for a renovated house; 見計らう is strictly about choosing the right moment to act.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 2 · 似ている言葉②

items.q: ドラマの最終回を（a.見落として b.見逃して）しまった。
items.qr: Dorama no saishuukai o (a. miotoshite b. minogashite) shimatta.
items.en: I ended up missing the final episode of the drama.
items.hi: मैं ड्रामा का आख़िरी एपिसोड देखने से चूक गया।
items.gu: હું ડ્રામાનો છેલ્લો એપિસોડ જોવાનું ચૂકી ગયો.

opts.en: overlooked (wrong verb — for a detail present in front of you)

items.why: 見逃す is the fixed verb for missing a one-time chance to see/catch something before it's gone, exactly a broadcast episode; 見落とす is about failing to notice a static detail, not a broadcast slipping by.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 2 · 似ている言葉②

items.q: 黒い煙が空（a.一様 b.一面）に広がっている。
items.qr: Kuroi kemuri ga sora (a. ichiyou b. ichimen) ni hirogatte iru.
items.en: Black smoke is spreading across the entire sky.
items.hi: काला धुआँ पूरे आकाश में फैल रहा है।
items.gu: કાળો ધુમાડો આખા આકાશમાં ફેલાઈ રહ્યો છે.

opts.en: uniformly, everyone alike (wrong meaning — describes people's reactions, not a covered area)

items.why: 空一面 ("the whole sky") is the fixed phrase for something covering an entire visible area; 一様に describes multiple people or things all behaving the same way, not smoke covering a surface.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 2 · 似ている言葉②

items.q: ここからの眺めは（a.一目 b.一見）の価値がある。
items.qr: Koko kara no nagame wa (a. ichimoku b. ikken) no kachi ga aru.
items.en: The view from here is worth seeing.
items.hi: यहाँ से दिखने वाला नज़ारा देखने लायक़ है।
items.gu: અહીંથી દેખાતું દૃશ્ય જોવા લાયક છે.

opts.en: a single glance (wrong word here — pairs with 置く or 瞭然, not 価値がある)

items.why: 一見の価値がある is the fixed idiom for "worth a look"; 一目 is reserved for its own set phrases like 一目置く ("to hold in high regard") and 一目瞭然 ("obvious at a glance"), and doesn't combine with 価値がある.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 2 · 似ている言葉②

items.q: この棚の商品は（ ）3割引きになっています。
items.qr: Kono tana no shouhin wa (___) san-wari-biki ni natte imasu.
items.en: The items on this shelf are uniformly 30% off.
items.hi: इस शेल्फ़ के सामान पर एक समान 30% छूट है।
items.gu: આ છાજલીની ચીજવસ્તુઓ પર એકસમાન 30% છૂટ છે.

opts.en: everyone present (wrong meaning — a group of people, not a rate)
a whole area (wrong meaning — land, not a discount)

items.why: 一律に is the fixed way to say a rate/rule applies equally to everything — a discount here, salaries in the vocabulary list above; 一同 refers to a group of people, not a percentage.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 2 · 似ている言葉②

items.q: 新型の車は以前のデザインを（ ）した。
items.qr: Shingata no kuruma wa izen no dezain o (___) shita.
items.en: The new car model completely renewed its previous design.
items.hi: नई कार मॉडल ने पुराने डिज़ाइन को पूरी तरह बदल दिया।
items.gu: નવા કાર મોડેલે જૂની ડિઝાઇનને સંપૂર્ણપણે બદલી નાખી.

opts.en: sweep away entirely (wrong verb — for eliminating something unwanted, not updating a design)

items.why: 一新する means "to refresh/renew something completely" — exactly a redesigned car; 一掃する means "to eliminate/sweep away" something undesirable (violence, debt), not to refresh a design.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 2 · 似ている言葉②

items.q: 彼の人を見下した態度が、（a.鼻が高い b.鼻につく）。
items.qr: Kare no hito o mikudashita taido ga, (a. hana ga takai b. hana ni tsuku).
items.en: His condescending attitude toward others really gets on my nerves.
items.hi: दूसरों को नीचा दिखाने वाला उसका रवैया बहुत खलता है।
items.gu: બીજાને નીચા દેખાડતું તેનું વલણ બહુ ખૂંચે છે.

opts.en: proud (wrong tone — positive, doesn't fit a complaint about someone)

items.why: 鼻につく describes a manner that becomes irritating the more one is exposed to it — exactly a condescending attitude; 鼻が高い is a positive feeling of pride about oneself or one's own family, the wrong tone entirely here.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 3 · 体の部分を使った言葉①

items.q: あの人は口が（a.すべっている b.こえている）から、そのレストランの料理では満足しないでしょう。
items.qr: Ano hito wa kuchi ga (a. subette iru b. koete iru) kara, sono resutoran no ryouri de wa manzoku shinai deshou.
items.en: That person has a refined palate, so they probably won't be satisfied with that restaurant's food.
items.hi: उस व्यक्ति की ज़ुबान बहुत नफ़ीस है, इसलिए वह उस रेस्तराँ के खाने से संतुष्ट नहीं होगा।
items.gu: તે વ્યક્તિની જીભ ખૂબ ચોખલિયું છે, એટલે તે રેસ્ટોરન્ટના ખાવાથી સંતુષ્ટ નહીં થાય.

opts.en: letting something slip (wrong meaning — about accidentally revealing a secret)

items.why: 口が肥える describes someone who's eaten enough good food to become hard to satisfy, exactly the reason they'd be picky about a restaurant; 口が滑る is about accidentally revealing something in speech, unrelated to taste.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 3 · 体の部分を使った言葉①

items.q: 答えるのに頭を（a.かたむける b.かかえる）ような質問がたくさん来た。
items.qr: Kotaeru no ni atama o (a. katamukeru b. kakaeru) you na shitsumon ga takusan kita.
items.en: A lot of questions came in that were hard enough to make one hold one's head in despair trying to answer them.
items.hi: जवाब देने में सिर पकड़ लेने जैसे कई सवाल आए।
items.gu: જવાબ આપવામાં માથું પકડી લેવું પડે એવા ઘણા સવાલ આવ્યા.

opts.en: tilt (wrong verb — 傾ける pairs with 耳, "to lend an ear," not 頭)

items.why: 頭を抱える is the fixed idiom for being so stumped or troubled by something that one holds one's own head in one's hands; 傾ける is reserved for 耳を傾ける ("to listen attentively"), not 頭.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 3 · 体の部分を使った言葉①

items.q: ありがとうございます。そうしていただけると私の（a.顔が立ちます b.顔がききます）。
items.qr: Arigatou gozaimasu. Sou shite itadakeru to watashi no (a. kao ga tachimasu b. kao ga kikimasu).
items.en: Thank you. If you could do that, it would save my reputation.
items.hi: धन्यवाद। अगर आप ऐसा कर दें, तो मेरी इज़्ज़त बच जाएगी।
items.gu: આભાર. જો તમે એમ કરી શકો, તો મારી આબરૂ જળવાઈ રહેશે.

opts.en: get special treatment somewhere (wrong idiom — about being a known customer, not reputation being saved)

items.why: 顔が立つ means one's honor/reputation is preserved thanks to someone's action, exactly what's being thanked for here; 顔が利く describes being well-known enough at a specific place to receive favors, an unrelated situation.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 3 · 体の部分を使った言葉①

items.q: 彼の努力には（a.頭が下がる b.会わせる顔が無い）。
items.qr: Kare no doryoku ni wa (a. atama ga sagaru b. awaseru kao ga nai).
items.en: I have to admire his effort.
items.hi: उसकी मेहनत के आगे सिर झुक जाता है।
items.gu: તેની મહેનત આગળ માથું ઝૂકી જાય છે.

opts.en: too ashamed to face someone (wrong tone — shame, not admiration)

items.why: 頭が下がる is the fixed idiom for feeling real admiration toward someone's effort or character; 合わせる顔がない describes one's own shame at facing someone, the opposite emotional direction.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 3 · 体の部分を使った言葉①

items.q: 美しい歌声に（a.耳を傾けた b.耳を貸した）。
items.qr: Utsukushii utagoe ni (a. mimi o katamuketa b. mimi o kashita).
items.en: I listened attentively to the beautiful singing voice.
items.hi: सुंदर गायन को ध्यान से सुना।
items.gu: સુંદર ગાયનને ધ્યાનથી સાંભળ્યું.

opts.en: lent an ear (wrong register — usually used for whether one will hear out a request/complaint, often negated)

items.why: 耳を傾ける is the natural, appreciative idiom for listening closely to music or a speaker; 耳を貸す typically appears in sentences about whether someone will listen to a request, and often in the negative (耳を貸してくれなかった) — a mismatched register for enjoying singing.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 3 · 体の部分を使った言葉①

items.q: 彼女はそれを聞いたとたん、（ ）驚きの声をあげた。
items.qr: Kanojo wa sore o kiita totan, (___) odoroki no koe o ageta.
items.en: The moment she heard that, her eyes went wide and she let out a cry of surprise.
items.hi: उसने वह सुनते ही, आँखें फाड़कर हैरानी से चीख़ पड़ी।
items.gu: તેણે તે સાંભળતાં જ, આંખો પહોળી કરીને આશ્ચર્યથી ચીસ પાડી.

opts.en: a slip of the tongue (wrong meaning)
not a fixed idiom (鼻にかける means "boast," this form is wrong)

items.why: 目を丸くする is the fixed idiom for one's eyes going wide with surprise, matching "the moment she heard it"; the other options describe unrelated actions like upholding a reputation or slipping up in speech.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 3 · 体の部分を使った言葉①

items.q: 女優の中でも、彼女は特に（ ）美しい女性です。
items.qr: Joyuu no naka demo, kanojo wa toku ni (___) utsukushii josei desu.
items.en: Even among actresses, she is an especially eye-catching, beautiful woman.
items.hi: अभिनेत्रियों में भी, वह ख़ासतौर पर ध्यान खींचने वाली ख़ूबसूरत महिला है।
items.gu: અભિનેત્રીઓમાં પણ, તે ખાસ ધ્યાન ખેંચે એવી સુંદર મહિલા છે.

opts.en: picture vividly (wrong meaning — for memories/scenes, not a person's looks)

items.why: 目を引く is the fixed idiom for something or someone that visually catches people's attention, exactly describing striking beauty; the other 目 idioms describe unrelated states like nostalgia, disbelief, or being overwhelmed.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 3 · 体の部分を使った言葉①

items.q: 服装だけでなく髪型にも（a.気が利く b.気を配る）。
items.qr: Fukusou dake de naku kamigata ni mo (a. ki ga kiku b. ki o kubaru).
items.en: I pay careful attention not only to my clothes but to my hairstyle too.
items.hi: कपड़ों के अलावा हेयरस्टाइल पर भी ध्यान देना।
items.gu: કપડાં ઉપરાંત હેરસ્ટાઇલ પર પણ ધ્યાન આપવું.

opts.en: quick-witted, tactful (wrong verb — a personality trait, not the act of paying attention to something specific)

items.why: 気を配る describes actively directing one's attention/care toward several things — exactly clothes and hairstyle both; 気が利く describes an inherent quality of being perceptive/thoughtful, not an action performed on an object marked with に.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 4 · 体の部分を使った言葉②

items.q: イカの刺身は（a.手が b.足が）早いので、今日中に食べたほうがいいです。
items.qr: Ika no sashimi wa (a. te ga b. ashi ga) hayai node, kyou juu ni tabeta hou ga ii desu.
items.en: Squid sashimi spoils quickly, so it's best to eat it today.
items.hi: स्क्विड सशिमी जल्दी ख़राब हो जाती है, इसलिए आज ही खा लेना बेहतर है।
items.gu: સ્ક્વિડ સાશિમી ઝડપથી બગડી જાય છે, એટલે આજે જ ખાઈ લેવું સારું છે.

opts.en: quick to act/flirt (wrong idiom — describes a person, not food)

items.why: 足が早い is the fixed idiom for food going bad quickly; 手が早い is an unrelated idiom describing a person who acts (or flirts) hastily.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 4 · 体の部分を使った言葉②

items.q: 私の学校は、やたら規律にうるさいので（a.息が切れる b.息が詰まる）。
items.qr: Watashi no gakkou wa, yatara kiritsu ni urusai node (a. iki ga kireru b. iki ga tsumaru).
items.en: My school is excessively strict about rules, so it feels suffocating.
items.hi: मेरा स्कूल अनुशासन को लेकर बहुत सख़्त है, इसलिए दम घुटता है।
items.gu: મારી શાળા શિસ્ત બાબતે ખૂબ કડક છે, એટલે ગૂંગળામણ થાય છે.

opts.en: out of breath (wrong meaning — physical exertion, not an oppressive mood)

items.why: 息が詰まる describes a stifling, oppressive atmosphere — exactly overly strict school rules; 息が切れる is purely about physical breathlessness after exertion like running.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 4 · 体の部分を使った言葉②

items.q: その景色の美しさに思わず（a.息をのんだ b.息が切れた）。
items.qr: Sono keshiki no utsukushisa ni omowazu (a. iki o nonda b. iki ga kireta).
items.en: I unconsciously held my breath at the beauty of the scenery.
items.hi: उस दृश्य की सुंदरता देखकर अनजाने में साँस थम गई।
items.gu: તે દૃશ્યની સુંદરતા જોઈને અજાણતાં શ્વાસ થંભી ગયો.

opts.en: became out of breath (wrong meaning — exertion, not an emotional reaction)

items.why: 息をのむ is the fixed idiom for gasping/catching one's breath in awe at beauty or shock; 息が切れる describes physical breathlessness from running or exertion, an unrelated cause.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 4 · 体の部分を使った言葉②

items.q: 客が多くても少なくても、彼はいつも（a.気がある b.手を抜かない）演奏をする。
items.qr: Kyaku ga ookutemo sukunakutemo, kare wa itsumo (a. ki ga aru b. te o nukanai) ensou o suru.
items.en: Whether there are many customers or few, he always performs without cutting corners.
items.hi: चाहे दर्शक ज़्यादा हों या कम, वह हमेशा बिना कोताही किए प्रदर्शन करता है।
items.gu: પ્રેક્ષકો વધુ હોય કે ઓછા, તે હંમેશાં કોઈ કસર છોડ્યા વિના પ્રદર્શન કરે છે.

opts.en: have romantic interest in (wrong meaning entirely)

items.why: 手を抜く/抜かない describes putting in (or skimping on) full effort in one's work — a performer's consistent professionalism regardless of audience size; 気がある means having romantic feelings for someone, unrelated here.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 4 · 体の部分を使った言葉②

items.q: 老いた母は我が子の帰国を（a.息を b.首を）長くして待っていた。
items.qr: Oita haha wa waga ko no kikoku o (a. iki o b. kubi o) nagaku shite matte ita.
items.en: The aged mother waited eagerly for her child's return home.
items.hi: बूढ़ी माँ अपने बच्चे की वापसी का बेसब्री से इंतज़ार कर रही थी।
items.gu: વૃદ્ધ મા પોતાના બાળકના પાછા આવવાની આતુરતાથી રાહ જોઈ રહી હતી.

opts.en: not a fixed idiom (息が長い describes career longevity, a different image)

items.why: 首を長くして待つ is the fixed idiom for waiting longingly, as if craning one's neck to see further down the road; 息を長くして isn't a set phrase — 息が長い describes something long-lasting like a career, a different image entirely.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 4 · 体の部分を使った言葉②

items.q: こんな大きな犬を飼うのは、ちょっと私の（ ）と思います。
items.qr: Konna ookina inu o kau no wa, chotto watashi no (___) to omoimasu.
items.en: I think keeping such a big dog is a bit beyond what I can handle.
items.hi: इतना बड़ा कुत्ता पालना मेरे बस से थोड़ा बाहर है, ऐसा मुझे लगता है।
items.gu: આટલો મોટો કૂતરો પાળવો મારી ક્ષમતાની થોડો બહાર છે, એવું મને લાગે છે.
items.why: 手に余る is the fixed idiom for a responsibility exceeding what one can personally manage, exactly a dog too big to handle; the other options describe unrelated situations like exhausting resources or overspending.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 4 · 体の部分を使った言葉②

items.q: ハイキングで一日中歩き回ったら足が（ ）。
items.qr: Haikingu de ichinichi juu arukimawattara ashi ga (___).
items.en: After walking around all day on the hike, my legs became stiff as rods.
items.hi: हाइकिंग में पूरे दिन चलने के बाद पैर लकड़ी की तरह अकड़ गए।
items.gu: હાઇકિંગમાં આખો દિવસ ચાલ્યા પછી પગ લાકડાની જેમ જકડાઈ ગયા.

opts.en: stopped coming out (not an idiom here)
got clogged (not an idiom with 足)

items.why: 足が棒になる is the fixed idiom for legs going stiff and rod-like from exhaustion after a long day of walking or standing; none of the other options form a real collocation with 足 in this sense.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 4 · 体の部分を使った言葉②

items.q: 祖父の自慢話は（a.顔から火が出るほど b.耳にたこが出来るほど）聞かされた。
items.qr: Sofu no jimanbanashi wa (a. kao kara hi ga deru hodo b. mimi ni tako ga dekiru hodo) kikasareta.
items.en: I've been made to listen to grandpa's boastful stories so many times I'm sick of them.
items.hi: दादा की डींगें इतनी बार सुनी हैं कि कान पक गए।
items.gu: દાદાની બડાઈઓ એટલી વાર સાંભળી છે કે કંટાળો આવી ગયો.

opts.r: kao kara hi ga deru hodo
opts.en: embarrassed enough for fire to shoot from one's face (wrong simile — about shame, not repetition)

opts.t: 耳にたこが出来るほど
opts.r: mimi ni tako ga dekiru hodo

items.why: 耳にたこができる is the fixed idiom for having heard the same thing so many times one is sick of it, exactly repeated boastful stories; 顔から火が出る describes intense embarrassment, an unrelated feeling.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 5 · よく使う表現①

items.q: （a.差し支えなければ b.夜分遅くすみませんが）お名前をお教えくださいませんか。
items.qr: (a. Sashitsukae nakereba b. Yabun osoku sumimasen ga) onamae o oOshie kudasaimasen ka.
items.en: If it's not too much trouble, could you tell me your name?
items.hi: अगर कोई असुविधा न हो, तो क्या आप अपना नाम बता सकते हैं?
items.gu: જો કોઈ અગવડ ન હોય, તો શું તમે તમારું નામ કહી શકશો?

opts.t: 夜分遅くすみませんが
opts.en: sorry to call this late at night (wrong context — no late-hour setting given)

items.why: 差し支えなければ is the general polite hedge used before any request for information; 夜分遅くすみませんが is reserved specifically for apologizing about the lateness of a call or visit, a context not established here.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 5 · よく使う表現①

items.q: 若いころなら（a.悪しからず b.いざ知らず）、今そんな無茶をすると体を壊すよ。
items.qr: Wakai koro nara (a. ashikarazu b. iza shirazu), ima sonna mucha o suru to karada o kowasu yo.
items.en: Setting aside what you could get away with when young, doing something that reckless now will ruin your health.
items.hi: जवानी की बात छोड़ो, अब ऐसी लापरवाही करने से सेहत बिगड़ जाएगी।
items.gu: જુવાનીની વાત જવા દો, હવે આવી બેદરકારી કરવાથી તબિયત બગડી જશે.

opts.en: don't take offense (wrong idiom — used when declining/refusing something, not contrasting past and present)

items.why: ～ならいざ知らず is the fixed pattern for "that might be true/acceptable for ~, but apart from that..." — exactly the youth-vs-now contrast; 悪しからず only appears when politely refusing or declining something.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 5 · よく使う表現①

items.q: 欲を言えば（a.ピン b.キリ）がないから、このくらいのアパートでいいんじゃないかな。
items.qr: Yoku o ieba (a. pin b. kiri) ga nai kara, kono kurai no apaato de ii n ja nai ka na.
items.en: If we start being greedy there's no end to it, so an apartment about this size should be fine, don't you think?
items.hi: लालच करें तो कोई हद नहीं है, इसलिए इतना-सा फ़्लैट काफ़ी है, है ना?
items.gu: લોભ કરીએ તો કોઈ હદ નથી, એટલે આટલો ફ્લેટ પૂરતો છે, ખરું ને?

opts.en: the top/best quality (wrong word — belongs to ピンからキリまで, not 欲を言えば)

items.why: 欲を言えばキリがない is the fixed idiom for "there's no end to wanting more" once greed takes over; ピン belongs to the separate idiom ピンからキリまで ("from the best to the worst"), a different fixed phrase entirely.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 5 · よく使う表現①

items.q: （a.去る b.来る）10月10日に体育祭が行われます。
items.qr: (a. Saru b. Kitaru) juu-gatsu tooka ni taiikusai ga okonawaremasu.
items.en: The sports festival will be held on the upcoming October 10th.
items.hi: आगामी 10 अक्तूबर को खेल उत्सव आयोजित होगा।
items.gu: આગામી 10 ઓક્ટોબરે રમતોત્સવ યોજાશે.

opts.en: the bygone/past (wrong direction — contradicts the future-tense 行われます)

items.why: 来る marks an upcoming/future date, matching the future-tense 行われます ("will be held"); 去る marks a date already in the past, which would contradict the sentence's own tense.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 5 · よく使う表現①

items.q: （a.申し訳ありませんが b.差し支えなければ）その商品は弊社では取り扱っておりません。
items.qr: (a. Moushiwake arimasen ga b. Sashitsukae nakereba) sono shouhin wa heisha de wa toriatsukatte orimasen.
items.en: I'm sorry, but our company does not carry that product.
items.hi: माफ़ कीजिए, हमारी कंपनी वह उत्पाद नहीं रखती।
items.gu: માફ કરશો, અમારી કંપની તે ઉત્પાદન રાખતી નથી.

opts.en: if it's no trouble (wrong context — for asking a favor, not delivering a refusal)

items.why: 申し訳ありませんが is the standard apology opener for delivering unwelcome news, like declining to carry a product; 差し支えなければ is used when politely asking something OF the listener, the opposite direction here.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 5 · よく使う表現①

items.q: （ ）あのドレスがほしいです。
items.qr: (___) ano doresu ga hoshii desu.
items.en: I want that dress more than anything in the world.
items.hi: वह ड्रेस इतनी बुरी तरह चाहिए कि जैसे गले से हाथ निकल आए।
items.gu: તે ડ્રેસ એટલી બધી જોઈએ છે કે જાણે ગળામાંથી હાથ બહાર આવી જાય.

opts.en: as unrealistic as grasping a cloud (wrong simile)
heartbroken enough to feel gouged (wrong simile)

opts.t: 猫の手も借りたいほど
opts.r: neko no te mo karitai hodo
opts.en: busy enough to want a cat's help (wrong simile)

opts.t: のどから手が出るほど
opts.r: nodo kara te ga deru hodo

items.why: のどから手が出るほどほしい is the fixed idiom for desperately wanting something; the other similes describe unrelated feelings — an unrealistic plan, heartbreak, and extreme busyness.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 5 · よく使う表現①

items.q: （ ）申し訳ありません。
items.qr: (___) moushiwake arimasen.
items.en: I'm sorry for causing such a commotion.
items.hi: हलचल मचाने के लिए माफ़ी चाहता हूँ।
items.gu: ખળભળાટ મચાવવા બદલ માફી માંગું છું.

opts.en: a quick note of thanks (wrong meaning — a thank-you closer, not an apology opener)
not a set phrase in this position
not the correct set phrase (the real idiom is お手数をおかけして)

items.why: お騒がせして申し訳ありません is the complete, fixed apology for having caused a stir; the other options are either the wrong sentiment (a thank-you note) or not valid set phrases in this exact form.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 5 · よく使う表現①

items.q: 恩師の名前を（a.物忘れ b.度忘れ）した。
items.qr: Onshi no namae o (a. monowasure b. dowasure) shita.
items.en: I suddenly blanked on my mentor's name.
items.hi: गुरुजी का नाम अचानक भूल गया।
items.gu: ગુરુજીનું નામ અચાનક ભુલાઈ ગયું.

opts.en: general forgetfulness (wrong word — a trait, not a one-off slip)

items.why: 度忘れ describes forgetting something you actually know well, just for a moment — exactly a familiar mentor's name; 物忘れ describes a general tendency toward forgetfulness as a trait, not a specific slip.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 6 · よく使う表現②

items.q: ボーリングの投球の（a.こつ b.めど）をつかんだ。
items.qr: Booringu no toukyuu no (a. kotsu b. medo) o tsukanda.
items.en: I got the hang of how to throw a bowling ball.
items.hi: बॉलिंग की गेंद फेंकने का गुर आ गया।
items.gu: બોલિંગનો બોલ ફેંકવાની આવડત આવડી ગઈ.

opts.en: a prospect/estimate (wrong word — about timing, not mastering a skill)

items.why: こつをつかむ is the fixed idiom for "getting the hang of" a physical skill; めど describes having a sense of when or how something will be completed, unrelated to mastering a technique.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 6 · よく使う表現②

items.q: 彼の話は時間的に（a.ひずみ b.つじつま）が合わない。
items.qr: Kare no hanashi wa jikanteki ni (a. hizumi b. tsujitsuma) ga awanai.
items.en: His story doesn't add up in terms of the timeline.
items.hi: उसकी बात समय के हिसाब से मेल नहीं खाती।
items.gu: તેની વાત સમયની દૃષ્ટિએ બંધબેસતી નથી.

opts.en: strain/distortion (wrong word — physical or structural, not logical)

items.why: つじつまが合わない is the fixed idiom for a story or account being internally inconsistent; ひずみ describes a physical or structural strain (from an earthquake or a bad policy), not a logical contradiction.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 6 · よく使う表現②

items.q: ビルの完成のめどがやっと（a.合った b.たった）。
items.qr: Biru no kansei no medo ga yatto (a. atta b. tatta).
items.en: A prospect for the building's completion has finally been established.
items.hi: इमारत के पूरा होने की कोई उम्मीद आख़िरकार दिखने लगी।
items.gu: ઈમારત પૂરી થવાની કોઈ શક્યતા આખરે દેખાવા લાગી.

opts.en: matched (wrong verb — めど doesn't pair with 合う)

items.why: めどが立つ is the fixed collocation for "a prospect/estimate becomes established"; めど simply doesn't combine with 合う the way つじつま does.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 6 · よく使う表現②

items.q: 彼らはとても（a.お似合い b.お見合い）のカップルですね。
items.qr: Karera wa totemo (a. oniai b. omiai) no kappuru desu ne.
items.en: They're such a well-matched couple, aren't they.
items.hi: वे बहुत जँचने वाला जोड़ा हैं, है ना।
items.gu: તેઓ ખૂબ શોભે એવું જોડું છે, ખરું ને.

opts.en: an arranged meeting (wrong word — describes a formal matchmaking meeting, not an existing couple's compatibility)

items.why: お似合い describes two people or things suiting each other visually/personality-wise, exactly a well-matched couple; お見合い refers to a formally arranged first meeting between prospective marriage partners, a different concept.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 6 · よく使う表現②

items.q: 彼はシャツのボタンを（a.互い違い b.裏返し）に止めていた。
items.qr: Kare wa shatsu no botan o (a. tagaichigai b. uragaeshi) ni tomete ita.
items.en: He had fastened his shirt buttons in the wrong order, alternating out of sync.
items.hi: उसने शर्ट के बटन उल्टे-सीधे, गड़बड़ क्रम में लगा रखे थे।
items.gu: તેણે શર્ટના બટન ઊંધા-છત્તા, ખોટા ક્રમમાં લગાવ્યા હતા.

opts.en: inside-out (wrong word — describes an entire garment flipped, not buttons misaligned)

items.why: 互い違いに describes something alternating out of its proper matching sequence, exactly buttons fastened one hole off; 裏返し means an entire item is turned inside-out, a different kind of mistake.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 6 · よく使う表現②

items.q: 初対面の彼女に（ ）してしまった。
items.qr: Shotaimen no kanojo ni (___) shite shimatta.
items.en: I fell in love at first sight with her the moment we met.
items.hi: पहली ही मुलाक़ात में उससे प्यार हो गया।
items.gu: પહેલી જ મુલાકાતમાં તેની સાથે પ્રેમ થઈ ગયો.

opts.en: the start of a romance (wrong part of speech — a noun describing an origin story, not a verb one "does")
an arranged meeting (wrong meaning — a formal matchmaking setup, not spontaneous attraction)

items.why: 一目ぼれする is the fixed verb for falling in love at first sight, exactly matching "at our first meeting"; the other options describe unrelated concepts — how a relationship is later described, a formal matchmaking meeting, and willpower.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 6 · よく使う表現②

items.q: 時間を（ ）して待ち合わせに遅れてしまった。
items.qr: Jikan o (___) shite machiawase ni okurete shimatta.
items.en: I mixed up the time and ended up late for our meeting.
items.hi: समय को लेकर ग़लतफ़हमी हो गई और मीटिंग के लिए देर हो गई।
items.gu: સમય બાબતે ગેરસમજ થઈ અને મુલાકાત માટે મોડું થઈ ગયું.

opts.en: a discrepancy (wrong word — between two accounts, not one person's own error)
crossed paths (wrong word — two people missing each other, not a personal mix-up)
not a standard noun in this form

items.why: 勘違いする is the fixed verb for mistakenly believing something incorrect, like the wrong meeting time; 食い違う and 行き違う describe two separate accounts or people failing to match up with each other, not a single person's own misunderstanding.
items.unit: Week 8 Day 6 · よく使う表現②

items.q: 子犬のしつけには（ ）います。
items.qr: Koinu no shitsuke ni wa (___) imasu.
items.en: I'm having a hard time training the puppy.
items.hi: पिल्ले को सिखाने में काफ़ी परेशानी हो रही है।
items.gu: ગલૂડિયાને તાલીમ આપવામાં ખૂબ મુશ્કેલી પડી રહી છે.

opts.en: struggling with, at one's wit's end

items.why: Why (official): 手を焼いている(＝困っている) — training a puppy is exactly the kind of ongoing struggle 手を焼く describes.

items.q: 彼の才能には社長も（ ）置いています。
items.qr: Kare no sainou ni wa shachou mo (___) oite imasu.
items.en: Even the company president acknowledges his talent with respect.
items.hi: उसकी प्रतिभा को कंपनी के अध्यक्ष भी सम्मान से स्वीकारते हैं।
items.gu: તેની પ્રતિભાને કંપનીના પ્રમુખ પણ આદરથી સ્વીકારે છે.

opts.en: a glance (in 一目置く, "hold in high regard")
at a glance (wrong word — pairs with 価値がある, not 置く)

items.why: Why (official): 一目置く(＝相手が優れているところを認め、敬意を払う) — to acknowledge someone's superior ability and show respect for it.

items.q: 火事で家が焼け、彼は財産も（ ）失ってしまった。
items.qr: Kaji de ie ga yake, kare wa zaisan mo (___) ushinatte shimatta.
items.en: The house burned down in the fire, and he ended up losing absolutely everything, fortune included.
items.hi: आग से घर जल गया, और वह अपनी संपत्ति सहित बिल्कुल सब कुछ खो बैठा।
items.gu: આગથી ઘર બળી ગયું, અને તે પોતાની મિલકત સહિત બિલકુલ બધું જ ગુમાવી બેઠો.

opts.en: indiscriminately, whatever it is (wrong meaning here)
(identical to option 1 — printed this way in the source book, reproduced faithfully)

items.why: Why (official): 何もかも(＝すべて)失う — "to lose absolutely everything," matching a total, exhaustive loss. Note: options 1 and 4 are printed identically in the original book — an apparent errata, not a transcription error on this site.

items.q: 秋の夜、老いた母は虫の声を（ ）聞いていた。
items.qr: Aki no yoru, oita haha wa mushi no koe o (___) kiite ita.
items.en: On an autumn night, the aged mother was listening intently to the sound of the insects.
items.hi: शरद ऋतु की रात में, बूढ़ी माँ कीड़ों की आवाज़ ध्यान से कान लगाकर सुन रही थी।
items.gu: પાનખરની રાત્રે, વૃદ્ધ મા જીવડાંનો અવાજ ધ્યાનથી કાન માંડીને સાંભળી રહી હતી.
items.why: Why (official): 耳をすまして(＝聞こうと集中して)聞く — to listen with one's full, concentrated attention, exactly straining to hear faint insect sounds at night.

items.q: 彼女と待ち合わせしたが、どうも（ ）になったようで、結局会うことができなかった。
items.qr: Kanojo to machiawase shita ga, doumo (___) ni natta you de, kekkyoku au koto ga dekinakatta.
items.en: I had arranged to meet her, but we somehow seem to have crossed paths without meeting, so in the end I couldn't see her.
items.hi: उससे मिलने का समय तय था, पर लगता है हम एक-दूसरे को चूक गए, आख़िरकार मुलाक़ात नहीं हो पाई।
items.gu: તેની સાથે મળવાનું નક્કી હતું, પણ લાગે છે અમે એકબીજાને ચૂકી ગયા, છેવટે મુલાકાત ન થઈ.
items.why: Why (official): 行き違い(＝すれ違いになる) — two people who each went to meet the other but missed each other.

items.q: 朝の魚市場は（ ）忙しい。
items.qr: Asa no uoichiba wa (___) isogashii.
items.en: The morning fish market is so busy they'd take help from anyone, even a cat.
items.hi: सुबह की मछली मंडी इतनी व्यस्त होती है कि बिल्ली का पंजा भी उधार माँग लें।
items.gu: સવારનું માછલી બજાર એટલું વ્યસ્ત હોય છે કે બિલાડીનો પંજો પણ ઉછીનો માંગી લે.

opts.r: kao kara hi ga deru hodo
opts.en: embarrassed enough for fire to shoot from one's face (wrong simile)

opts.t: のどから手が出るほど
opts.r: nodo kara te ga deru hodo

opts.t: 猫の手も借りたいほど
opts.r: neko no te mo karitai hodo

opts.t: 胸をえぐられるように

items.why: 猫の手も借りたいほど is the fixed simile for being so busy one would accept help from anyone, however unlikely — the classic image for a bustling early-morning market.

items.q: この電球は高いけれど、（ ）、結局は節約になる。
items.qr: Kono denkyuu wa takai keredo, (___), kekkyoku wa setsuyaku ni naru.
items.en: This lightbulb is expensive, but taking the long view, it ends up saving money.
items.hi: यह बल्ब महँगा है, पर लंबे समय की सोच से देखें तो, आख़िरकार यह बचत ही है।
items.gu: આ બલ્બ મોંઘો છે, પણ લાંબા ગાળાની દૃષ્ટિએ જોઈએ તો, છેવટે તે બચત જ છે.
items.why: Why (official): 長い目で見る(＝今のことだけ考えず、長期的に考える) — to think long-term rather than fixating on the present cost.

items.q: お風呂場のリフォームをするため、業者に（ ）をしてもらった。
items.qr: Ofuroba no rifoomu o suru tame, gyousha ni (___) o shite moratta.
items.en: To renovate the bathroom, I had a contractor give me a cost estimate.
items.hi: बाथरूम की मरम्मत के लिए, ठेकेदार से लागत का अनुमान लगवाया।
items.gu: બાથરૂમના સમારકામ માટે, કોન્ટ્રાક્ટર પાસેથી ખર્ચનો અંદાજ કઢાવ્યો.
items.why: 見積もり is the standard noun for a contractor's cost estimate/quote before work begins, exactly what's needed before a bathroom renovation.

items.q: 前はおいしいと思ったのにそう思えないのは、（ ）しまったのかもしれない。
items.qr: Mae wa oishii to omotta noni sou omoenai no wa, (___) shimatta no kamoshirenai.
items.en: The reason it doesn't taste as good as it used to might be that my palate has become more refined.
items.hi: पहले जो स्वादिष्ट लगता था अब वैसा नहीं लगता, शायद इसलिए क्योंकि मेरी ज़ुबान अब पारखी हो गई है।
items.gu: પહેલાં જે સ્વાદિષ્ટ લાગતું હતું તે હવે તેવું નથી લાગતું, કદાચ મારી જીભ હવે વધુ ચોખલિયું થઈ ગઈ છે.

opts.en: not a natural verb form here

items.why: Why (official): 口が肥えて(＝おいしいものを食べ慣れて、「おいしい」と思うレベルが上がっている) — having grown used to good food, one's standard for "delicious" has risen.

items.q: 電気のコードが（ ）いると、熱を持つから危ないですよ。
items.qr: Denki no koodo ga (___) iru to, netsu o motsu kara abunai desu yo.
items.en: If the electrical cord is twisted, it can build up heat, so that's dangerous.
items.hi: अगर बिजली का तार मुड़-तुड़कर उलझा हुआ हो, तो गर्मी पैदा होकर ख़तरा हो सकता है।
items.gu: જો ઈલેક્ટ્રિક કોર્ડ વળ ખાઈને ગૂંચવાયેલો હોય, તો ગરમી પેદા થઈને જોખમ થઈ શકે.

opts.en: crooked (wrong verb — for a fixed shape like a tie)
coming apart at the seam (wrong verb — for stitching)

items.why: ねじれる describes a long, flexible object twisting along its own axis, exactly a tangled cord — and a twisted cord really can build up dangerous heat.

items.q: 賢い。 ("Clever.")
items.qr: Kashikoi.
items.why: 頭が切れる is the fixed idiom for being sharp-witted/clever, matching 賢い directly.

items.q: 付き合いをやめる。 ("To stop an association/relationship.")
items.qr: Tsukiai o yameru.
items.why: 手を切る is the fixed idiom for severing ties with a person or group, exactly "stopping an association."

items.q: すっかり取り除く。 ("To remove completely.")
items.qr: Sukkari torinozoku.

opts.en: completely renew (wrong meaning — refreshes, doesn't remove)

items.why: 一掃する is the fixed verb for eliminating/sweeping something away entirely, matching "removing completely."

items.q: 物事の前後関係や話のつながりかた。 ("The sequence of events or how a story's parts connect together.")
items.qr: Monogoto no zengo kankei ya hanashi no tsunagarikata.
items.why: つじつま describes exactly how the parts of a story or account logically connect and stay consistent with each other.

items.q: 自慢する。 ("To boast.")
items.qr: Jiman suru.

opts.en: grating/annoying (wrong meaning — about how others react, not the act of boasting)
not a fixed idiom in this sense

items.why: 鼻にかける is the fixed idiom for boasting/being smug about something, matching 自慢する directly.

items.q: 痛み止めの注射をしたので、すぐに痛みは和らいでくるでしょう。
items.qr: Itamidome no chuusha o shita node, sugu ni itami wa yawaraide kuru deshou.
items.en: Since I had a painkiller injection, the pain will probably ease up soon.
items.why: じきに means "soon" (time), the exact match for すぐに here; じかに is the sound-alike trap meaning "directly" (manner), a different word entirely.

items.q: 彼は仕事に熱中した生活をしている。
items.qr: Kare wa shigoto ni netchuu shita seikatsu o shite iru.
items.en: He lives a life devoted single-mindedly to his work.

opts.en: not the fixed collocation (一心 pairs with 同体/に祈る, not 仕事の)

items.why: 一筋 is the fixed word for single-minded devotion to one thing, exactly matching a life devoted entirely to work.

items.q: これは私にはできない問題だ。
items.u: 私にはできない / watashi ni wa dekinai
items.qr: Kore wa watashi ni wa dekinai mondai da.
items.en: This is a problem beyond what I can handle.

opts.en: not a fixed idiom (足が出る means "over budget")

items.why: 手に負えない is the fixed idiom for something exceeding one's own ability to manage, exactly "a problem I can't handle."

items.q: 彼女のことはすべて知っているつもりだ。
items.qr: Kanojo no koto wa subete shitte iru tsumori da.
items.en: I think I know everything about her.

opts.en: from best to worst (wrong meaning — a range of quality, not totality of knowledge)
from one to ten, i.e. every last detail

items.why: 一から十まで is the fixed idiom for "absolutely everything, down to the last detail," the natural match for すべて here.

items.q: このおもちゃは一時期とてもよくはやったね。
items.qr: Kono omocha wa ichijiki totemo yoku hayatta ne.
items.en: This toy was really popular for a while, wasn't it.

opts.en: an instant (wrong meaning — too brief for a toy's fad period)

items.why: 一頃 is the fixed word for "at one time in the past, for a stretch," matching a toy fad's period of popularity — 一瞬 would describe something lasting only a literal instant.

items.q: あべこべ
items.qr: abekobe

opts.t: 収入と支出のあべこべが合わない。
opts.r: Shuunyuu to shishutsu no abekobe ga awanai.
opts.en: "The income-and-expense's あべこべ doesn't match" — wrong noun; this needs つじつまが合わない, a story/figures being consistent

opts.t: トラックが多く通る道路はあべこべしている。
opts.r: Torakku ga ooku tooru douro wa abekobe shite iru.
opts.en: "A road with lots of trucks is あべこべ" — wrong word; a bumpy road needs でこぼこしている, not あべこべ

opts.t: 工事で車線が狭く、車はあべこべに通行した。
opts.r: Kouji de sharen ga semaku, kuruma wa abekobe ni tsuukou shita.
opts.en: "Lanes narrowed by construction, cars passed あべこべに" — wrong word; alternating one at a time needs 互い違い／交互に, not あべこべ

opts.t: ぬいぐるみの頭とシッポをあべこべにつけてしまった。
opts.r: Nuigurumi no atama to shippo o abekobe ni tsukete shimatta.
opts.en: I ended up attaching the stuffed animal's head and tail the wrong way round.

items.why: Why (official): 「あべこべ」は順序や位置が逆さまに入れ替わっている様子を表す — あべこべ describes two things swapped into each other's correct position (head and tail reversed); options 1, 2, and 3 each need a different word (つじつま, でこぼこ, 互い違い／交互).

items.q: 度忘れ
items.qr: dowasure

opts.t: 今まで覚えていたのに、度忘れしてしまった。
opts.r: Ima made oboete ita noni, dowasure shite shimatta.
opts.en: Even though I'd known it until now, it suddenly slipped my mind.

opts.t: 今日の気温を度忘れしないように気をつけよう。
opts.r: Kyou no kion o dowasure shinai you ni ki o tsukeyou.
opts.en: "Let's be careful not to 度忘れ today's temperature" — odd; you can't "momentarily blank" on something you never memorized in the first place

opts.t: 今日は雨なので電車の中に傘の度忘れが多い。
opts.r: Kyou wa ame na node densha no naka ni kasa no dowasure ga ooi.
opts.en: "Since it's raining, there are many umbrella 度忘れ on trains" — wrong noun; a left-behind item needs 忘れ物, not 度忘れ

opts.t: 緊張して度忘れしたことが思い出せない。
opts.r: Kinchou shite dowasure shita koto ga omoidasenai.
opts.en: "Nervous, I can't recall the thing I 度忘れした" — redundant/circular; 度忘れ already IS the state of being unable to recall

items.why: Why (official): 「度忘れ」は知っているはずのことを、その場で忘れて思い出せないこと — 度忘れ describes momentarily forgetting something you actually do know, exactly option 1; option 3's left umbrellas need 傘の忘れ物, a different concept.

items.q: 気が散る
items.qr: ki ga chiru

opts.t: 面接で予想していないことを聞かれて気が散った。
opts.r: Mensetsu de yosou shite inai koto o kikarete ki ga chitta.
opts.en: "Asked something unexpected in the interview, I 気が散った" — odd; a sudden surprise needs 動揺した/慌てた, not the ongoing-distraction sense of 気が散る

opts.t: 気が散るからテレビを消して。
opts.r: Ki ga chiru kara terebi o keshite.
opts.en: It's distracting, so turn off the TV.

opts.t: 5人も人を殺したという犯人は、気が散っているね。
opts.r: Gonin mo hito o koroshita to iu hannin wa, ki ga chitte iru ne.
opts.en: "A criminal who killed 5 people is 気が散っている" — wrong word; describing someone as deranged needs 気が狂っている, not 気が散る

opts.t: こんなに作ったのにまだ予定の半分にも満たないとは、とても気が散る。
opts.r: Konna ni tsukutta noni mada yotei no hanbun ni mo mitanai to wa, totemo ki ga chiru.
opts.en: "Made this much and still under half the target — very 気が散る" — wrong word; that frustration needs 気が滅入る/がっかりする, not 気が散る

items.why: Why (official): 「気が散る」は一つのことに気持ちを集中できないという意味 — 気が散る means being unable to concentrate on one thing, exactly why background noise like a TV is distracting; options 1, 3, and 4 each need a different emotional word entirely.

items.q: 足が出る
items.qr: ashi ga deru

opts.t: 今月は足が出るほどの買い物をしなければならない。
opts.r: Kongetsu wa ashi ga deru hodo no kaimono o shinakereba naranai.
opts.en: "This month I must shop enough for 足が出る" — awkward phrasing; 足が出る describes a resulting state (over budget), not a purpose/degree clause like this

opts.t: いたずらな末っ子には本当に足が出る。
opts.r: Itazura na suekko ni wa hontou ni ashi ga deru.
opts.en: "With the mischievous youngest child, 足が出る" — wrong idiom; struggling with a mischievous kid needs 手を焼く, not 足が出る

opts.t: 彼女はインテリアの世界ではかなり足が出た存在です。
opts.r: Kanojo wa interia no sekai de wa kanari ashi ga deta sonzai desu.
opts.en: "In the interior design world, she is a 足が出た presence" — wrong idiom; standing out needs 名の知れた／際立った, not 足が出る

opts.t: 海外旅行でお土産を買いすぎて、予算から足が出てしまった。
opts.r: Kaigai ryokou de omiyage o kaisugite, yosan kara ashi ga dete shimatta.
opts.en: I bought too many souvenirs on the overseas trip and ended up going over budget.

items.why: Why (official): 「足が出る」は出費が多く、予算が足りなくなるという意味 — 足が出る means spending too much and running over one's budget, exactly buying too many souvenirs; option 2's mischievous child instead needs 手を焼く.

items.q: いかにも
items.qr: ikanimo

opts.t: 彼女はいかにも自分が能力があるかを必死でアピールした。
opts.r: Kanojo wa ikanimo jibun ga nouryoku ga aru ka o hisshi de apiiru shita.
opts.en: "She desperately appealed いかにも whether she was capable" — wrong word; a question like "whether/how much ability" needs いかに, not いかにも

opts.t: このドレッシングはいかにもおいしく食べられます。
opts.r: Kono doresshingu wa ikanimo oishiku taberaremasu.
opts.en: "This dressing can いかにも be eaten deliciously" — odd collocation; いかにも intensifies a description/impression, not a potential-form verb phrase like this

opts.t: そのラーメン屋の看板にはいかにもおいしそうなラーメンの絵が描かれている。
opts.r: Sono raamen-ya no kanban ni wa ikanimo oishisou na raamen no e ga kakarete iru.
opts.en: That ramen shop's sign has a picture of ramen that looks every bit as delicious as can be.

opts.t: 空がいかにも晴れてきた。
opts.en: "The sky いかにも cleared up" — odd; a simple factual change like weather clearing doesn't take いかにも's "every bit the stereotype of" nuance

items.why: Why (official): Option 1 should use いかに (＝いかに能力があるかを, "however much ability she had") — いかにも only intensifies a description that already carries a comparison/impression, like ～そうな ("looking like ~"), exactly option 3's "looking every bit as delicious."
